$comment: READ THIS BEFORE YOU CHANGE A `value`. This file is read at RUNTIME by all four
repos: the compiled engine carries a copy, and it REFUSES TO CONSTRUCT when the two
disagree. So a value edit and `maturin develop --release` are ONE STEP. Between them,
every other session's engine is down -- not slow, down, with `RustEngine()` raising.
That happened twice in twenty minutes on 2026-09-22, and the second time was twenty
minutes after the rule was written into a log, which is why it is written here instead:
nobody reads history before editing a file. `tests/test_ledger_build_step.py` fails the
moment the two disagree, so run the suite and you will trip over it before anyone else
does. Adding a KEY counts: an engine built without it refuses just as loudly.
THE CALIBRATION REGISTRY. Every physics constant in the engine lives here, and
every one of them carries how well it is known. Nothing in the Rust core or the
Python layer may hardcode a number that appears in this file.
WHY: this project's predecessor stalled for weeks trying to make pathfinding
match the real game. The cause was not difficulty -- it was that plausible
numbers and measured numbers were stored the same way, so a wrong guess was
indistinguishable from a fact and later tuning absorbed the error instead of
revealing it. A constant fitted to the one case anybody checked makes a wrong
LAW read as right, on every board at once.
STATUS VALUES, in increasing order of trust:
guess        nobody has evidence; a placeholder so the engine runs
disputed_existence  the key names something no shipped data or recording shows
exists; ranked with guess, because nobody has evidence either way
hypothesis   an argument from data shape, not an observation
community    multiple independent third parties agree, no primary source
third_party_measured  one outside measurement, its source, method and sample named,
not reproduced by this project's own instruments. Ranked WITH community
and never overwrite-protected, so this project's own measurement replaces
it without --supersede. Added 2026-09-24: two outside readings had been
filed as measured, which protected them against the very correction
that should replace them.
datamined    taken from shipped game data (state the file and the vintage)
measured     observed in the real game in this project's own recorded traces
owner_ruling a first-hand observation of the live game by a maintainer,
quoted verbatim and dated. Ranked WITH measured, never below it:
a direct observation of the live 2026 game, which is the target,
is a primary source. Added 2026-09-17, because
filing the Log ruling as 'community' would have made it
indistinguishable from the fandom prose it overturned -- exactly
the confusion this registry exists to prevent. Like measured, it
cannot be overwritten with a different value without --supersede.
A ruling may settle only PART of a key (the Log's sign, not its
off-axis vector); say which part in confidence, and keep a
promotion_rule for the rest.
PROMOTION RULE: a constant may only be promoted by adding evidence, never by
an engine result looking right. If the sim matches reality with a 'guess' in
it, that is a coincidence until measured, and saying so costs nothing.

meta.target_note: The LIVE 2026 game was chosen over a frozen 2023 build. Consequence: every datamined constant below is from 2016-2018 or 2023 game data and is therefore EVIDENCE, NOT SPEC. Supercell rewrote ground pathfinding on 2025-03-31; anything tagged pre-2025 about movement is archaeology until re-measured.

SUBTILE_PER_TILE.provenance: Design choice, following cr-sim. NOT a game constant.
rationale: This number is chosen so that it cannot bake in the answer to the two
biggest open questions (tick rate, speed divisor). Under EVERY candidate
hypothesis, a unit's per-tick displacement is an exact integer:
Speed is tiles/min, 20 TPS -> Speed * 15 subtiles/tick
Speed is tiles/min, 30 TPS -> Speed * 10 subtiles/tick
Speed is tiles/min, 60 TPS -> Speed *  5 subtiles/tick
18000 = 1000 * 18, so one millitile (the unit ALL shipped distances use)
is exactly 18 subtiles and no game data value ever needs rounding.
Consequence: we can run at 20 TPS and re-run at 60 TPS and any divergence
is a real signal rather than a rounding artefact.
SUBTILE_PER_TILE.promotion_rules: Not promotable -- it is ours, not Supercell's. Revisit only if a measured per-tick displacement is not an integer multiple of 1/18000 tile.

MILLITILE_PER_TILE.provenance: All distance columns in characters.csv/buildings.csv are millitiles. Cross-checked against community tile values across dozens of cards: Knight SightRange 5500 = 5.5 tiles, CollisionRadius 500 = 0.5, Mini P.E.K.K.A 450 = 0.45, Mortar/X-Bow Range 11500 = 11.5.
MILLITILE_PER_TILE.promotion_rules: Already as good as it gets from data and traces.

POSITION_TYPE.provenance: Community projects report entity positions as raw i32. The internal SCALE is unknown; we choose our own (above) and do not claim it matches.
POSITION_TYPE.note: Arena max is 32 tiles * 18000 = 576000, far inside i32. Squared distances reach 3.3e11 and MUST use i64 -- an i32 squared-distance is a silent overflow bug.
POSITION_TYPE.promotion_rules: Not observable in a trace; out of scope.

TICK_MS.provenance: MEASURED. OFFLINE TRACE CORPUS (Clash Royale 15.535.29 / versionCode 150535029). Traces: data/oracle-native/{walk (6 cards x 1 deploy), lane_sweep_Knight (128 files / 64 distinct experiments), building_Giant (12), repath_Giant (2), meet (3), orient (1)} -- 150 units, 51926 entity-ticks. Analysis: passes over the offline traces -- grid, cost model, occlusion and goal rule; every law re-measured over every unit of every trace; timing and the speed law. Report: docs/movement-measurements.md; implementation contract: docs/pathfinder-spec.md. The free per-unit speed fit (no card table, S in 1..5000, synth_adjudicate B2) has exactly one survivor per card and every unit of a card fits the same integer, which only happens when one trace frame is one logic tick; at 2-5 sub-steps per tick no integer speed survives at all. The stomp pause schedule ((k+1)*TICK_MS) mod (Stop+Wait) > Stop reproduces Giant 308/308 and Golem 306/306 moving ticks with TICK_MS = 50 and no phase offset.

disagreement.30_TPS_33ms: the old engine in legacy/ used dt=0.033 (and not even exactly 1/30).

TICK_MS.why_it_matters: Every interaction is a function of this: body-block timing, whether a Fireball lands before a unit crosses, how many tower hits a Hog gets. A 3x error here is absorbed into fitted card constants and never shows up as itself.
TICK_MS.promotion_rules: SETTLED by the 15.535.29 measurements. Re-open only against a second independent trace capture, never against an argument from data shape.
TICK_MS.engine_contract: Read from here. Never write `50` in engine code.

history.provenance: No primary source exists. This is the single most load-bearing unknown in the engine.
history.overturned_by: the 15.535.29 traces advance the battle by one logic tick per 50 ms of shipped DeployTime/HitSpeed: every measured per-tick speed is an integer number of millitiles and the stomp phase (Giant 308/308, Golem 306/306) only closes at TICK_MS = 50.

struck.60_TPS_16.67ms: STRUCK. Its arithmetic is wrong: PhoenixNoRespawn DeployTime 733 ms is 733/16.667 = 43.98 ticks at 60 Hz, not 44 -- the argument needs 733.33. Lightning HitSpeed = 460 is a whole number of ticks at none of 50, 33.3 or 16.67 ms, so 'shipped durations are whole ticks' is void in either direction. Overturned by the 15.535.29 measurement above in any case.

SPEED_TO_SUBTILES_PER_TICK.units: multiplier applied to the Speed column
SPEED_TO_SUBTILES_PER_TICK.provenance: MEASURED. OFFLINE TRACE CORPUS (Clash Royale 15.535.29 / versionCode 150535029). Traces: data/oracle-native/{walk (6 cards x 1 deploy), lane_sweep_Knight (128 files / 64 distinct experiments), building_Giant (12), repath_Giant (2), meet (3), orient (1)} -- 150 units, 51926 entity-ticks. Analysis: passes over the offline traces -- grid, cost model, occlusion and goal rule; every law re-measured over every unit of every trace; timing and the speed law. Report: docs/movement-measurements.md; implementation contract: docs/pathfinder-spec.md. Free integer per-unit fit over every moving tick of every unit (synth_adjudicate B2, no card table, S in 1..5000): exactly one survivor per card and every unit of a card fits it -- Knight 60 (131 units), Giant 52 (12), Golem 54, Skeletons 90 (3), MiniPekka 90, HogRider 120. Those are the raw Speed column values themselves (Giant 45 and Golem 45 after the StopMovementAfterMS/WaitMS rule, movement.STOMP_SPEED_RULE), i.e. Speed is millitiles per tick exactly. 1 millitile = 18 subtiles, so subtiles_per_tick = Speed * 18.
SPEED_TO_SUBTILES_PER_TICK.why_it_matters: A flat 20% error on the movement speed of every unit in the game.
SPEED_TO_SUBTILES_PER_TICK.promotion_rules: SETTLED. The former value is in `history` and the two former hypotheses are in `struck` with their original arguments, the same way time.TICK_MS archives its refuted entry -- a promotion adds evidence, it never deletes it. A buffed speed (SpeedMultiplier) follows the SAME law with a larger integer S: data/oracle-native/rage/Knight_rage_seed2.jsonl.gz fits S = 60 on t121..155, S = 78 on t156..217 (the Rage) and S = 60 again on t218..340, and 78 = 60 x 1.3 exactly. Its ROUNDING is still unmeasured, because 60 x 1.3 is a whole number and floor/round/truncate/ceil all give 78 -- see movement.STOMP_SPEED_RULE.
SPEED_TO_SUBTILES_PER_TICK.engine_contract: subtiles_per_tick = Speed * SPEED_TO_SUBTILES_PER_TICK. Set to 10 for 30 TPS, 5 for 60 TPS, 18 for the millitile-per-tick reading.

history.provenance: Derived: assumes Speed is tiles/minute AND TICK_MS=50. Speed 60 (Medium) -> 1.0 tiles/s.
history.overturned_by: the 15.535.29 measurements: Speed is millitiles per 50 ms tick (divide_by_50), so one Speed unit is 18 subtiles per tick, not 15.

SPEED_TO_SUBTILES_PER_TICK.resolves: divide_by_50 vs divide_by_60: divide_by_50 is correct. Medium (Speed 60) is 1.20 tiles/s, not 1.00.

struck.divide_by_60: STRUCK 2026-09-18 by the 15.535.29 measurements. Its argument was: 'Speed is tiles/minute. Medium (60) = 1.00 tiles/s. Supported by cr-sim's exact-at-60TPS derivation and by the highest-sample community VOD medians (skeletons 1.56 at Speed 90, hog 1.45 at Speed 120).' Overturned because the free per-unit integer fit's survivors ARE the raw Speed column (Knight 60, Giant 52, Golem 54, Skeletons 90, MiniPekka 90, HogRider 120) at TICK_MS = 50, i.e. one Speed unit is one millitile per 50 ms tick; at 60 TPS the same fit has no integer survivor.
struck.divide_by_50: UPHELD 2026-09-18, and now measured rather than argued. Its argument was: 'Speed is millitiles per 50ms tick. Medium (60) = 1.20 tiles/s. Architecturally cleaner. Matches lower-sample VOD medians (musketeer 1.20, knight 1.12 at Speed 60).' Kept here because the entry it lived in was deleted on promotion; the evidence that settled it is in `provenance`.

PROJECTILE_SPEED_TO_SUBTILES_PER_TICK.provenance: MEASURED on the live 16.402 effects stream (every projectile object on every frame of the captures): the princess tower's arrow (TowerPrincessProjectile Speed 600) advances 599-600 native per tick on 293 consecutive steps of capture 20260920-003751-B and 688 of 20260920-081819-B, the king tower's (Speed 1000) 999-1000, the Musketeer's (Speed 1000) 1000, the Bomber's (Speed 400) 399-400, the Cannon's (Speed 500) 499-500 -- one projectile Speed unit is one native millitile per 50 ms tick, the troop unit (18 subtiles), not 15. History: hypothesis 15 (2026-09-13) mirrored a 'tiles/min at 20 TPS' reading; the AesDragon wiki blog's assertion and the Darknighture frame test (x1.2 for both a Musketeer projectile and a Giant) were right.

history.provenance: Mirrors time.SPEED_TO_SUBTILES_PER_TICK (Speed = tiles/min at 20 TPS). Community: the AesDragon wiki blog ASSERTS (unmeasured) that projectile Speed uses the troop unit; a Darknighture frame test (2023) measured x1.2 (Speed/50) for BOTH a Musketeer projectile and a Giant. No source was found for a 'troops /50, projectiles /60' split. crforge and legacy/ use /60 for both. Kept as its own key so a recording can split projectiles from troops without a code change (docs/spell-spec.md, projectile and rolling families).
history.overturned_by: the live effects stream: 600 native per tick for Speed 600 on 981 arrow steps (2026-09-21)

PROJECTILE_SPEED_TO_SUBTILES_PER_TICK.units: subtiles per tick per raw projectile Speed unit
PROJECTILE_SPEED_TO_SUBTILES_PER_TICK.applies_to: EVERY projectile: troop and tower projectiles (combat.rs fire) and spell projectiles (spell.rs), including The Log's airborne and rolling phases
PROJECTILE_SPEED_TO_SUBTILES_PER_TICK.promotion_rules: Time a Goblin Barrel from release to landing, Blue king centre to enemy princess centre (23.16 tiles: 3.474 s at 15, 2.895 s at 18), or a live Log roll from first contact to despawn (3.03 s vs 2.525 s). Split from the troop key only if the projectile measurement disagrees with the troop measurement beyond frame error.
PROJECTILE_SPEED_TO_SUBTILES_PER_TICK.engine: read by crates/royalesim (state.rs Calib::from_json); a candidate without an engine implementation is refused at load, never silently substituted

arena.$comment: NOT stored here. Derived from the shipped tilemap by tools/extract_arena.py into data/derived/arena.json, and gated there. Hardcoding arena geometry is what made the old engine wrong about the river, the bridges and the king footprint all at once.

ARENA_SOURCE_VINTAGE.caveat: The modern client no longer ships a Map section -- the battlefield moved out of data and into code. The 2016-era per-arena data sets show TWO geometries (2-tile bridges in most arenas, 3-tile in Legendary/Royal), so bridge width is arena-dependent and possibly changed since. An 0.5-tile error in bridge span is about one Knight hitbox and decides every bridge body-block.
ARENA_SOURCE_VINTAGE.promotion_rules: Re-measure against a screenshot of the live arena with a calibrated tile overlay.

TERRITORY_MODEL.provenance: data/raw/retroroyale-2018/csv_logic/buildings.csv NoDeploySizeW / NoDeploySizeH, ~2018 client data (PRE-2025; evidence, not spec). The columns are set on exactly three rows: KingTower (18, 16), PrincessTower (11, 21) and NOTINUSE21, a disused copy of the king (18, 16). Carried into data/derived/cards.json towers[].no_deploy_size_tiles by tools/extract_cards.py.
TERRITORY_MODEL.rule: A TROOP may not be placed at a point inside the closed axis-aligned rectangle, centred on the tower centre with half-extents NoDeploySizeW/2 and NoDeploySizeH/2 tiles, of any ALIVE ENEMY crown tower; plus the tilemap WATER and NO_DEPLOY bits, arena bounds, building footprints, and the river band (never troop territory, see open_question). Buildings stay own half only (unsourced, unchanged). Spells anywhere.
TERRITORY_MODEL.unit_inference: TILES, inferred from 4 of 4 landmarks that come out exact under that reading and 0 of 4 under the half-tile reading, against the independently derived data/derived/arena.json and the princess tower centre (3.5, 6.5): (1) the king rect spans x = [0, 18], exactly the arena width; (2) the left and right princess rects (x = 3.5 +- 5.5 and 14.5 +- 5.5) meet exactly at x = 9, the centre line; (3) and (4) each princess rect's far edge (y = 6.5 + 10.5 = 17) is exactly the far river bank. tools/check_data.py gates all four.
TERRITORY_MODEL.consequence: With every enemy tower up, the rects forbid everything from the near river bank onward. When one enemy princess falls, the ground that opens on that side is between the far river bank (y = 17) and the enemy king rect (y = 21): 8 half-rows (4 tiles), x from the side wall to the centre line.
TERRITORY_MODEL.open_question: The four dry bridge half-columns (rows 15-17) are marked neither WATER nor NO_DEPLOY in the tilemap, so the rects alone would open them once that lane's princess falls. The engine keeps the river band closed to troops, carried from the previous rule WITHOUT a source. A recording of a troop placement attempt on the bridge after a princess tower falls settles it.

history.provenance: NONE. A pocket-depth constant in crates/royalesim/src/arena.rs: after a princess tower fell, troop territory reached 12 half-rows (6 tiles) past the far river bank on that engine-column side. Not in globals.csv, locations.csv, arenas.csv, game_modes.csv or the tilemap; chosen only to equal protocol.py MOCK_POCKET_DEPTH_HALF_ROWS. Before it, the engine used the far bank up to the destroyed tower's centre row (8.5 tiles), equally unsourced.
history.overturned_by: buildings.csv NoDeploySizeW/H on the crown towers, read as tiles: 4 of 4 arena landmarks exact (see unit_inference). The shipped mechanic replaces the depth; the depth was not tuned to 8.

TERRITORY_MODEL.promotion_rules: Record the DEEPEST legal troop placement on one lane after that lane's enemy princess tower falls (drag a troop card forward until the placement indicator refuses). This model predicts the limit at the enemy king rect edge, 4 tiles past the far river bank; the old 12-half-row model predicts 6 tiles, 2 tiles deeper. Also record whether the bridge accepts a troop then (open_question).

ADD_CHARACTER_RANGE_TO_RADIUS.provenance: globals.csv, present in both 1.3.2 and modern data sets.
ADD_CHARACTER_RANGE_TO_RADIUS.meaning: Range is measured EDGE to EDGE, not centre to centre: in_range = centre_distance <= range + target.collision_radius. The old engine used centre-to-centre only, so every melee unit under-reached.
ADD_CHARACTER_RANGE_TO_RADIUS.open: Whether the ATTACKER's own collision radius is also added: SETTLED by targeting.ATTACK_RANGE_RULE -- it is (measured: the live Prince, Range 1600 and CollisionRadius 600, stops 3135 native from a princess tower's centre, CollisionRadius 1000, the first step inside 3200; under Range + the target's radius alone it would walk on to 2600).

ATTACK_RANGE_RULE.confidence: HIGH -- three independent stop distances and a tower acquisition tick of the live corpus, each one walking step wide, all inside the both-radii sum and all outside the target-radius-only sum
ATTACK_RANGE_RULE.provenance: MEASURED on the live 16.402 corpus (the reach gap of the corpus report): the Prince (Range 1600, CollisionRadius 600) of capture 20260920-003751 stops 3135 native from the princess tower's centre (CollisionRadius 1000) and the one of 20260920-002736 at 3133, never inside 3126 -- the first step inside 3200 = Range + own R + the tower's R, 600 short of the 2600 the target-radius-only sum gives; the Dark Prince (Range 1200) stops at 2776, inside 2800, not 2200; the princess tower (Range 7500, R 1000) acquires the Prince on the tick after it steps inside 9100 (t279 at 9009 -> attacking at t280), not at 8500. THE RULE (target.rs in_attack_range): a target is in range when the centre distance is <= Range + the ATTACKER's CollisionRadius + the TARGET's CollisionRadius; the sight scan sums SightRange the same way (with EXTRA_SIGHT_RANGE_TO_CROWN_TOWERS / _TO_BUILDING by the candidate's kind); MinimumRange adds the lower bound (R + minRange). The goal cell of the walk stays Range + own R to the target's CENTRE (pathfinding.PATH_SEARCH), so a unit stops walking EARLIER than its goal cell: its attack sees the target in range at Range + own R + target R.
ATTACK_RANGE_RULE.meaning: range_plus_both_radii: a target is in range when the centre distance is <= Range + the ATTACKER's CollisionRadius + the TARGET's CollisionRadius (the same sum, with SightRange, for the sight scan and the keep-target / cancel-hit extensions). range_plus_target_radius: the earlier engine -- Range + the target's radius only, so every unit walked its own radius too far (a Prince 600 native past where the game stops it) and every tower acquired a unit its radius too late.
ATTACK_RANGE_RULE.promotion_rules: Measured; re-open only against a live capture whose stop distance parts from Range + both radii by more than one walking step.
ATTACK_RANGE_RULE.engine: read by crates/royalesim (state.rs Calib::from_json -> attack_range_rule); target.rs in_attack_range takes the attacker's radius and adds it under the shipped arm (every caller: combat.rs attack_step, the Path phase's attacking test, the sight scan, keep-target, the lock hold, the wake trigger); the goal reach was already Range + own R. The old arm stays runnable as range_plus_target_radius (the regression plant reach_without_own_radius forces it). tests/reach.rs pins the stop distances from the card data.

VARIABLE_DAMAGE_WALK_REACH.confidence: LOW for the old arm range_plus_both_radii, the engine before this flip: its Inferno Dragon stops and starts to burn with the target 500 farther than the client's, on 31 of 31 corpus ticks and 16 of 16 client 15.535.29 ticks that separate the arms. HIGH that a walking Inferno Dragon's reach adds no radius of its own: 0 of 47 such ticks against it, and its goal cells stay within Range of the target (25 of 25 choices within 23). The arm is scoped to what was measured: it reads a flying row that sets VariableDamage2, which in the 15.535.29 tables is the Inferno Dragon's alone. That column is the one that separates the Inferno Dragon from every other attacker the records hold, but no other card with the column walks in any record: the Mighty Miner, a ground row that sets it, keeps its own radius under both arms, and a flying row added later with the column (the Inferno Dragon's evolution is not in these tables) would be reached by inference, not by measurement.
VARIABLE_DAMAGE_WALK_REACH.provenance: MEASURED on the 16.402 corpus (one Inferno Dragon battle, 20260920-082459, one seat: two Dragons) and on client 15.535.29 (the Inferno Dragon sweep scene), on start-of-tick positions. A tick counts when the Dragon's pointer names a unit, and it is filed by what the Dragon did on the tick before (walked or stood) and by x, the target's centre distance less Range and the target's collision radius. WALKING: on 31 corpus and 16 sweep ticks that started with 0 < x <= 500 (inside Range + both radii, outside Range + the target's radius) the Dragon walked on, and it stopped on none; it stopped 4 + 2 times, each on the first tick with x <= 0 (x of -37, -57, -52 and -10 on the corpus against a Goblin, a princess tower and a Giant twice; -69 and -41 in the sweep against a Knight). Walkers of every other card stood on 979 corpus and 235 sweep ticks of that band (and walked on 277 and 38, a target moving away or a unit pushed), so the band separates the Dragon from the rest. STANDING: on 42 + 17 ticks with the target in the same band it held its place, walking on none. Its attack gate (the tick after a hit) kept it at x = 324 and 454 against a Giant (corpus 3001 and 3009) and let it go at x = 506 against a Knight (sweep 329): Range + both radii, as for every unit. It let go of the Giant at x = 526 (corpus 3012), past the keep reach Range + both radii + LOGIC_RANGE_EXTENSION_TO_KEEP_TARGET (525). A standing Dragon took a new target at x = 294 (corpus 3017) and stood; its attack progress started on 3024, when its load timer allowed it, as the engine's cycle has it. GOAL CELLS: the Dragon's single path node lay within Range of the target's centre on every fresh choice (the largest 3,523 of 20 corpus choices and 3,509 of 5 sweep choices, 23 and 9 past Range while the target moved); every other flyer's reached Range + its radius (for example the Baby Dragon's 3,800 and 4,007, the Minions' 3,098 of 177 choices). Three corpus ticks where a walking Dragon's frame repeats the one before it after a double step are left out (a recording artefact: it moves again on the next tick). Switched on at the 2026-09-28 flip build (scored on RoyaleSim 238274a). Alone on that build (every other key at its old arm; the corpus rebuilt by that build's fixture maker): sweep +189 within 250 / +0 both alive / +99 hp exact, +1 scene at 95/95 (InfernoDragon +189/+99); corpus +55 within 250 / -1,362 both alive / +717 hp exact (20260920-082459-B +122/+354, 20260920-082459-A -67/+363). Inside the 15-key flip, the set minus the set without it: sweep +189 within 250 / +0 both alive / +99 hp exact, +1 scene at 95/95 (InfernoDragon +189/+99); corpus +3,633 within 250 / +471 both alive / +2,410 hp exact (20260920-082459-A +1841/+1225, 20260920-082459-B +1792/+1185).

VARIABLE_DAMAGE_WALK_REACH.meaning: client16402_no_own_radius_walking: a walking flyer whose row sets VariableDamage2 (the Inferno Dragon's row alone in the 15.535.29 tables) chooses its goal cell within Range of the target's centre, aims its direct walk there, and stops, with its attack starting, once the target's centre is within Range + the target's radius; a unit that holds a walking goal from the previous tick is walking. Standing, its reach is Range + both radii (targeting.ATTACK_RANGE_RULE). Every other card is unchanged, the Mighty Miner (a ground row with the column) among them. range_plus_both_radii: today's engine, every unit walks to Range + its own radius and stops at Range + both radii.

TARGET_RANK_DISTANCE.confidence: LOW for the old arm centre_minus_target_radius, the engine before this flip: a scan ranks its candidates by centre distance minus the candidate's collision radius, so a princess tower (radius 1000) or a king tower (1400) wins against a nearer troop or building, and it misses 18 of 578 walking switches of the 16.402 corpus. HIGH for client16402_centre: 577 of 578 walking switches, 3 of 9,249 non-switch ticks against it (each ending with no target because the enemy died on that tick), 21 of 21 acquisitions and 92 of 95 walking ticks where the two rankings name different enemies (the other 3 took neither), and 1 of 1 walker whose two rankings name different crown towers
TARGET_RANK_DISTANCE.provenance: MEASURED on the 16.402 corpus, one seat per battle (40 battles). A troop walking to a crown tower (its recorded target is the tower, and it is not attacking) re-decides on every tick from the start-of-tick positions: it takes the nearest enemy it may target within SightRange + both collision radii when that enemy's CENTRE distance is below the tower's CENTRE distance, and keeps walking otherwise. 577 of 578 switches fit; 537 of them had a decision on the tick before, and on none of those did the condition already hold, so there is no scan period. Of 9,249 non-switch walking ticks with an enemy within 1,500 of the sight sum, 3 fit the condition, and on each the walker ends the tick with no target because that enemy died on the tick (121158 tick 1936, 181741 tick 431, 184136 tick 359). The null of 'any enemy in sight beats the tower': 894 ticks of 57 walkers in 15 battles had a valid enemy in sight farther than the tower by centre and did not switch (20260918-124946: Goblins 32, 33 and 35 beside the Cannon that Goblin 34 took). The bounds are tight: a switch at a centre difference of -2.6 (112215 tick 494) and none at +0.4 (115249.b1 tick 1931); an enemy taken 1.0 inside the sight sum and none taken 0.3 beyond it. Today's key gives the tower its radius as a head start and misses 18 switches the rule fits, among them 20260918-124946 tick 941: a Goblin 6,578.4 from a Cannon and 6,840.8 from its princess tower (keys 5,978.4 and 5,840.8) takes the Cannon; Skeletons of the same battle take the same Cannon on 1006, 1126 and 1138 and Ice Spirits on 2247 (walking to the king tower); Skeletons take a Musketeer (112751, six; 122757.b2, two, walking to the king tower), an Archer (115249.b1), a Mini P.E.K.K.A (121158) and an Ice Wizard (010218), and two Minions an Archer (112751). The ranking among enemies: 21 of 21 acquisitions (troops, and a Goblin Cage) where centre and centre minus radius name different enemies took the centre-nearest. On 95 ticks of a troop walking after an enemy out of its reach where they disagree, it held or took the centre-nearest on 92; on the other 3 a Skeleton took a Tombstone's Skeleton, neither pick. Two Goblin Cages (20260920-072148 and 20260920-072831) held the centre-nearest of two troops on 37 ticks where the other was nearer by centre minus radius. The ranking between crown towers: on 13,645 walking ticks with two or more enemy crown towers within SightRange + 2000 + both radii and no enemy in sight, the two rankings name different towers on 10, all one Minion (20260920-083112). On tick 2587, the first tick a princess tower came within that reach, it turned from the king tower (9,118.8 by centre, 7,718.8 minus the radius) to the princess tower (8,957.0 and 7,957.0), as the centre ranking does; by centre minus radius the king stays first through tick 2597. Where the king is the nearer by both rankings, walkers keep it (4,687 of 4,690 ticks, 151 walkers, 32 battles), so a princess tower does not simply win. The client 15.535.29 sweep (94 single-card scenes) fits the rule on 72 of 72 switches but cannot separate the rankings: its tower is always 2,000 or more farther than the enemy taken. Switched on at the 2026-09-28 flip build (scored on RoyaleSim 238274a). Alone on that build (every other key at its old arm; the corpus rebuilt by that build's fixture maker): sweep +106 within 250 / +69 both alive / +117 hp exact (Graveyard +106/+117); corpus +3,209 within 250 / +742 both alive / +1,219 hp exact, +2 reports at 95/95 (20260918-124946 +1255/+384, 20260918-122757 +984/+107, 20260920-071056-B +316/+322). Inside the 15-key flip, the set minus the set without it: sweep +106 within 250 / +69 both alive / +117 hp exact (Graveyard +106/+117); corpus +6,606 within 250 / +1,990 both alive / +4,158 hp exact, +1 report at 95/95 (20260920-071056-A +1541/+1672, 20260920-071056-B +1630/+1562, 20260918-124946 +1254/+386).

TARGET_RANK_DISTANCE.meaning: client16402_centre: target selection ranks every candidate, crown towers included, by its centre distance; which candidates are in sight (SightRange + both radii) is unchanged. centre_minus_target_radius: today's engine, which ranks by centre distance minus the candidate's collision radius (centre alone when ADD_CHARACTER_RANGE_TO_RADIUS is false).
TARGET_RANK_DISTANCE.open: A crown tower or a building choosing between enemies of different radii. No crown-tower acquisition separates the rankings (0 of 400 with two or more enemies in reach). For a building only Goblin Cages do (2 acquisitions and 37 held ticks, all the centre-nearest). One switch the rule misses: 20260918-121158 tick 2199, a Spear Goblin that took a Witch 61.9 beyond its sight sum, six ticks after dropping a doomed Skeleton. A unit created on the decision tick: 57 corpus switches took an enemy whose first frame is that tick, while in four client 15.535.29 sweep scenes (ElectroWizard, IceWizard, TriWizards, GoblinBarrel) the new unit was taken a tick later; that is the creation order, not this key.
TARGET_RANK_DISTANCE.promotion_rules: The test file (crates/royalesim/tests/target_rank_distance.rs) passes. Then score the corpus with this arm switched on alone; the registered prediction: the reports that move are among those of 112751, 115249.b1, 121158, 122757, 124946, 181741, 010218, 072148, 072831, 082459 and 083112 (both seats where both exist), where the two rankings part on the recorded positions, and 124946 gains.
TARGET_RANK_DISTANCE.engine: target.rs key: the first component of the preference key is the centre distance under client16402_centre, and centre minus the candidate's radius otherwise. It is read by scan (every Target phase rescan) and by the nearest-tower fallback of default_tower.

EQUAL_DISTANCE_TIE.confidence: LOW for the shipped arm own_frame_low_x, today's engine: of two candidates a scan ranks at one distance it takes the one with the lower x in the attacker's own frame, so a Blue unit on x 9000 with both enemy princess towers equidistant takes the left one. MEDIUM for own_frame_high_x on one event (a Blue unit; the Red seat unmeasured)
EQUAL_DISTANCE_TIE.provenance: READ on the 16.402 corpus (parity, round 9 item 36): sweep-GoblinDrill, the drill building at (9000, 21000), its t328 wave's Goblin (key 9) created exactly on (9000, 22000). Both Red princess towers stand 6,519 from it, within its sight, and the client's Goblin holds the RIGHT tower (14500, 25500) as its target on its first frame and steps (+113, +38) toward it; the engine takes the left one on its first frame by this tie-break and steps (-84, +85), its first divergence (75 lost). Its waves off the line, at (8500, 21000) and (9500, 21000), match in both. At x 9000 the two princess towers are always equidistant, so this event cannot tell a tie-break by x from a first pick by the unit's spawn lane (the tilemap gives the right lane at x 9000: targeting.FIRST_TOWER_PICK's open); either sends it right. It is also the first unit read standing exactly on the centre line, targeting.CENTRE_LANE_FRAME's one discriminating point, and it goes right, as engine_frame_tie_right says for Blue. own_frame_high_x is the seat-symmetric reading of the one event: a Red unit on x 9000 would take the engine-left tower under it and the engine-right one under an engine-frame rule, which no event has read.
EQUAL_DISTANCE_TIE.meaning: Which of two candidates a scan ranks at one distance (targeting.TARGET_RANK_DISTANCE) it takes first: own_frame_low_x, the one with the lower x in the attacker's own frame (then the lower y, then the earlier created); own_frame_high_x, the higher own-frame x (then the same). Both read the attacker's own frame, so both are seat-symmetric.
EQUAL_DISTANCE_TIE.open: A Red unit on x 9000 (own_frame_high_x sends it engine-left, an engine-frame rule engine-right). A tie between two troops, or a troop and a building (every read tie is two crown towers). Whether the client's first pick here is a distance tie at all or the unit's spawn lane (the two agree at every point where the princess towers are equidistant).
EQUAL_DISTANCE_TIE.promotion_rules: The test file passes (crates/royalesim/tests/equal_distance_tie.rs). Flip to own_frame_high_x when parity's scoring by override agrees with the reading above with nothing else moving; a Red unit created on x 9000 settles the frame.
EQUAL_DISTANCE_TIE.engine: target.rs key (the second element of the rank: the candidate's own-frame x, negated under own_frame_high_x)

CHASE_DROP_RANGE.provenance: MEASURED on client 15.535.29, the chase-drop scenarios: a P.E.K.K.A (SightRange 5000, radius 750), a Knight (5500, 500), a Prince (5500, 600) and a Mini P.E.K.K.A (5500, 450) walking down the right lane; a Hog Rider (600) or a Battle Ram (750), plain or raged, played behind the chaser and outrunning it up the same lane (|dx| <= 6). The chaser drops the runner for the crown tower on the first tick whose start-of-tick centre distance exceeds SightRange + the chaser's radius + the runner's radius + c: 18 of 18 drops fit one c in [-1008, -990), and -1000 fits. The decision reads both units' positions at the start of the tick, before the chaser moves. A chaser that has just finished a swing applies the same test on its first walking frame (a Prince at -990). Off the lane (a Valkyrie with dx 925, a Knight after a Battle Ram with dx 649, both held at a c above -986), the Euclidean distance does not fit one c with the lane drops; |dy|, max(|dx|, |dy|) and sqrt(w dx^2 + dy^2) with w below 0.365 all do. On a true diagonal (the diagonal chase scenarios: the Hog Rider on the bridge line, the chaser 2850-3508 to its side) a Knight held the Hog Rider at a centre distance of 6064.6 (dx -3508, dy -4947; SightRange + radii - 1000 = 5600) and a P.E.K.K.A at 5879.9 (dx -2850, dy -5143; 5350), walking after it until it stopped at its tower: the Euclidean distance would need c >= +464.6 and +529.9, so it is refuted; the weighted distance needs w < 0.267 at c = -1000. |dy| and max(|dx|, |dy|) fit every event. The drop is an edge: in the chase scenarios, on 35 of 35 ticks where a held troop first stood past the limit the chaser let it go, and on 31 of 31 ticks where a troop it had taken past the limit (a deploying Hog Rider, a deploying or walking Knight) still stood past it the chaser kept it, one Knight walking away for 16 ticks. Two Knights meeting at the left bridge take each other at 6423, past their limit of 5500, and keep each other to contact. Switched on at the 2026-09-26 loader2 flip wave 2 (RoyaleSim 126992a). On that build (the 19-key flip shipped), alone: sweep -3 within 250 / -1 both alive / +15 hp exact, +1 scene at 95/95 (BattleRam +109/+19, HogRider -112/-4); corpus -18 within 250 / +1 both alive / -1 hp exact (20260918-112751 -18/-1). Inside the 8-key wave, the wave minus the wave without it: sweep +319 within 250 / +37 both alive / +217 hp exact, +2 scenes at 95/95 (HogRider +210/+198, BattleRam +109/+19); corpus -18 within 250 / +1 both alive / -1 hp exact (20260918-112751 -18/-1). It ships with targeting.LEAPING_UNIT_TARGETABILITY: alone each loses sweep-HogRider because the other is missing (a Knight 590 native behind the client for want of the leap rule; a chase past the client's edge drop for want of this one).

CHASE_DROP_RANGE.promotion_rules: The test file passes. The flip moves every scene where a walking unit chases a faster one away from it; register the prediction before the flip.
CHASE_DROP_RANGE.engine: target.rs decide: for a walking unit whose live target is a unit out of its attack reach, drop it when the start-of-tick measure exceeds SightRange + both radii - 1000 and the previous Target phase held it within that limit (entity.rs chase_inside), before the move

CHASE_DROP_KNOCKED_TARGET.confidence: LOW for the old arm drops_knocked, the engine before this flip: the chase drop lets go of a target pushed past the limit by a knockback, which the client did on none of 3 such pushes. MEDIUM for client_holds_knocked on what was measured: 3 of 3, in two battles of the 16.402 corpus, all three a push by the holder's own boulder (a Bowler's). The arm holds any troop target sliding under a knockback; that a push by anything else (a spell, another unit's hit, a Mega Knight's landing) is held the same way is inferred from these three, not measured, and so is the hold against a nearer enemy in sight during the slide.
CHASE_DROP_KNOCKED_TARGET.provenance: MEASURED on the 16.402 corpus (one seat per battle). Three pushes carried a held troop target across the chase limit (SightRange + both radii - 1000 on max(|dx|, |dy|), start-of-tick), each by the holder's own boulder (the tick ranges are the crossings, from inside the limit to past it): 20260920-081051 ticks 947-949, a Bowler attacking a Bomber that its boulder pushed from 5,499 to 5,767 (limit 5,750; 259 past at most, on 953); 20260920-081819 ticks 2023-2025, the same pair, 13 inside to 212 past (362 past at most); 20260920-081819 ticks 1687-1688, a walking Bowler after a Knight its boulder pushed, 78 inside to 52 past (327 past at most). In all three the holder kept the target on every tick of the slide and on every later tick it stood past the limit: the attacking Bowler kept its swing running and launched its next boulder one HitSpeed (50 ticks) after the one before (081051: 928 and 978), and the walking one walked on after the Knight. The Knight that was pushed kept the Bowler too (the holder sliding, which the engine already holds through `Entities::knocked`). DOOMED_TARGET_DROP.meaning: projectile_attackers: at the Target phase of tick t, an attacker whose card fires a projectile (troops, buildings and crown towers) and whose current target X was doomed at the end of tick t-1 drops X unless it has launched a shot at X since acquiring it; its windup is cancelled and it rescans with every doomed unit excluded from the candidates, so it does not take X back while X lives. Doomed: the summed damage of the projectiles in flight at X (crown-tower arrows included) is at least X's hitpoints, and that damage's ETA, a countdown fixed at launch (the flight in whole ticks x 50 ms: ceil(distance / speed) fits 3,109 of 3,202 single-shot launches on client 15.535.29, the rest are a few units past a whole tick and read one tick less), is at most 600 ms (LOGIC_PENDING_DAMAGE_IGNORE_IF_DURATION_LESS). With two shots in flight the countdown followed the one that lands later, in both cases seen. Attackers without a projectile (whatever their range, flying or not), and attackers that have fired at X and are in reach, keep X. keep: the engine before this key flipped, where a doomed target is kept like any other.
DOOMED_TARGET_DROP.open: A fired attacker out of reach (Minions dropped at 257-434 beyond reach; a Mother Witch kept at 62-147 beyond). A melee attacker's first swing (the records cannot show whether a direct hit has started). Whether the ETA of several pending shots is the later or the earlier landing (two cases, the later in both, but both under 600, so no decision turned on it). A doomed building or crown tower as the target (all 62 measured drops were at troops). For a walker at a doomed princess tower see targeting.DOOMED_LANE_TOWER (2026-09-28): the walkers whose card fires a projectile let go of it and those without keep it, as this key's rule has it, and where they then walk is that key's. Whether a unit that was not already after X may acquire a doomed X. A moving target: the countdown is fixed at launch, but the tests use a still target and cannot tell it from an ETA recomputed each tick. The 16.402 reading of combat.POST_KILL_RETARGET_WAIT counts homing projectiles only; on client 15.535.29 the princess tower's arrow is in the pending damage. A projectile attacker that has fired at its target and then WALKS after it: the sweep's Skeleton Dragons drop the doomed Knight while walking (client 15.535.29) and one scenario Sparky keeps its doomed target while walking. Not settled (targeting.PROJECTILE_HOLD_SCOPE's client_troop_in_attack would rescan such a walker past its keep reach). (A 16.402 reading that walking Witches keep doomed Skeletons counted the Witch's Skeletons, which carry her card id and fire no projectile: the Witch herself had no walking tick with a doomed target in the corpus, and kept her target on 78 of 78 attacking ones.)

DOOMED_TARGET_DROP.engine: combat.rs doomed_by_shots_in_flight (the doomed set from the projectiles in flight at the tick's start: summed damage against hitpoints and shield, and ticks_to_land of the last shot against target.rs DOOMED_ETA_LIMIT_MS), built in state.rs phase_target before the decisions and handed to target.rs can_target through TargetCtx::doomed, where a projectile attacker neither keeps nor takes a doomed unit it has not fired at (entity.rs fired_at: set when it launches, cleared when its target changes). An event: on frame F an attacker whose card fires a projectile (a troop, a building or a crown tower) is attacking (behaviour state 2) target X; X still stands on F + 1 and the attacker names another target Y there; X is doomed on F (its pending damage is at least its hitpoints) and the attacker has not fired at X since taking it (no shot from it at X, no fall of its progress while it held X). When Y stands in the attacker's reach on the start-of-tick positions (the F frame: centre distance less both collision radii, at most Range) the attack progress on F + 1 is the progress on F plus 50, the swing running on: 57 of 57 (38 troops and buildings in 13 battles: Goblin Hut Spear Goblins 11, Musketeers 10, Spear Goblins 7, Minions 7, Cannons 2, a Bomber; and 19 crown towers). When Y is out of reach the progress reads 0: 44 of 44 troops walk (state 1) and 19 of 19 crown towers go idle. 20260920-072148 tick 1035: a Minion at progress 1050 of its 1200 attacking a Skeleton that a Musketeer's shot (217 against 81 hitpoints) dooms switches to another Skeleton 2,419 from its edge (Range 2500), reads 1100 and 1150 and fires on 1037 on the old cycle; its partner, whose new target stood 3,132 away, walks with progress 0. The engine cancels the first Minion's swing and starts a fresh cycle, so that Skeleton dies on 1053 in the engine against 1040, and the second Minion does not drop it as doomed on 1038 as the client does. The switch itself (which target, on which tick) is targeting.DOOMED_TARGET_DROP's and is unchanged. Switched on at the 2026-09-27 round-4 flip (scored on RoyaleSim fc4dbe4). DOOMED_DROP_SWING.meaning: client_keep_in_reach: dropping a doomed target is a switch away from a live target, not a broken lock, so combat.RETARGET_PROGRESS decides what it does to the swing: under keep_when_dead_or_in_reach an attacker whose new target already stands in its reach keeps its progress and fires on the old cycle, and one whose new target is out of reach, or that finds none, cancels. cancel: the old arm, shipped until the 2026-09-27 round-4 flip (scored on RoyaleSim fc4dbe4), where an attacker in its swing that drops a doomed target cancels the swing whatever it takes next.
DOOMED_DROP_SWING.open: One corpus attacker switched away from a doomed target it had already fired at and kept its progress (the fired-at exemption of targeting.DOOMED_TARGET_DROP says it keeps the target; one event). The walker's load timer: on the 072148 switch the walking Minion's attack_load_timer ran on (700, 650, 600, ...) while its progress read 0, which combat.ATTACK_CYCLE's credit may or may not reproduce; not measured here. Two melee switches in reach reset their progress, where combat.RETARGET_PROGRESS's in-reach rule keeps it (not this key's: a melee attacker drops no doomed target; not read further). This key, combat.CORPSE_SWITCH_REACH (the replacement of a dead target) and combat.RETARGET_PROGRESS (a switch from a live one) describe one law: the swing is kept only when the new target stands in reach. One key may serve all three when they flip.
DOOMED_DROP_SWING.promotion_rules: The test files (crates/royalesim/tests/doomed_drop_swing.rs, tests/test_doomed_drop_swing.py) pass. Then score the corpus with this arm switched on alone and stacked on placement.TROOP_TOWER_TAPS = client16402_half_open_relocate; the registered prediction: the reports that move are among the seats of 20260918-112215, 112751, 115249.b1, 121158, 122757.b1/.b2, 124946, 130203.b1/.b2, 134739, 20260919-182539, 20260920-005517, 070448, 072148 and 083112 (both seats where both exist), where the client makes such a switch, and 20260920-072148's Minions gain from tick 1041 on in the stacked run.
DOOMED_DROP_SWING.engine: target.rs decide: an attacker in its swing whose live target can_target refuses only because the shots in flight doom it (dropped_for_doom) no longer sets cancel_attack under client_keep_in_reach; state.rs phase_target_with then cancels only a switch that combat.RETARGET_PROGRESS cancels (not in reach under keep_when_dead_or_in_reach). Plant doomed_drop_cancels_swing.

DOOMED_LANE_TOWER.meaning: projectile_walkers_take_king: a unit that targeting.DOOMED_TARGET_DROP makes let go of a doomed princess tower, or not take it (a card that fires a projectile, with no shot launched at the tower since acquiring it), treats the tower as fallen as the one it walks to: its default tower is the next one, the king, in every pick (targeting.FIRST_TOWER_PICK's spawn-lane window, FALLEN_LANE_TOWER_PICK, the lane by x, the nearest), wherever it stands. Doomed: the set the Target pass read, the shots in flight at its start. A unit without a projectile, and an attacker that has shot at the tower, keeps it; a doomed king is kept (it has no next tower); inert under DOOMED_TARGET_DROP = keep. walkers_take_king, parity's proposal as written: every WALKING troop (its attack phase idle) neither keeps nor takes a doomed princess tower, and its default tower is the king; attackers keep it. standing: the engine before the 2026-09-28 round 9 flip, where a doomed princess is the lane tower while it stands.
DOOMED_LANE_TOWER.open: Ten distinct events, three on 16.402. Where the king stands out of sight the engine's walker has no target and walks to the king by default, while the client's target reads the king: the walk is the same, the target column is not. A walker with a projectile that has fired at the doomed princess (none seen). The replayed MinionHorde scene had diverged before its event, so (5) is the engine's rule applied to the capture's shots, not a replay. Whether walkers_take_king's walker includes a charging or dashing unit (none seen).
DOOMED_LANE_TOWER.promotion_rules: SETTLED at the 2026-09-28 round 9 flip (see provenance): parity's scores by override were positive on the special-form scenes and the 16.402 corpus, and no report lost. The test file (crates/royalesim/tests/doomed_lane_tower.rs) passes. The registered prediction held: sp-scene-c's six variants and sp-m6a/b1/b2/c/d gained within 250 through their spirits' walk to the king, scene-c's first divergence (t729) moved to none on five variants and to t1241 on the sixth, and the corpus moved only on 20260920-083112, where a Goblin Hut's two Spear Goblins walk at a doomed princess. What would reopen it: a walker whose card fires a projectile keeping a princess tower the engine's doomed set holds, or a walker without one taking the king; a walker with a projectile that has already fired at the doomed princess (none seen).
DOOMED_LANE_TOWER.engine: target.rs default_tower (every pick reads live(), which lane_fallen filters), lane_fallen, drops_when_doomed (targeting.DOOMED_TARGET_DROP's population, shared with can_target), walker_refuses_doomed_princess (walkers_take_king, in can_target). state.rs phase_target_with takes the doomed set under the new arms too and leaves it in Scratch::lane_doomed for the same tick's Path phase and charge_pass (TargetCtx::lane_doomed). The read-only instrument BattleState::doom_reading (combat.rs shots_in_flight_at). Test: crates/royalesim/tests/doomed_lane_tower.rs.

LOGIC_CANCEL_HIT_FROM_LONG_DISTANCE_RANG.confidence: LOW (the recorded corpus contradicts 1500 on all 3 swings that test it; measured_2026_09_22)
LOGIC_CANCEL_HIT_FROM_LONG_DISTANCE_RANG.meaning: An attack already started is only cancelled if the target gets this far beyond range.
LOGIC_CANCEL_HIT_FROM_LONG_DISTANCE_RANG.measured_2026_09_22: Read from the attack timers of the recorded corpus (data/derived/replay, attack_progress_ms and attack_load_timer_ms). A swing is under way when attack_progress_ms % HitSpeed > 50 (the engine's own hit-started test) and lands when the counter crosses the next multiple of HitSpeed; distance beyond range follows targeting.ATTACK_RANGE_RULE (centre distance less Range and both CollisionRadius, cards.json). Across the 40 distinct battles, 13 swings of attackers that fire a projectile (crown towers included) had their target leave range while the swing was under way. 11 were kept to the hit, 10 of them with the target at most 887 beyond range and one far past 1,500: a Lava Pup (20260920-071744-A, key 59, ticks 1957-1983) whose Goblin walked away fired with it 2,506 beyond range. 2 were dropped well inside 1,500: a Spear Goblin (20260918-112751, key 57, tick 1965) dropped its Valkyrie at 501-550 beyond range, on the tick after the Valkyrie first stood beyond the Spear Goblin's own SightRange (5,500 edge to edge, passed by 1), and the king tower (20260918-124946, tick 2517) dropped a Knight that had gone 500 beyond its range. So 1500 predicts none of the 3 swings that test it. The rival attacker_sight_range (a started swing holds while the target stays within the attacker's own SightRange, edge to edge) predicts the Lava Pup (its SightRange sits 3,900 past its Range) and the Spear Goblin, and misses the king tower, whose SightRange equals its Range and which held its Knight 500 past both. Ground melee attackers are LOGIC_PRESERVE_TARGET_IF_HIT_STARTED's business: they drop a target that leaves range when a nearer enemy is in reach. With no nearer enemy their swings also land with the target out of range, a Skeleton's 1,131 beyond (20260918-134739-A, tick 603); four melee swings were dropped 34 to 467 beyond range with no nearer enemy, which neither value explains. Recorded on client 16.402 by the client instrument that records ground-truth traces from the real game.
LOGIC_CANCEL_HIT_FROM_LONG_DISTANCE_RANG.proposed_value: attacker_sight_range, once it is implemented in target.rs and the corpus parity run does not get worse; it fits 2 of the 3 deciding swings where 1500 fits none, on a sample of three. Left at 1500 here because a value change alters engine behaviour and must ride one announced rebuild with a parity score beside it.

LOGIC_PRESERVE_TARGET_IF_HIT_STARTED.measured_2026_09_22: Read from the attack timers of the recorded corpus (data/derived/replay). Inside range the engine keeps the target under both values, through the 25 hysteresis, so the 8,297 in-range frames with a nearer enemy (8,282 kept, 6 switched, 9 dropped) do not separate them. Ten swings in 6 distinct battles reach the deciding case. Eight, all ground attackers that strike directly (a Valkyrie, a Prince, a Mini P.E.K.K.A, a Knight, three Skeletons and a Goblin), switched to the nearer enemy on the first tick the old target stood 27-122 beyond range, the old target still alive and on the board; the swing ran on (the counter kept adding 50 across the switch) and the next hit landed on the new target. PROJECTILE_HOLD_SCOPE.meaning: client_troop_in_attack: a troop holds its target past its keep reach, to Range + both radii + 500, only while it is in its attack (its attack phase, which the previous tick's Attack phase left, stands it). Walking, it keeps its target within Range + both radii + LOGIC_RANGE_EXTENSION_TO_KEEP_TARGET and rescans past it, as a direct striker does. Buildings and crown towers hold on every tick. A launch at the target from beyond reach ends the hold under both arms. every_tick: today's engine, whose projectile attackers hold on every tick whatever they are doing.
PROJECTILE_HOLD_SCOPE.open: A troop that attacked its target and then walks after it inside the hold (after a launch beyond reach whose rescan kept the target, or after a hit when the target ran out before the next swing began): this arm rescans it, and neither client shows a nearer enemy in sight there. Under this arm the chase drop (targeting.CHASE_DROP_RANGE) reaches a walking projectile troop from its keep reach, where every_tick reached it only past the hold. Buildings are held on every tick: none walks, and no sample separates. This is the branch targeting.DOOMED_TARGET_DROP leaves open (a projectile attacker that has fired and then walks after its target), and it is the lock targeting.LOGIC_PRESERVE_TARGET_IF_HIT_STARTED's meaning describes.
PROJECTILE_HOLD_SCOPE.promotion_rules: The test files (crates/royalesim/tests/projectile_hold_scope.rs, tests/test_projectile_hold_scope.py) pass. CENTRE_LANE_FRAME.meaning: Which frame decides a unit's lane for LOGIC_XPOS_BASED_TOWER_TARGETING, and therefore which enemy princess tower a targetless unit walks to. own_frame_tie_left: the attacker's own (rotated) frame, centre going own-left. engine_frame_tie_right: the absolute arena x, centre going engine-right.
CENTRE_LANE_FRAME.candidates_differ_only_at: BLUE STANDING EXACTLY ON x = W/2, and nowhere else in the arena for either seat. Verified over every integer x for both seats. That value is unreachable by a deploy, because a tap snaps to its tile centre: x=9000 and x=9001 both land a unit at 9500. So no tap-driven scenario can ever discriminate these arms, and the 12 rows above never stood on the line. To settle it, a unit must WALK onto x = W/2 and be read on the tick it is there.
CENTRE_LANE_FRAME.why_this_arm: Chosen on a structural prior, the 15.535.29 scenarios being silent. own_frame_tie_left is seat-symmetric at every x; engine_frame_tie_right breaks the 180-degree seat rotation at x = W/2 exactly. RoyaleGym's rotation gate measured that break on build 1b8fc1eace21feb7 (one seed of three -- a tie is rare, which is the signature of a tie rather than a systematic flip). Both seats share one policy head and the observation is built in the acting side's own frame so that Blue and Red are the same problem, so an absolute-direction tie makes the same board a different game depending on colour. No evidence for the other arm, a measured cost against it.

history.provenance: the 12 client 15.535.29 scenarios, read as showing that the seats do not mirror on the centre line
history.overturned_by: parity session the same day: both arms reproduce all 12 rows, so the experiment never discriminated them. The divergence it was introduced to fix was a DEPLOY POSITION -- the harness spawned the fixtures at their raw tap (x=9000, a tile corner) where the client spawns at the tile centre (9500), and at 9500 the own-frame rule already agrees. Across all 21 fixtures the only lane divergence was side 0 at x=9000, while x=8999, x=9001 and every side-1 row agreed, which is exactly what 'the arms differ only at 9000' predicts. Changing this rule moved the engine to agree with a fixture convention and cost seat symmetry to do it.

CENTRE_LANE_FRAME.observability: THE ARMS MAY BE BEHAVIOURALLY INDISTINGUISHABLE IN REAL PLAY, measured over the 73-battle corpus on 2026-09-23. (a) x = W/2 = 9000 is NOT a path-node x: nodes sit on half-cell centres k*500+250, so the nearest are 8750 and 9250 and a unit walking the grid never stands there. (b) 3477 non-tower truth entities yield 72 unit-ticks with a unit exactly on x=9000 -- 55 Archer and 14 Goblins in behaviour_state 4, 3 Archer in state 1 -- and ALL 72 carry target = -1, no resolved pointer. (c) ZERO unit-ticks in the corpus have a unit on x=9000 while holding a resolved crown-tower pointer. Positive control on that scan: the same logic finds 557705 such unit-ticks off the centre line across 63 cards, so the zero is a measurement and not a broken query. A unit reaches the exact centre line only while DEPLOYING, before any tower pointer exists. So the corpus cannot settle this, and the behaviour difference between the arms was never observed in 73 recorded battles -- which is also why the fixture score moved when this key was flipped: the movement came entirely from the oracle fixtures placing units on a tile CORNER, which real play does not do.
CENTRE_LANE_FRAME.promotion_rules: Reach x = W/2 by MOVEMENT rather than by a tap -- a unit whose walk crosses the centre exactly on a tick boundary, or a placement that is not tile-snapped -- and record which tower it then walks to. Until then neither arm may be cited as measured, and a figure that improves after flipping this key has not confirmed anything: the arms differ at one coordinate that the game never places a unit on.
CENTRE_LANE_FRAME.note: Not a globals.csv key: it is a choice royalesim must make that the game makes implicitly. Related: targeting.LOGIC_DEFAULT_TARGET_USE_LANE_ID is FALSE in 15.535.29, consistent with both arms -- the tilemap lane-id model (nearest lane cell) predicts LEFT at x=9500 on an exact distance tie, and client 15.535.29 goes RIGHT, so tower choice is not the path lane id.

FIRST_TOWER_PICK.meaning: client_spawn_lane: at creation a unit gets a lane. lane(x, y) is the lane (1 left, 2 right) of the nearest lane-marked half-cell of the arena tilemap to (trunc(x/500), trunc(y/500)): squared cell distance, the first minimum in column-outer, row-inner ascending order. A summon member (a unit of a troop card that deploys two or more units) also reads its deploy point's x, a: with c = trunc((x + 5)/500) (a member at 8999 counts as on column 18) and ac = trunc(a/500), when (a < x, ac < 18 and c >= 18) or (a > x, ac > 18 and c <= 18), and the nearest lane cell to (ac, trunc(y/500)) has the same lane as lane(x, y), the member takes the other lane. Any other unit (a single troop, a spell's or a spawner's units, a death spawn) has lane(x, y). The lane is read at the unit's creation point, before any contact push of its first tick. A Miner's lane is read at its deploy point, where it surfaces. For its first 500 ms after it becomes active a unit only picks among the enemy princess towers of its own lane; after that it picks the princess tower nearest in x, and takes it over its current target only when it is strictly nearer (squared distance). current_x: today's engine, the tower of the unit's current x on every tick.
FIRST_TOWER_PICK.open: Whether a re-pick also follows a lost target (the corpus's re-takes follow the current x, 15 of 15). The lane of a unit that is not a summon member created exactly on x 9000 (the tilemap gives the right lane on both sides; no measured unit tests it).
FIRST_TOWER_PICK.promotion_rules: The test file passes. The flip moves every scene where a summon member is created within a half-tile of the centre line on the other side of it from its deploy point; register the prediction before the flip.
FIRST_TOWER_PICK.engine: the unit's creation (formation_members knows the deploy point) stores the lane; target.rs default_tower reads it until the first re-pick; arena.rs lane cells (the tilemap bits already in arena.json)

LEAPING_UNIT_TARGETABILITY.meaning: airborne: a unit mid-leap (the river leap of a JumpEnabled troop, movement.JUMP_WATER_HOP) is a target only for attackers that attack air. It is read in the Target phase from the leap state the previous tick left, so a ground-only attacker still holds the unit on the hop tick F, drops it from F+1 (a running windup is cancelled, as for any target it can no longer target), cannot acquire it on the landing tick, and can acquire it again on the tick after. Only target selection changes: the unit does not become a flying unit for collisions, area damage or spells. ground: today's engine, where a leaping unit stays a ground target for every attacker.

CONTACT_LAW.provenance: SETTLED ON THE LIVE 16.402 CAPTURES on 2026-09-19/20 and VERIFIED against every one of them. The per-tick contact and locomotion update (the step, the avoidance and separation scans, the position write and the update order) is implemented in crates/royalesim/src/move16402.rs; the evidence for every rule is the live capture set. THE LAW: (1) each tick every attack update runs before every move update, and the move updates run one unit after another in CREATION order against a bucket index of collision circles (each grown by 250 for movers) built from the start-of-tick positions -- unit i sees units j < i already moved and j > i where they started (a replay with previous-tick neighbours reproduces 46 % of the contact ticks, the sequential order 98 %). (2) avoidance (states 1 and 4, not while attacking): the entities whose circle overlaps the circle of radius min(R,500) around pos + facing (facing has length 256) vote; a static (a unit that does not move) wins over movers, the last seen wins; offset 0 -> +-200, a running offset +-20 only when a static is seen, clamped to +-200, then -10 toward zero every walk tick (so 190 is the visible onset and +10/tick the visible ramp); a static whose circle contains the current waypoint's centre pops that waypoint. (3) separation (states 1, 2, 4): every overlapping neighbour of either side -- buildings and towers included, touching counts (d2 <= (R1+R2)^2; my radius capped at 500 against a static) -- adds trunc(dx x mag / d), trunc(dy x mag / d) away from it with mag = min(299, trunc(min(R1+R2-d, 300) x M_other / M_self)) + 1, and one count; coincident centres push +-1 in y by team. (4) the step: dist = max(1, isqrt(dist2)); step = min(speed, dist, 250); heading = trunc((aim - pos) << 8 / dist); step vector = trunc(heading x step / 256) per axis; facing := normalize256(aim - pos); if the offset is nonzero the step is rotated by the blend v' = ((256 - |a|) v + a perp(v)) >> 8 renormalised to the step length (tan theta = a / (256 - |a|)); the accumulator's MEAN (trunc(acc / count)) capped at 150 is added; pos += step, an axis that crosses out of the grid clamps to the cell edge, and only a DEPLOYING ground unit is clamped at a water edge; then reached := proj(aim - pos', segment) <= 1000. (5) Mass as loaded from the card data: an empty Mass column becomes tdiv(floor(R^2/250) x R, 62500) and every Mass is clamped to [1, 20] -- towers, Tombstone and Goblin Hut weigh 20, a Cannon 13, a Tesla 8 -- which is why a unit touching a tower flies back at the 150 cap. (6) With an empty path and a target out of range the unit walks at the point reach = Range + own CollisionRadius away from the target on the line to itself. VERIFICATION (over the 31 live captures, every frame pair, the world rebuilt at the start of each tick): 240389 / 242232 unit-tick positions exact (0.99239); isolated 0.99367, separation active 0.98319, two or more overlaps 0.98406, against buildings 0.99829, avoidance active 0.98221, spawn overlaps 0.99656, attacking 0.99277; the post-decay avoidance offset exact on 0.99962. The 1843 misses are diagnosed (Skeleton crowds with dying neighbours, missed stomp pauses / freezes, replanned aims, Rage inference, knockbacks not in the trace); no contact-law alternative explains more than 0.005 % of them. The Rust implementation is gated by equivalence with an independent reimplementation on random worlds (20 000 / 20 000 per seed). THE TIE INSIDE ONE GROUP (fixed 2026-09-28, round 9): two bodies first sighted in one group of the index are met in creation order, the update order of (1), which is the order the 242,139 exact offsets were measured in. The engine broke that tie by the entity SLOT, which a slot reused after a death puts out of creation order (move16402.rs Index::query now keys it by Body::seq, each body's Entities::creation_seq). Read on client 16.402, 20260918-130203.b2 t1568: a deploying Ice Spirit whose look circle lies in one group with two waiting Goblins created that tick, mirror images across its heading; the client meets the later-created (right) one last and holds -190, and the slot order met the other one last and gave +190. With the tie by creation order the spirit's offset is the client's, -190 held through t1573, then -180 and -170, and it stands on the client's points through t1576; 20260918-122757.b2's Goblin takes the client's +190 on t1168 for the same reason. Scored by sim against the shipped run of the round 9 flips' tree (towers left out; within 250 / both alive / hp exact unit-ticks): the 16.402 corpus (73 reports) moves on 9, +2,035 / +301 / +549, 8 up and 20260918-115249.b1 -10 / 0 / +1; 20260918-122757.b2's first divergence moves from t1174 to t2647 and 20260918-130203.b2's from t1629 to t1928. The client 15.535.29 scenario fixtures (every one on 2026-09-28 18:33, 1,369, each in its own replay_parity process: 11 abort on a crown tower slot 3 the engine does not have and 1,358 are scored) move on 2, -9 / +102 / +83: sp-m4-towerhit-s0 0 / +82 / +63 and sp-m5-clone-s0 -9 / +20 / +20, 952 at the bar either way (95% of both-alive unit-ticks within 250 and 95% hp exact). The battles of tests/hash_continuity.rs meet such ties, but in none does the order change the offset. Run with every avoidance scan made both ways (sim, 2026-09-28), its battles on both card tables make 240 scans that meet their neighbours in another order by slot than by creation, 70 of them two neighbours other than the scanner and 6 two of the neighbours that vote, and none of the 240 ends on another offset or waypoint pop. So none of its hashes moved, and that test cannot see this fix: crates/royalesim/tests/avoidance_tie_order.rs is its guard.

PUSH_MODEL.provenance: NONE. The data ships a Mass column (Skeleton 1, Knight 6, Giant 18, Golem 20) and the wiki says mass matters qualitatively -- but a field existing is not a formula, and the best public reimplementation ignores Mass entirely and weights by speed ratio instead.
PUSH_MODEL.why_it_matters: Unit push governs body-blocking, swarm spread, and whether a tank walks through or around its own support -- i.e. most of what a player is actually doing. The old engine had NO unit collision whatsoever, which is the single biggest reason it could not model the game.
PUSH_MODEL.promotion_rules: Directly measurable from captures: record scripted head-on collisions across a mass ladder (Skeleton 1 / Knight 6 / Giant 18 / Golem 20) and a speed ladder, then fit the displacement ratio against mass-ratio, speed-ratio and the product. Also check for a per-tick displacement cap, which is invisible in aggregate.
PUSH_MODEL.offline_note: NOTHING RECORDS THE PUSH. It is not separately observable in the offline trace corpus -- it must be fitted from the movement RESIDUAL (movement.CONTACT_DOMAIN): |step| about S plus a 15-28 unit lateral residual perpendicular to the heading for crowd separation, and 0.06-2.5 x S, possibly opposing the heading, for combat pushback. placement.$comment: WHERE A BUILDING MAY BE PUT, which is a different question from what its body does to movement (collision.BUILDING_FOOTPRINT_MODEL). A building occupies a whole number of TILES when it is placed, and troops walk through that box freely: over the recorded corpus a troop centre is inside a Cannon's box on 394 of 943 nearby frames and inside a princess tower's on 11923 of 49173. Settled 2026-09-22 over 114 recorded building placements.

FOOTPRINT_TILES.confidence: HIGH for the cards the recordings pin, MEDIUM for the rest
FOOTPRINT_TILES.provenance: MEASURED on 114 unique building placements recorded from the real game on client 16.402 (the A/B twins of one battle deduplicated), through the client instrument that records ground-truth traces. The footprint is an N x N tile box with N = ceil(2R / tile) + 1 from CollisionRadius: R 500 gives 2, R 600 gives 3, R 1000 gives 3 and R 1400 gives 4. Pinned per card by sweeping N against every placement's legality and every relocation: Cannon 3 (N = 1 refuted by two placements, N = 5 by four), Tombstone 3, Goblin Hut 3, Bomb Tower 3, Goblin Cage 3, Barbarian Hut 3, Tesla 2, the surfaced Goblin Drill building 2. Inferno Tower, Mortar, X-Bow and Elixir Collector follow the rule and are NOT individually pinned, because no recorded placement of them discriminates. The losing arms: an all-odd N of 1 explains 31 of the 64 tapped placements and N of 5 explains 30, against 64 of 64 for the rule; floor + 1 and round + 1 both fail on R 600, which is the witness, because 2R is 1.2 tiles.
FOOTPRINT_TILES.why_it_matters: It decides whether a Cannon can be put against the arena wall or flush inside a tower, which is a large part of defensive placement.
FOOTPRINT_TILES.promotion_rules: To pin the four unpinned cards, record a placement of each whose legality differs between N = 1, 3 and 5: tapped one tile from a wall separates 3 from 1, and tapped two tiles from a tower separates 3 from 5.
FOOTPRINT_TILES.engine_contract: crates/royalesim/src/arena.rs placement_tiles; the box is built by Arena::placement_box and judged by Arena::box_zone. It is NOT a collision shape: collision.BUILDING_FOOTPRINT_MODEL still decides what movement sees.

TOWER_FOOTPRINT_TILES.confidence: HIGH on the king, MEDIUM on the princess
TOWER_FOOTPRINT_TILES.provenance: MEASURED on the same 114 placements: a crown tower blocks a building the way another building does, and the same size rule gives a princess tower 3x3 and a king tower 4x4. Scoring the alternatives against every placement, a princess of 1 tile fails one placement, a princess of 4 or 5 fails at least five, and a king of 5 fails five. THE CORPUS CANNOT SEPARATE a 3x3 princess from a 2x2 one, nor a 4x4 king from a 3x3 one, because every building box has integer tile edges, so a box overlaps the closed 2.5-to-4.5 span exactly when it overlaps 2-to-5. The shipped reading is the one that needs no special case: a tile-aligned box centred on a tile centre must be odd, and one centred on a corner must be even.
TOWER_FOOTPRINT_TILES.why_it_matters: It decides how close a defensive building may sit to a tower, and the viewer draws it.
TOWER_FOOTPRINT_TILES.promotion_rules: Record a building tapped so that its box would overlap the disputed ring of a tower by exactly one tile, on each of the two towers.
TOWER_FOOTPRINT_TILES.engine_contract: The towers take the same arena.rs path as buildings, through their own CollisionRadius.

ILLEGAL_TAP.confidence: HIGH that the tap is moved rather than refused; LOW on which of the two relocating arms
ILLEGAL_TAP.provenance: MEASURED: of the 64 recorded building taps whose tap point is known, 39 ended somewhere other than the tapped tile, so the game MOVES a building whose footprint does not fit rather than refusing the play, and 'refuse' is refuted outright. The two relocating arms are NOT separated by the corpus: every relocation with a reliable tap moves 1 or 2 tiles (two at ring 1, three at ring 2), and the two orders agree below ring 3, because a ring-r diagonal is r x sqrt(2) away while a ring-(r+1) axial cell is only r + 1. Relocation is only ever observed INSIDE the placer's own half, because a player's own client never sends a tap from outside it, so the engine refuses a tap whose own point fails the cell or territory rules rather than extrapolating past what was seen.
ILLEGAL_TAP.why_it_matters: It decides whether a building tap is a refusal or a different building, which changes what a placement mask means and what a policy can learn.
ILLEGAL_TAP.promotion_rules: Record a building tap whose only fits are three or more rings away, with a ring-r diagonal fit and a ring-(r+1) axial fit both available. The two arms then land it on different tiles.
ILLEGAL_TAP.engine_contract: crates/royalesim/src/state.rs building_placement, bounded by PLACEMENT_SEARCH_RINGS = 30 tiles, which spans the arena. The ring scan order is built in the placer's frame so the two seats mirror; the corpus leaves exactly one tie, so the order is the engine's choice and not a measurement.

BUILDING_TERRITORY.engine_contract: crates/royalesim/src/state.rs deploy_rule returns Territory::OwnHalf for a building; arena.rs box_zone judges the BOX against it, not the tap.
BUILDING_TERRITORY.gap_box_zone_has_no_rect_test: arena.rs box_zone applies NO enemy-crown-tower no-deploy rect test, and it should, because the BOX is what occupies the ground. The tap rule does apply one (territory_zone, alive enemy rects) but only under EnemyTowerRects, and a building uses OwnHalf, so today nothing consults a rect for a building and the gap cannot fire. It fires the moment this key takes its rival arm: the box would go untested against rects while its snapped centre is tested, which is the wrong one to test. The concrete wrong outcome is a building whose BOX overlaps an alive enemy tower's rect while its centre does not. Whoever flips this key adds the rect test to box_zone IN THE SAME CHANGE. Noted 2026-09-22 after the gym session proved its honest-tap arm lossless on the invariant BOX LEGALITY IMPLIES TAP LEGALITY, which this gap would silently falsify.

ALGORITHM.provenance: MEASURED. OFFLINE TRACE CORPUS (Clash Royale 15.535.29 / versionCode 150535029). Traces: data/oracle-native/{walk (6 cards x 1 deploy), lane_sweep_Knight (128 files / 64 distinct experiments), building_Giant (12), repath_Giant (2), meet (3), orient (1)} -- 150 units, 51926 entity-ticks. Analysis: passes over the offline traces -- grid, cost model, occlusion and goal rule; every law re-measured over every unit of every trace; timing and the speed law. Report: docs/movement-measurements.md; implementation contract: docs/pathfinder-spec.md. Cost stage: over 150 recorded first paths, the recorded path is exactly cost-minimal for its own endpoints under road 5 / plain 8 / water impassable / bit-16 impassable / 8-connected / diagonal x sqrt(2) -- 0 suboptimal, 0 infeasible. 4-connected reproduces 44/150; a uniform diagonal leaves 3 paths strictly dearer than the optimum (witnesses lane_sweep_Knight c00_r06 173 vs 171, c08_r04 197 vs 190, c10_r06 181 vs 174); a flat cost 8 fails 96.
ALGORITHM.supercell_2025_release_note: Troops now rely much less on lanes. Previously, they would move horizontally to reach their lane before advancing. Now, they move diagonally. | Troops can now see Buildings and adjust their movement in advance instead of walking straight into them and only navigating around after a collision.
ALGORITHM.why_it_matters: This is the mechanic the whole project is named after, and the version everybody documented is the one Supercell replaced on 2025-03-31.
ALGORITHM.promotion_rules: Black-box discrimination, not archaeology. Design scenarios where candidate models predict visibly different tracks -- a building offset from the lane centre, a building wall forcing a non-lane detour, a building destroyed mid-path -- record the real tracks, and score each model. The engine must therefore keep the pathfinder behind a swappable interface with all candidates implemented.
