history.provenance: The three most complete public engines implement three DIFFERENT algorithms and none was verified against the client. Worse, all three model the PRE-2025 game.
history.overturned_by: the path_nodes published in the 15.535.29 traces: a weighted A* over a 36x64 half-tile grid reproduces the cost of 150/150 first paths; lane_flow, authored waypoints and pure post-2025 lookahead do not.

candidate_meanings.weighted_grid_astar: THE MEASURED 2026 MODEL (royalesim PathModel::Oracle2026, src/path2026.rs): 8-connected weighted A* over the 36x64 half-tile grid, cell-entered costs (PATHFINDING_COSTS), the sqrt(2) diagonal (DIAGONAL_COST_RATIO), CHEBYSHEV heuristic over the GOAL SET (HEURISTIC_FORM; octile is refuted by the live 16.402 corpus), half-open AABB occlusions of EVERY building on the board (OCCLUSION_MODEL; friendly-only is refuted likewise) priced at PATHFINDING_BUILDING_COST rather than blocking (OCCLUDED_CELL_TREATMENT), and the reach goal rule (PATH_GOAL_RULE).
candidate_meanings.weighted_grid_astar_community: The pre-measurement community model royalesim still carries (PathModel::GridAStar): uniform octile 10/14 step costs, no cost table, mover-radius-inflated blocking and a string-pulled waypoint list. REFUTED for the 2026 game -- a uniform diagonal makes road 5 / plain 8 and a flat cost 8 classify every path identically, so the road discount becomes unidentifiable, and the flat model then fails 96 of 150 paths.

ALGORITHM.still_open: The EXPANSION ORDER is not reproduced: the exact node sequence matches 13 of 76 distinct experiments at best (see TIE_BREAK). The cost model, the occlusions and the goal predicate are settled; which of several equally-optimal paths the game takes is not. RESTATED 2026-09-18 against the live 16.402 corpus: it remains the single largest gap, but the ceiling moved -- 192/292 exact node sequences with the goal cell HANDED to the search and 142/292 with the reach predicate (HEURISTIC_FORM, promoted to Chebyshev on that evidence). Two things narrowed it: the tie-break knob provably cannot move the result under strict-better relaxation with an f-ordered open list (TIE_BREAK), and the residual has ONE systematic signature -- the recorded path shifts column one cell earlier than the model, always immediately after a road/bridge segment. Settled on 2026-09-19 (PATH_SEARCH).

PATH_SEARCH.provenance: SETTLED ON THE LIVE 16.402 CAPTURES on 2026-09-19 and verified against every first path they publish (three independent reproductions of the search agree on every rule below). Every tie-break below was chosen because it reproduces the published node lists, not because a different order was ruled out by argument. The rules cover the search and the path request that enters it, the expansion and relaxation, the heuristic, the cell cost, the building box, the per-tick occlusion rebuild, and the move component's goal-cell choice. THE RULES: (1) ONE goal cell, chosen by the move component: scan rows ascending over target_cell +- (reach/500 + 1), columns ascending when the mover's x < 9000 native else descending, keep the highest category (2 = dry and outside every building box, 1 = water or boxed) and within it the strictly smallest squared distance to the MOVER (first scanned wins ties); reach = Range + own CollisionRadius. (2) the cell cost: -1 out of bounds only; water costs BLOCKED = 50 for a walker and is priced, not refused; lane cells cost ROAD = MATCHINGROAD = 5; else DEFAULT 8; then max(base, occlusion[cell]) where every building of BOTH sides stamps BUILDING = 50 over the half-open box [c - R, c + R) after snapping its centre UP to the next multiple of 500 on each axis, and a box that does not fit entirely inside the grid stamps nothing. NO_DEPLOY plays no part in the cell cost; the king block is priced by the king's own R = 1400 box. (3) step cost = entered cell's cost x 10, x 14 on a diagonal (integer); h = 5 x (10 max(|dc|,|dr|) + 4 min(|dc|,|dr|)) (HEURISTIC_METHOD 1, times DEFAULTHEURISTIC_COST 5); f = g + h. (4) among equally cheap routes, the published route is the one an open list ordered on f alone (no g, no h, no insertion order) produces when equal keys keep their existing order. (5) neighbours in the order N, S, W, E, NW, SW, SE, NE; the start is expanded before the loop; a popped cell is closed, expanded, and the loop ends when the GOAL is closed (i.e. after it has been popped and expanded). (6) an open node reached with a strictly better f takes the new parent, g and f (REFRESH_OPENNODES); a closed node is never revisited (REOPEN_CLOSEDNODES = FALSE). (7) the published list is the parent chain from the goal, goal first, without the start cell. VERIFICATION (scored against the captures): over the 747-case fixture, 615/616 live 16.402 first paths and 128/128 offline 15.535 lane-sweep paths reproduce the exact recorded node sequence. Three further live cases are skipped, not scored: Goblins chasing a MOVING target whose goal cell the trace cannot recover (the sample's target position is the previous tick's). The one live case that diverges takes an equal-cost lane route (tests/oracle2026.rs names it). The trace-fitted arm scored 168/345 and 15/128. Controls run on the same harness: water impassable instead of priced 306/388 and 24/128; friendly-only occlusion 336/388; KS_POS_TO_TARGET_GROUND_AVOID_BUILDINGS off 421/425. See docs/pathfinding.md.
PATH_SEARCH.why_it_matters: Which of several equally cheap routes a unit takes is decided by heap order, and the whole engine's positional fidelity in a crowded lane rests on it: 331 of 425 live first paths have a non-unique optimum.
PATH_SEARCH.promotion_rules: SETTLED. Re-open only against a new client build (re-verify); a trace disagreement is a capture or fixture problem first.
PATH_SEARCH.engine_contract: path2026::plan_cells dispatches on this key: client16402 -> path16402.rs (absolute-coordinate planning, Red un-rotated; NavRequest.team). trace_fitted_astar -> the 2026-09-18 goal-set A* driven by TIE_BREAK / HEURISTIC_FORM / OCCLUDED_CELL_TREATMENT, kept runnable as the refuted arm. The goal-cell scan's box demotion is passed the TARGET's flying flag (NavRequest.target_flying, path2026.rs avoid_buildings16402), and the cost field prices water at PATHFINDING_COSTS.value.water for a JumpEnabled mover (NavRequest.jumper, path16402.rs cell_cost_for) -- see movement.JUMP_WATER_HOP for what the walk then does at the water.
supersedes: TIE_BREAK (heap order is the tie-break, no neighbour-order knob reproduces it)
HEURISTIC_FORM (octile 14/10 to ONE goal cell, not Chebyshev over a goal set)
PATH_GOAL_RULE (the reach predicate picks the goal SET; the code picks one cell of it by category then mover distance)
WATER_RULE_GROUND (water is priced 50 and pushed, never entered because never cheaper)
OCCLUSION_MODEL (the box snaps the centre up to a multiple of 500 and is dropped when it leaves the grid; the target building is not exempt)
DIAGONAL_COST_RATIO (14/10 in x10 integer units, not 1414/1000)
open: the target-side condition on KS_POS_TO_TARGET_GROUND_AVOID_BUILDINGS: the engine passes the global ANDed with the TARGET not flying (FlyingHeight > 0; path2026.rs avoid_buildings16402, NavRequest.target_flying, phase_path16402 hands it the target's flying flag), so a ground unit whose target hovers over a building box takes the nearest in-reach cell, boxed or not (tests/jump16402.rs a_ground_unit_chasing_a_flying_target_takes_the_boxed_cell). No corpus case has a flying target, so the live score above is unchanged by construction and the flying-target arm itself is unmeasured; regression plant goal_ignores_flying_target

REPATH_INTERVAL_TICKS.why_it_matters: Cadence governs how fast a unit responds to a building dropped in its path, which is the central defensive interaction in the game.
REPATH_INTERVAL_TICKS.promotion_rules: Measure the lag between placing a building and the unit visibly changing heading.

history.overturned_by: the 15.535.29 measurements: there is no periodic replan timer. 150 structural path recomputes over 31859 path-ticks (0.47 per 100), evenly spread across trace families; the gaps within a trace are {17, 24, 29, 100, 185, 190, 228, 248, 250} with no common period. A 30-tick timer would give about 10 changes per trace.

REPATH_INTERVAL_TICKS.engine_contract: royalesim reads this as Option<i32> (state.rs Calib::repath_interval_ticks). null = event-driven; a positive value re-arms the legacy periodic cadence for the pre-2026 models only. The 2026 model ignores it entirely.
REPATH_INTERVAL_TICKS.limits: This bounds OBSERVABLE path changes only. A recompute that returns an identical list is invisible in the traces (8 of 94 tail-surviving recomputes leave path_segment_direction frozen and path_node_consumed clear), and PATHFINDING_SAMEPATH_EPSILON = 3 may be suppressing near-identical results.

PATHFINDING_COSTS.water: WATER (7) IS PAID since the river hop was measured (movement.JUMP_WATER_HOP): a JumpEnabled or hovering mover pays WATER_COST for a water cell and any other walker BLOCKED (50), both before the occlusion max. The engine reads it as Calib::path_cost_water and pays it for every mover with a card.rs JumpDef (path16402.rs cell_cost_for; NavRequest.jumper). Over the five live hops, pricing water at 7 for the jumper reproduces every published node list and pricing it at BLOCKED reproduces none of the five (regression plant jumper_pays_blocked, red on 5 of the 8 gates of tests/jump16402.rs). On the shipped arena the cost-7 water DOES move a jumper's route: from the river centre (9500, 12500) the Hog Rider's published list runs through the water cells (26,32), (25,31), (24,30) -- the diagonal to the bridge's far corner cell (27,33), cheaper at 7 than the detour at DEFAULT 8 -- where a walker's never touches water (the fixture's Hog Rider case; tests/jump16402.rs a_jumper_routes_across_priced_water_where_a_walker_takes_the_bridge); from the lane placements (x 3500 / 14500) the straight line north IS a bridge column, so the flag is invisible there. The HOP -- what the walk does when its next node is water -- is movement.JUMP_WATER_HOP, not this table. The `action` text above ('Does ground A* cross water at 7? NO') stands for walkers.

PATHFINDING_COSTS.note: This matters beyond pedantry: if these costs do not exist, then 'buildings bend paths' collapses, and the Cannon-pull behaviour is entirely a TARGETING effect (building-targeters carry 7000-9500 sight range vs the 5500 modal value). Those are two different mechanisms producing the same observation and they predict differently for the case that matters: whether a unit already locked on a tower deviates around a building placed off its path.

PATHFINDING_COSTS.no_primary_source: Searched every key, cell and column name in all 18 vendored csv_logic files: NO key or column named PATHFINDING_*_COST exists. The only globals containing PATHFIND are LOGIC_SPAWN_PATHFIND_REACHED_RADIUS_FROM_SPEED and LOGIC_PATHFIND_BACKWARDS_TRY_KEEP_TARGET; the only columns are SpawnPathfindSpeed/Effect/Morph. The claimed cost table therefore has no primary source in the 2018 data, and the data supports the TARGETING explanation of building pull instead: building-targeters carry longer sight ranges (Hog Rider 9500, Balloon 7700, Giant 7500 vs modal 5500). This does not rule out costs in the post-2025 client.

HOVERING_WATER_RULE.provenance: MEASURED on client 15.535.29, the hovering scenarios (seed 363): the Battle Healer played at (11500, 14500) and the Royal Ghost at (8500, 14500), their non-hovering twins the Knight and the Mini PEKKA on the same tiles, each pair once with no enemy in sight and once with a red Goblin Cage at (9500, 18500). The card data sets Hovering = true on the Battle Healer and the Royal Ghost (and on an evolution row, not measured). With no enemy, the Battle Healer's path holds the water cells (25,31) and (26,32), its centre crosses the river's middle line (y 16000) at x 13000, west of the right bridge (13500 to 15500), and goes 740 from land or bridge; the Royal Ghost's path holds 3 water cells, it crosses at x 6999 and goes 988 from land. With the cage, both walk straight across (a 4-cell path, 3 cells of water) and stand and attack the cage from over the water: the Battle Healer on 39 frames at (11168, 15893), 893 from land, the Royal Ghost on 47 frames at (8321, 16006), 994 from land, until the cage dies. The Battle Healer's water cells and crossing are exactly those of a JumpEnabled row walking priced water without its hop (this engine's Hog Rider under movement.JUMP_WATER_HOP = walk_priced_water, from the same tile: cells (25,31) and (26,32), crossing x 13000, 740 from land). Today's engine: the Battle Healer holds no water cell, crosses at x 13858 on the bridge, goes 158 from land, and attacks the cage only from the far bank. HEURISTIC_FORM.superseded_by: SUPERSEDED BY pathfinding.PATH_SEARCH = client16402, whose search uses an octile h = 5 x (10 max + 4 min) to ONE goal cell and reproduces the recorded node sequences outright. The scores below were measured on the trace-fitted arm (path2026.rs), which is kept runnable as the refuted arm; this key steers only that arm.
HEURISTIC_FORM.formula: h(cell) = min over the GOAL SET of PATHFINDING_DEFAULTHEURISTIC_COST * max(|dc|, |dr|), i.e. 5 * Chebyshev, with the goal set unchanged (see why_the_goal_set).
HEURISTIC_FORM.provenance: MEASURED. LIVE CLIENT, CR 16.402 -- recorded from the real game and converted to the offline trace format; 13 captures. Analysis: the expansion pass (exact node-sequence reproduction; corpus 337 first paths, 292 after de-duplicating the two two-client pairs). Report: the live 16.402 measurements. HANDED THE RECORDED GOAL CELL, exact node-sequence reproduction: the engine's shipped ortho-first + octile 78/292; Dijkstra (h = 0) 171/292; forward A* with strict-< relaxation, entered-cell costs and h = W * max(|dc|, |dr|) for W in 3..5, 192/292 (65.8 %). Offline, the same sweep on lane_sweep_Knight reads 36/128 for Chebyshev against 14/128 for ortho-first + octile, so this is not a 16.402 change -- it is a better fit on both builds. THE WEIGHT IS NOT PINNED: W = 3, 4 and 5 are indistinguishable on this corpus; 5 is taken because it is the shipped PATHFINDING_DEFAULTHEURISTIC_COST, a datamined constant that fits rather than a fitted one. With the reach PREDICATE as the goal test instead of the handed goal cell the best falls to 142/292, which is the goal-cell question (PATH_GOAL_RULE `limits`), not the heuristic's.
HEURISTIC_FORM.admissibility: 5 * Chebyshev is admissible and consistent against this cost field, so REOPEN_CLOSEDNODES = FALSE stays safe and the returned path is still exactly cost-minimal. The cheapest cell costs road = 5 to enter and the cheapest diagonal 5 * 1414/1000 = 7, so a route of Chebyshev distance N costs at least 5N; and h changes by at most 5 across any neighbour while a diagonal step costs at least 7. crates/royalesim/src/path2026.rs `the_measured_heuristic_is_chebyshev_and_both_forms_are_admissible` asserts the consequence directly -- swapping the form may not change what a path COSTS.
HEURISTIC_FORM.why_the_goal_set: ADMISSIBILITY TRAP, and it is not cosmetic. THIS HALF IS UNCHANGED BY THE 16.402 PROMOTION -- only the metric inside the minimum changed. The goal is 'any cell within reach of the target' (PATH_GOAL_RULE), so a heuristic computed to the TARGET cell over-estimates the cost to the actual goal by up to reach/500 * 5 and is non-zero at goal cells -- A* then pops a goal that is not the cheapest one. Measured on the walk traces: with h to the target cell the search returns column 7 (cost 152) instead of the recorded column 6 (cost 150) for every one of the six cards; with h as the min over the in-reach cells it returns the recorded path.
HEURISTIC_FORM.still_not_reproduced: The heuristic does not change WHICH paths are optimal (the cost model was validated with Dijkstra), only the expansion order. 192/292 is a ceiling, not a solution: the residual has one systematic signature -- the recorded path shifts column one cell EARLIER than the model, always immediately after a road/bridge segment (witnesses 20260918-112215:25:MiniPekka and 20260918-112751:7:Giant both 8,33 -> 7,32 -> 7,31 -> 8,30 where the model stays 7,30; 112751:32:Musketeer 5,39 -> 6,38 vs 5,38). A heuristic charging more than the 11-vs-8 diagonal premium for a one-column offset would produce it, but every b - a >= 4 member of h = a*(max-min) + b*min scores far worse overall. It may not be a heap A* at all: a different heuristic form, a post-processing pass over the raw route and a hierarchical search are all still live. Keep it swappable.

history.overturned_by: the live 16.402 expansion sweep: handed the recorded goal cell, octile reproduces 78/292 exact node sequences where 5 * Chebyshev over the same goal set reproduces 192/292 -- and 171/292 for h = 0 alone, so the octile form was scoring WORSE than no heuristic at all. It was never an observation, only an argument from the shape of the step cost.

HEURISTIC_FORM.dropped_candidates: `octile_to_target_cell_minus_reach` and `none` were removed from the candidate list because royalesim implements no arm for either, so naming one in `value` would be refused at load (state.rs `pick`) rather than silently substituted. The registry may still LIST alternatives the engine does not run, as the only()-backed keys do (state.rs documents that); only the value has to resolve. Their evidence is not lost: `octile_to_target_cell_minus_reach` is the admissibility trap described in why_the_goal_set and is refuted on the walk traces, and `none` is Dijkstra, measured at 171/292 above. Add either back together with its arm.
HEURISTIC_FORM.engine_contract: royalesim reads this into Calib::heuristic_form (state.rs) and path2026.rs `heuristic_weights` SELECTS the chamfer weights from it -- (5, 5) for Chebyshev, (5, 7) for octile -- which `goal_set_heuristic` then runs as a two-pass transform (exact for any weights with straight <= diag <= 2*straight). Both listed candidates are wired; a name with no arm is refused at load, never silently substituted. This key used to be read by `only()` and not stored at all, so its value could not have been changed without an engine edit.
HEURISTIC_FORM.promotion_rules: Raise to HIGH by reproducing the node sequence, not by scoring it better than its rivals: 192/292 is a large improvement and still a minority. Re-open the WEIGHT (3, 4 and 5 are indistinguishable) with a corpus whose h-weight is discriminating, which requires a board where the heuristic's inflation changes the pop order.

TIE_BREAK.provenance: UNVERIFIED AND KNOWN TO BE INSUFFICIENT. Where several successors are equally optimal the recorded paths prefer the orthogonal one on 1568 of 1672 ambiguous steps (93.8 %), but an ortho-first neighbour order still reproduces only 22/140 exact node sequences, and with the sqrt(2) diagonal exact ties are rare -- so the residual divergence is not a classic tie-break at all. 76 distinct experiments over neighbour order x queue discipline x relaxation rule; none exceeds 13/76. OFFLINE TRACE CORPUS (Clash Royale 15.535.29 / versionCode 150535029). Traces: data/oracle-native/{walk (6 cards x 1 deploy), lane_sweep_Knight (128 files / 64 distinct experiments), building_Giant (12), repath_Giant (2), meet (3), orient (1)} -- 150 units, 51926 entity-ticks. Analysis: passes over the offline traces -- grid, cost model, occlusion and goal rule; every law re-measured over every unit of every trace; timing and the speed law. Report: docs/movement-measurements.md; implementation contract: docs/pathfinder-spec.md.
TIE_BREAK.why_it_may_be_unreachable: The recorded path_nodes is a POST-TICK snapshot: a repath can insert one or two nodes below the old waypoint that the unit aims at and consumes within the same tick, so they appear in no recorded frame. 142 ticks in the corpus show this; all carry path_node_consumed == 1 and 140 are explained exactly by a cell 1-2 rows nearer in the same column. Any pathfinder fitted to the recorded node lists is missing those insertions.
TIE_BREAK.why_the_knob_provably_cannot_matter: LIVE 16.402, the expansion sweep over the live corpus: 36 combinations of 6 open-list keys x 6 neighbour orders produce ZERO different paths across 418 samples. The reason is structural, not statistical -- with strict-`<` relaxation and an f-first heap, rival parents of a cell differ in g by 2, 3 or 6 while their h differs by 0 or one cell-weight, so an f-tie between them essentially never occurs and the neighbour order never gets a vote. The offline 1040-configuration sweep therefore had at most ~5 genuinely distinct members. THE VALUE STAYS A PLACEHOLDER AND IT IS A HARMLESS ONE; the note below that 'the three orders give a DIFFERENT path on only 25 of 6802 engine problems' is the same fact measured on the engine's own grid. Whatever settles the expansion order will have to change the open-list key or the algorithm, not the neighbour list -- and the leading suspects are now the HEURISTIC (promoted to chebyshev_over_goal_set on the same corpus, 78/292 -> 192/292) and the possibility that it is not a heap A* at all.
TIE_BREAK.promotion_rules: Do not record a tie-break as settled on this corpus. Settle it with a scenario whose optimum is unique but whose EXPANSION order is observable, or by the measured 16.402 search itself (PATH_SEARCH = client16402 settles it). Note that a scenario cannot settle it while the relaxation stays strict-`<`: see why_the_knob_provably_cannot_matter.
TIE_BREAK.engine_contract: royalesim reads this key into Calib::tie_break and path2026.rs `neighbours()` SELECTS the neighbour order from it -- the three candidates above are the three the engine implements, and Calib::from_json refuses any other name. It used to be read and then ignored, with one hardcoded order underneath, so two of the three values named a discipline that never ran. MEASURED while wiring it: the neighbour order reaches the result ONLY through the push counter in the open-list key (f, then the smaller h, then FIFO), so over a 6802-problem sweep on the shipped grid the three orders give a DIFFERENT path on only 25, and never a different cost. Whatever settles spec 3.6 will therefore have to change the open-list key, not just the neighbour list (path2026.rs `OpenKey`). The two candidates cw_from_n / ccw_from_n were dropped from this list because the engine does not implement them; add them back together with their arms.

OCCLUSION_MODEL.engine_divergence_target_building: KNOWN, DELIBERATE, AND NOT MEASURED EITHER WAY. royalesim exempts the building a unit is currently attacking from its own occluder set (state.rs `NavRequest.ignore`, path2026.rs `CostField::for_mover`). The scored reference model (779/785) does NOT -- it occludes every building including the target, and that is how the 97 enemy-king crossings were scored, so on a unit walking at a king the two models differ: the reference model charges 50 for the last cells, the engine sees plain terrain under them (and the bit-16 goal exemption, OCCLUDED_CELL_TREATMENT, carries the goal cell). It costs nothing on any gate in the repo. OPEN: scoring the live corpus with the target building exempted would settle it; the corpus already has the 97 king approaches that discriminate.
OCCLUSION_MODEL.corpus: RE-SCORED 2026-09-18 after the oracle2026 fixture was regenerated from the traces (tools/make_oracle2026_fixture.py): the box admits ALL 37 published first paths -- no INTERIOR cell of any of them lies inside a friendly box. OCCLUDED_CELL_TREATMENT.meaning: An occluded cell is ENTERED at PATHFINDING_BUILDING_COST = 50 (the entered-cell cost, so a diagonal pays 50 * DIAGONAL_COST_RATIO = 70). It is not a wall.
OCCLUDED_CELL_TREATMENT.provenance: MEASURED. LIVE CLIENT, CR 16.402 -- recorded from the real game and converted to the offline trace format. Traces: the live corpus: 13 native captures, absolute arena coordinates, both sides, training camp and friendly battles at level 11; 785 first-published paths of ground troops over 16 cards. Analysis: the cost-model / occlusion / goal-rule fit, driven by the path sweeps and cross-checked against an independent 292-path corpus. THE DISCRIMINATOR THE OFFLINE CORPUS LACKED: 97 of 785 live paths cross a building-box INTERIOR -- always exactly one cell, always the cell before the goal, always inside the enemy king's R = 1400 box ((17,8) x68 and (18,8) x17 for side-1 units attacking the side-0 king, (18,55) x9 and (17,55) x3 the other way). Scores over the 785 (the live path sweeps, own + enemy occluders throughout): hard block with no goal exemption 6 suboptimal + 456 infeasible; hard block WITH the goal exemption 20 suboptimal + 97 infeasible; cost 50 6 suboptimal + 0 infeasible. The independent 292-path corpus: 257 pass under hard block, 292 under cost 50.
OCCLUDED_CELL_TREATMENT.the_value_is_bracketed_not_pinned: Anything >= 14 scores identically: cost 12 -> 114 failures, 13 -> 99, 14 / 16 / 20 / 25 / 50 / 100 / 1000 -> 6. The SHIPPED PATHFINDING_BUILDING_COST = 50 sits inside the window and is what is used -- a datamined constant that fits, not a constant fitted to the data. Also open: whether the occluded cost REPLACES the terrain cost or is ADDED to it. Every discriminating cell in the corpus is road (5) or plain (8), so 50 and 50 + terrain are indistinguishable at this resolution; the engine replaces.
OCCLUDED_CELL_TREATMENT.an_alternative_reading_survives: All 97 crossings are the ENEMY KING. OCCLUDED_CELL_TREATMENT.promotion_rules: SETTLED as 'a cost, not a block'. Re-open only against a capture that shows a path refusing a strictly cheaper crossing, or against a second reading of the same corpus. The exact CONSTANT is a separate question (see the_value_is_bracketed_not_pinned) and is still open below 50.
OCCLUDED_CELL_TREATMENT.scope: APPLIES TO BUILDING OCCLUSION BOXES ONLY -- never to water, and, since 2026-09-18, no longer to bit-16 terrain either. WATER: the two used to share one branch in path2026.rs `CostField::terrain`, so selecting `cost_50` here silently made the river traversable and overrode WATER_RULE_GROUND, which Calib::from_json refuses to load with any value but `impassable`. BIT-16: the same defect, one key deciding another's question -- `cost_50` is a statement about BUILDINGS and it used to make the deploy-restricted arena-edge strips walkable as a side effect. path2026.rs `CostField::terrain` now writes the goal-exempt OCCLUDED sentinel for bit 16 unconditionally and `CostField::occlude` overwrites it with the box cost where the two overlap (see precedence). One ledger key may not quietly override another.
OCCLUDED_CELL_TREATMENT.precedence: THE BOX COST TAKES PRECEDENCE OVER THE TERRAIN FLAG, and that is the actionable finding -- neither analysis stated it, and their apparent disagreement about bit 16 was entirely this. A bit-16 cell inside a building box costs 50 like any occluded cell. An engine that resolves terrain FIRST and lets an impassable bit-16 flag win costs 39 of 337 live paths, because the tilemap's bit-16 king 3x3 block IS the king tower's own R = 1400 half-open box, cell for cell. Live paths use 744 distinct cells, of which 13 carry bit 16 and ALL 13 lie inside a king box; the other 104 bit-16 cells (the arena-edge strips) are never entered by any path, and no live path touches water anywhere. So bit 16 has no measurable pathfinding meaning of its OWN -- impassable, 5, 8, 12, 50 and 1000 all score 6/785 once enemy occlusion is on -- and spec rule 2.2 is NOT refuted. It is kept impassable outside every box as the conservative reading of an unidentifiable flag.
OCCLUDED_CELL_TREATMENT.engine_contract: royalesim reads this into Calib::occluded_cells (state.rs) and path2026.rs `CostField::occlude` selects the value it stamps: PATHFINDING_BUILDING_COST under `cost_50`, the goal-exempt OCCLUDED sentinel under `block`. Both candidates are wired and a name with no arm is refused at load. The SHAPE is kept separately from the cost -- `CostField::in_building_box` answers 'is this cell inside a box' whichever treatment is selected -- because under `cost_50` nothing is refused and every gate that asked `refused` would have passed vacuously.
OCCLUDED_CELL_TREATMENT.goal_cell_exemption: SPEC 4.6 BECOMES UNNECESSARY, and deleting it is an improvement. 456 of 785 live goal cells sit inside a building box, so under the old hard-block reading the exemption was load-bearing; under cost 50 it can go and the score IMPROVES -- 6 failures without it against 12 with it, otherwise identical settings. In royalesim the exemption is now unreachable for building boxes (they are a price, not the sentinel) and survives only on the bit-16 king block, where it is what keeps a short-reach card able to path to a king tower at all and where the live corpus cannot see it either way (path2026.rs OCCLUDED).

PATH_GOAL_RULE.superseded_by: SUPERSEDED BY pathfinding.PATH_SEARCH = client16402, whose ONE goal cell comes from `choose_goal_cell` in path16402.rs. The rule below is read only by the trace-fitted arm (path2026.rs), kept runnable as the refuted arm.
PATH_GOAL_RULE.provenance: MEASURED. OFFLINE TRACE CORPUS (Clash Royale 15.535.29 / versionCode 150535029). Traces: data/oracle-native/{walk (6 cards x 1 deploy), lane_sweep_Knight (128 files / 64 distinct experiments), building_Giant (12), repath_Giant (2), meet (3), orient (1)} -- 150 units, 51926 entity-ticks. Analysis: passes over the offline traces -- grid, cost model, occlusion and goal rule; every law re-measured over every unit of every trace; timing and the speed law. Report: docs/movement-measurements.md; implementation contract: docs/pathfinder-spec.md. The path is truncated at the FIRST cell whose CENTRE is within Range + CollisionRadius of the TARGET'S CENTRE POINT -- the target's centre, not its footprint, and not the sum of both collision radii. Verified two-sided (the goal is in reach AND its predecessor is out of reach) on 150/150 first paths, including the meet/ traces with moving targets and side-1 units. Rivals: 'Range only' 1/140, 'Range + both radii' 0/140, 'footprint edge' 0/140. Per-card stop cells from one deploy tile: Giant (reach 1950) row 47; Knight 1700, Golem 1500, HogRider 1400 all row 48; MiniPekka 1250 and Skeletons 1000 row 49.
PATH_GOAL_RULE.limits: NECESSARY, NOT DETERMINATIVE. It is a condition on the last node, not a predictor of which cell the search stops at: between 12 and 52 cells per sample satisfy it (median 32) and the recorded goal cell is not the cheapest reachable in-reach cell in 114 of 140 samples, with no cost ties among them. Handing an A* the recorded goal cell raises exact-sequence reproduction from 22/140 to 43/140 -- THE GOAL CELL IS AN OUTPUT OF THE EXPANSION ORDER. Implement the reach test as the goal PREDICATE and let the pop order choose; do not implement 'pick the nearest or cheapest in-reach cell'. A constant k added to Range + CollisionRadius fits all 150 paths for any k in [-125.2, +24.8), so the reach is pinned to about +-75 units, not exactly.
PATH_GOAL_RULE.sign: The standoff is on the APPROACH side, not unconditionally negative in y: in meet/Knight_vs_HogRider ticks 250-273 the Knight's target is BELOW it and the goal row is cell_centre_y + reach. An unconditional minus puts the goal on the far side of the target. The predicate form (a radius about the target centre) carries this for free.
PATH_GOAL_RULE.cadence: Re-derive the goal cell every tick and replan only when the resulting CELL changes (REPLAN_TRIGGERS): that reproduces the 137 observed goal-driven replans with the observed 1-2 tick lag.

candidate_meanings.segment_projection: Consume the tail node when the REMAINING DISTANCE ALONG THE SEGMENT, dot(node_centre - post_move_position, segment_direction) / 256 with integer truncation, is <= WAYPOINT_ARRIVE_RADIUS. segment_direction is the 1/256 unit vector frozen when the node was assigned (norm256(node_centre - POST-move position), the engine's own path_segment_direction field).
candidate_meanings.euclid_post_move: the pathfinder spec's rule 7.5 as written: consume when the post-move EUCLIDEAN distance (floored integer sqrt) to the node centre is <= WAYPOINT_ARRIVE_RADIUS.

WAYPOINT_ARRIVE_RULE.provenance: MEASURED, and it SUPERSEDES the spec's rule 7.5 on the same corpus. OFFLINE TRACE CORPUS (Clash Royale 15.535.29 / versionCode 150535029). Traces: data/oracle-native/{walk (6 cards x 1 deploy), lane_sweep_Knight (128 files / 64 distinct experiments), building_Giant (12), repath_Giant (2), meet (3), orient (1)} -- 150 units, 51926 entity-ticks. Analysis: passes over the offline traces -- grid, cost model, occlusion and goal rule; every law re-measured over every unit of every trace; timing and the speed law. Report: docs/movement-measurements.md; implementation contract: docs/pathfinder-spec.md. Scored over all 34644 stable-list tick pairs (3975 ordinary drops, 30669 keeps) (reproduced by tools/oracle_diff.py --rule): euclid_post_move misses 153 drops and fires 3 times early (156 errors); segment_projection misses 6 and fires 10 times early (16 errors), and ALL TEN of its early fires carry avoidance_offset != 0 (110, 190, 150, 140, 130, -160) -- the avoidance regime that is outside the domain of every movement law here (CONTACT_DOMAIN). On the walk family (the isolated-unit gate) segment_projection has ZERO errors; euclid_post_move misses 4, which is exactly why the spec expected '~4 % of pop ticks to diverge'. The mechanism it adds was already in the spec as rule 7.7 -- the segment direction is frozen at consumption and held for the whole segment, zero exceptions on the walk traces -- it was simply never connected to the consumption predicate.
WAYPOINT_ARRIVE_RULE.disproof_of_a_pure_radius: No radius on the post-move distance can be right: restricted to ISOLATED units (single-unit traces, avoidance_offset == 0, behavior_state == 1) the Knight corpus contains a DROP at distance 1004.478 and a KEEP at 1000.648, so drops and keeps overlap in distance. They do not overlap in the projection.
WAYPOINT_ARRIVE_RULE.engine_contract: royalesim stores the frozen direction per entity (entity.seg_dir) and evaluates the predicate AFTER the move, at most one pop per tick (state.rs phase_path_2026). Setting this key to euclid_post_move runs the spec's rule 7.5 instead.

ATTACK_CYCLE.confidence: HIGH -- measured on 1690 fresh attack entries and 911 first projectile launches of the live corpus (below); the windup arm misses every one of them
ATTACK_CYCLE.provenance: MEASURED on the whole live 16.402 corpus (73 captures): the captures carry two per-unit attack counters, and on the frame a unit starts attacking a fresh target they read LoadTime + 50 and LoadTime on 1690 of 2024 entries (the misses are spawned units filed under their spawner's card, whose LoadTime is not the spawner's); 911 of 1004 projectile units launched their first projectile exactly (HitSpeed - LoadTime) / 50 - 1 ticks after that frame (Musketeer 13, Archers 9, Bomber 3, Bowler 9, princess tower 15, king tower 9; the misses are interrupted cycles); 453 of 520 uninterrupted melee cycles dropped the target's hp on that tick (Knight 9, Barbarian 7, Skeleton 9, Goblin 11); 113 of 172 re-entries with the second counter still running show the first at LoadTime + 50 - (load - 50); every later hit HitSpeed apart, the first counter running on across hits (1400, 2800, 4200 on a Prince) and the second reset to LoadTime on every hit. The princess tower of capture 20260920-003751: attacking at t280, progress 50, the first arrow at t295 (progress 800), then t311 and t327; the engine fired on the acquisition tick. THE RULE (combat.rs attack_step_progress): every tick the LOAD TIMER counts down 50 clamped at 0, whatever the state; with a target, the unit attacks this tick when the target is in range (targeting.ATTACK_RANGE_RULE) OR a hit is already started (progress % HitSpeed > 50), else its progress is RESET to 0 and it stops attacking; attacking, a fresh cycle (progress == 0, not charged) is CREDITED progress = LoadTime - loadTimer (with loadTimer := LoadTime) and then += 50, so a unit whose load timer has run out starts its first cycle at LoadTime + 50 and every later tick adds 50; when LoadTime > HitSpeed no credit is given and the cycle waits until the load timer is <= HitSpeed; a CHARGED entry snaps progress to the next multiple of HitSpeed instead (charge.CHARGED_HIT_TIMING). THE HIT lands on the tick progress crosses a multiple of HitSpeed, which sets loadTimer := LoadTime and leaves progress running. So the FIRST hit on a fresh target lands (HitSpeed - LoadTime) / 50 - 1 ticks after the entry frame, the cadence is HitSpeed, and a unit re-entering range within LoadTime of its last hit or entry gets only LoadTime - (remaining load) of credit. TWO BOUNDARIES OF THE RULE, both corrected against the corpus: (a) the hit-started test is STRICTLY GREATER than 50, not >= 50 -- a fire leaves the progress on an exact multiple of HitSpeed, so the next credited tick puts the remainder at exactly 50 on every cycle of every shipped card (Knight 1250 % 1200, Prince 1450 % 1400, Musketeer 1050 % 1000), and under >= a unit whose target stepped out of reach on that tick kept swinging instead of resetting; the corpus moves with the correction (Skeletons 43.6 -> 43.9 % within 250 with the alive-mismatch share 14.6 -> 13.5 %, Bomber 75.8 -> 76.1 %). (b) A HELD unit's load timer keeps counting down: the hold (a -100 HitSpeedMultiplier, combat.HIT_SPEED_BUFF) stops the PROGRESS step alone, so a unit frozen mid-cooldown does not keep its whole remaining reload and its first hit after the hold is not LoadTime / 50 ticks late.
ATTACK_CYCLE.meaning: progress_credit: the measured progress counter -- first hit HitSpeed - LoadTime after entering range (a princess tower, LoadTime blank = 0, waits a full HitSpeed = 16 ticks for its first arrow), HitSpeed between hits, a swing already started finishes on a target that stepped out of range, the load timer's remainder reduces the credit on re-entry. windup_load_time: the earlier engine -- a LoadTime windup after entering range, then HitSpeed - LoadTime of cooldown -- so every first hit landed 2 x LoadTime - HitSpeed later than the game's (a Knight 400 ms late, a princess tower 800 ms EARLY).
ATTACK_CYCLE.promotion_rules: Measured. The hit-speed buff is combat.HIT_SPEED_BUFF (Rage's HitSpeedMultiplier into the 50 ms step); LoadFirstHit (Sparky) is not modelled. Re-open only against a live first hit that parts from the rule on an uninterrupted cycle.
ATTACK_CYCLE.engine: read by crates/royalesim (state.rs Calib::from_json -> attack_cycle); combat.rs attack_step runs the progress / load-timer counters (Entities::attack_ms = progress, Entities::attack_load_ms = the load timer, snapshot format 16), AttackPhase::Windup = attacking with the swing under way (the target lock), Cooldown = attacking on the hit tick, Idle = not attacking; the Path phase holds any attacking unit. The old arm stays runnable as windup_load_time. tests/reach.rs pins the tower's first arrow and the Knight's first hit from the card data.

A unit whose row sets LoadFirstHit leaves its deploy with attack_load_timer at LoadTime (3000 for the Sparky) and the timer counts down 50 a tick from then on, walking or not. On entering the attack its progress is LoadTime - (the timer on the tick before) + 100, and it launches when the progress reaches HitSpeed (4000). RETARGET_PROGRESS.meaning: keep_when_dead: a unit whose target DIED keeps its attack progress and fires on its own cadence; switching away from a target still ALIVE cancels the swing as before. reset_always: any target change cancels, which is what the engine did before this key existed. The size of the difference is set by LoadTime, because the fresh cycle credits back min(LoadTime, elapsed) through the load timer (combat.ATTACK_CYCLE): a princess tower's LoadTime is 0, so under reset_always it lost the whole interval and reloaded in 19 ticks instead of 16, while a Musketeer's 300 ms covered the gap and it measured the same under both arms.

What would REOPEN it: a scenario where a unit switches away from a LIVE target -- this key says nothing about that case, which still cancels, and nothing here measured it. A client 15.535.29 scenario would settle both halves at once by firing at a swarm and at a passing target. reset_always is kept runnable as the arm the engine shipped through 2026-09-23, so the defect can be reproduced rather than only described.

POST_KILL_RETARGET_WAIT.engine: state.rs phase_target. THE DOOMED TEST: the damage of the homing projectiles in flight at the tick's start, summed per target (level-scaled as fired, from every source), against the target's hitpoints; each unit keeps the answer for its live target in entity.rs target_doomed, so at the loss it holds the victim's last live tick. THE ARM: a unit whose target is dead waits unless (a) its unit_name is on value.attack_finish_override_units, (b) its attack progress is 0, or (c) its card has a projectile and target_doomed is set. THE HOLD is the list arm's code: held with no target, the attack timer zeroed on the loss + 5, the next target accepted on the loss + 6; phase_attack freezes a waiting unit's timers and the Path phase holds it like an attacking one (entity.rs retarget_wait). retarget_wait is hashed under either waiting arm, target_doomed under client16402_attack_finish only. value.units is read by client16402_measured_list alone.

POST_KILL_RETARGET_WAIT.measured_2026_09_25: client16402_attack_finish, MEASURED on the 16.402 corpus per event (1,164 events: an attacker in state 2 whose target is alive on one frame and gone on the next, tick-contiguous frames, one seat per battle). A unit whose target is removed takes its next target after 1 tick when ANY of these holds, and after the 250 ms attack-finish time (6 ticks; attack progress frozen, zeroed on the loss + 5) otherwise: (a) its card sets OverrideAttackFinishTime (15.535.29 characters data: Valkyrie, Bowler, Princess, ElectroWizard; value.attack_finish_override_units); (b) its attack progress is 0 on the loss tick; (c) its card has a Projectile AND the victim was doomed: on its last live tick the damage of HOMING projectiles already flying at it, from any source, level-scaled, was at least its hitpoints. It agrees with 1,138 of the 1,152 events observed at 1 or 6 ticks (315 of 323 that are not crown towers; 7 of the 8 other misses are projectile units the event reader could not name). A reading that applies (c) to every attacker agrees with 280 of 323: a direct hitter whose victim was doomed by a pending tower arrow waits 6 in 35 of 35. Lethality matters: projectile troops with pending damage below the victim's hitpoints wait 6 in 5 of 5, and at or above take 1 in 65 of 66. Only homing projectiles count: a non-homing Bomber bomb, Princess arrow or Fisherman hook never shows in its target's pending damage, and a Bomber takes 1 on all 7 events where other units' homing shots doomed its victim. Exceptions: one Hunter (non-homing pellets) with a doomed victim waited 6; 6 of 829 crown-tower events.

DASH_ATTACK.meaning: client_dash: a unit whose row has a dash block, walking after a target, starts a dash on the first tick whose start-of-tick centre distance is at most DashMaxRange + the target's radius, unless the target's edge gap was under DashMinRange when first seen (then it walks in). It stands DashCooldown, holding one goal cell: the 500-cell of the point (own radius + target radius) short of the target's centre. It then moves at JumpSpeed a tick toward that cell's centre: a Bandit in two half-steps, stopping after the first whose edge gap to the target (start of tick) is within its Range, and dealing DashDamage on that tick; a Mega Knight to the cell, dealing DashDamage on the onset + DashConstantTime/50. Tower arrows landing on the moving Bandit, through its arrival tick, are discarded (DashImmuneToDamageTime). Its ordinary attack cycle follows. none: today's engine, where the dash block is not read.
DASH_ATTACK.open: DashRadius, DashPushBack and DashLandingTime (the Mega Knight's landing push is measured only on the pushback-1000 ladder). A target that moves during the stand. The immunity's first two onset ticks and the arrival + 1, and damage other than tower arrows. A Mega Knight jump near DashMinRange.
DASH_ATTACK.promotion_rules: The test file passes. The flip moves every scene with a Bandit or a Mega Knight chasing a target, so replay reports can move; register the prediction before the flip.
DASH_ATTACK.engine: a dash state beside the walk (the stand with a one-cell goal, the half-steps with the Range test for the Bandit, the timed landing for the Mega Knight, the damage immunity), entered from the attack decision when the trigger holds; the card's dash block is already in cards.json

DASH_FIRST_SIGHT_TRIGGER.provenance: MEASURED on client 15.535.29, 25 dashes, and the 16.402 corpus, 3 dashes. For each dash: F, the first tick the dasher's target pointer names the unit it dashes at; the start-of-tick centre distance on F; the onset, its first move over 150. 12 dashers first saw their target inside DashMaxRange + the target's radius and not nearer than DashMinRange edge to edge. The 2 Mega Knights moved on F + 17: the Mega Knight's single-card scenario (4,863.6 from a walking Knight) and a jump at a Giant standing at its tower (5,231.4). The 10 Bandits moved on F + 16: the Bandit's single-card scenario (4,863.6), five Bandits walking to a tower when a Giant was played in front of them (5,274.4 to 5,634.1, F the Giant's first frame) and four played 5,314.6 to 6,622.3 from a Giant at its tower. 16 dashers walked into the trigger distance; each moved on T + 17 (5 Mega Knights) or T + 16 (11 Bandits), T the first tick whose start-of-tick distance is within it. So the count from the trigger is the same in all 28, when the first-sight tick F is the trigger. A unit put down reads its first target on its first active frame + 1, so these are the first active frame + 18 and + 17 the combat.DASH_ATTACK entry cites. Today's engine triggers on F + 1 and moves on F + 18 and F + 17 (12 of 12, one tick late). It is exact on 14 of the 16 walking triggers; the other two follow an earlier divergence (the single-card Mega Knight's second jump, after its first landed 500 off, and a Bandit already 360 off in 20260920-081819-B). In the Mega Knight's single-card scenario the late tick moves the jump's goal cell: the Knight walks 59 in that tick, and the point (both radii) short of it crosses a 500-cell line, so the Mega Knight lands 500 from the client and walks its whole route from there. PROJECTILE_LAUNCH.meaning: start_radius_next_tick: the projectile starts ProjectileStartRadius from the attacker's centre toward the target on the fire tick, takes its first step the next tick, lands the tick its step reaches the target's centre. attacker_centre_same_tick: the earlier engine -- created at the attacker's centre and stepped in the fire tick's own Projectile phase, one tick early on a tower arrow.
PROJECTILE_LAUNCH.promotion_rules: To HIGH on troops: a troop projectile track (Musketeer / Archers) checked against its own ProjectileStartRadius on the launch frame, the way the tower arrows were.
PROJECTILE_LAUNCH.engine: read by crates/royalesim (state.rs Calib::from_json -> projectile_launch); combat.rs fire places the projectile (CardDef::projectile_start_radius from cards.json projectile_start_radius_milli) and marks it fresh, step_projectiles skips a fresh projectile's first phase. The old arm stays runnable as attacker_centre_same_tick.

Rows without the column (every loaded card; the princess towers) are unchanged. not_read: today's engine, which loads the column (cards.json projectile_y_offset_milli) and does not use it.

PROJECTILE_COLLISIONS.meaning: client_columns: a straight shot (combat.RANGE_PROJECTILE, combat.MULTIPLE_PROJECTILES) reads three columns of its row. CheckCollisions: the shot is gone on the tick it hits (every unit it reaches on that tick takes the hit), where a shot without it hits each enemy once and flies on. It passes a unit that the hits already dealt that tick have killed, so the pellets after a kill fly on: the shots are tested in creation order, each after the hits of those before it. ProjectileStartExtraRadius: the test on the shot's creation tick reaches ProjectileRadius plus this plus the enemy's radius; later ticks reach ProjectileRadius plus the enemy's radius. RandomDelay: the shot stands ceil(U / 50 ms) ticks after its creation tick before its first step, U drawn uniformly from 0..RandomDelay ms from the battle's Rng. not_read: every straight shot flies on after a hit, its creation-tick test reaches ProjectileRadius, and a fan pellet stands a uniform 2-5 ticks.

Whether the pellets that pass a kill hit a unit behind it (none stood in their path; the engine lets them hit whatever they reach next). Whether a pellet passes a unit killed earlier in the tick by something other than pellets (the engine counts every hit already written that tick, and the client's order of the tick's other hits is unmeasured). Whether the order is creation order or nearest offset first (the fan makes the two the same). Whether the creation-tick reach is ProjectileRadius + ProjectileStartExtraRadius (950) or another value in 805-1084 (ProjectileStartRadius 1000 also fits), and whether the Elite Archer's arrow (ProjectileStartExtraRadius 400) and the Firecracker's spark (650) use it: unmeasured. HIT_SPEED_BUFF.provenance: WHAT A HitSpeedMultiplier DOES TO THE ATTACK CYCLE. progress_scaled (shipped): the attack progress counter (combat.ATTACK_CYCLE) advances per tick by the buff composition of TICK_MS under the unit's HitSpeedMultiplier columns -- the same composition as the speed (movement.BUFF_SPEED_COMPOSITION) with the column swapped -- 65 under Rage, 35 under an Ice Wizard's slow; when the composed advance is <= 0 the progress step is skipped whole, which is how a -100 buff (every shipped stun and freeze) holds an attack mid-cycle. START_MANA.measured_2026_09_22_tick0_ramp:
Read off truth.elixir_raw of all 73 regenerated replay fixtures, every one of which now carries it (data/derived/replay; 10,000 raw is one elixir). Rates are counted only on CONSECUTIVE-tick pairs that ROSE, so a spend and a full bar cannot enter the count. 63 of the 73 fixtures begin at tick 0, giving 126 (side, tick-0) readings. ALL 126 read raw 60000, which is 6 elixir. None reads 5.

IS THAT THE START VALUE, OR THE START VALUE PLUS REGEN ALREADY CREDITED? Three things say it is the start value. (a) The tick-0 raw is EXACTLY 60000, which is exactly 6 elixir. 5 elixir plus one tick of the 1x rate would be 50178, and reaching 60000 from 50000 needs 56.18 ticks of that rate, which cannot be credited to a frame labelled tick 0. (b) Where a capture publishes frames at both tick 0 and tick 1, the step between them is 178, exactly ONE tick of the 1x rate, so tick 0 is the origin of the ramp and not a point part-way up it. (c) The 126 readings AGREEING is itself the argument, not just a sign of a stable reading: elixir rises every tick, so a first frame published at an arbitrary point after the battle began would catch a different value in every capture. 126 identical readings mean tick 0 is a common anchor. The ramps check out from that anchor: 20260918-122757.b2 publishes ticks 0, 3, 4, 6, 7 as 60000, 60534, 60712, 61068, 61246, which is 60000 plus 178 per elapsed tick exactly.

WHY IT MATTERS more than a ledger line: at 5 the engine starts every battle a FULL ELIXIR short of the real game, and a card-play distribution is dominated by the elixir economy. FLIPPED 2026-09-22 17:3x in a window the training session opened for it, with the rebuild and the new engine digest announced. The old 5 is in history.

The one side where the king was hit before any tower fell (20260918-112751, side 0, first hit tick 2837) had no enemy in the king's range until tick 3247, so its first swing (3248) marks a target arriving, not the wake. KING_ACTIVATE_TIME_MS.measured_2026_09_22: Read from the recorded corpus (data/derived/replay). Per side: the first frame without a princess tower, with the frame before it one tick earlier, so the loss tick is exact; and the king tower's first attacking tick, behavior_state 2 with the fresh-cycle reading attack_progress_ms 550 (LoadTime 500 + 50) and the frame before it one tick earlier, or 600 after a two-tick gap, which puts the first tick one earlier. A side counts only when an enemy stood in the king's range on every frame of the six ticks before that swing, so the king had a target waiting. 28 distinct battle-sides qualify: 27 give exactly 71 ticks from the loss to the first swing, one gives 72 (20260920-072148-A, where the other seat's capture still shows the tower on that frame). In the engine the delay starts on the tick the tower is lost and the king targets and swings on the tick it wakes, so the gap is KING_ACTIVATE_TIME_MS / 50 rounded up: 3300 gives 66 (0 of 28), and 71 needs 3501-3550. While it waits, the king's attack_progress_ms, attack_load_timer_ms and event_timer_ms read 0 (60 of 67 side-captures; the other 7 show only event_timer_ms counting), so no timer on the king counts the delay. THE STEP FROM THERE TO 'so none of the 71 ticks is a load' DOES NOT FOLLOW, and the committer of this measurement disagreed with it in the commit body rather than here, which is the defect this sentence now fixes: timers reading 0 during the wait shows the delay is not an attack timer, and says nothing about whether a LoadTime is paid between waking and the first swing. That 3300 itself falls is the safe part and is recorded in confidence: it predicts 66 ticks if no load sits inside the measured window and 76 if one does, and the corpus has 0 sides at either (39 at 71, 3 at 72). What the value should BE depends on the confound: 3501-3550 if the king's first swing carries no LoadTime, and about 3001-3050 if it does, because the king ships LoadTime 500 with load_first_hit false. The entry argues the first reading below from the king's own timers reading 0 while it waits, and that is evidence the DELAY is not counted by an attack timer, not evidence that no load is paid between waking and the first swing. Settle that before flipping. Left at 3300 meanwhile, and a value change would ride one announced rebuild with a parity score beside it.

TICK_ORDER.measured_2026_09_26: MEASURED on client 15.535.29, the per-frame records of the 15.535.29 scenario runs (775 runs read): when a walking unit's target dies to a melee strike, the frame on which the walker holds its next target follows the creation order of the striker. A striker is a unit attacking the target, with no projectile, whose attack load timer restarted on the frame the target was gone. (1) Every striker created before the walker: the walker held its next target on that same frame, 11 of 11 (Barbarians, Elixir Golems, Bats, a Knight, Night Witch units; one more walker waited 6 frames, the post-kill wait). (2) Every striker created after the walker: one frame later, 9 of 9 (Skeleton Army, Bats, Night Witch units; one more waited 6). (3) No melee striker (a shot killed the target): one frame later, 22 of 23 (one waited 6). So each unit takes its target decision and its strike in its own turn, in creation order, and a melee strike's damage lands at once: a unit later in the order sees the kill in the same tick, one earlier in the order sees it on the next.
TICK_ORDER.meaning_client_sequential_strike: client_sequential_strike: as client16402, except that the Target and Attack phases run as ONE pass over the units in creation order (the order of the sequential move pass): each unit decides its target, then advances its attack; a direct strike's damage is applied at once, so the struck unit's hp and death are what every later unit in the pass reads. Projectiles, splash from projectiles and spells keep landing where they do now. Under client16402 every unit decides its target before any strike and strikes land at Resolve, so a walker sees a melee kill one tick late whatever the order.
TICK_ORDER.measured_16402_2026_09_26: MEASURED on the 16.402 corpus (the 73 replay fixtures of client 16.402; a battle recorded from both sides counts twice), with the events of measured_2026_09_26. The rule there holds on client 15.535.29 only: client 16.402 does what client16402 does, and client_sequential_strike stays a candidate. (1) A walker whose target fell to strikers all created before it held its next target one frame after the kill in 104 of 112 events, two frames after in 4, and after the 6-frame post-kill wait in 2. The other 2 are one event read on the kill frame from one side of a battle; the other side of that battle reads it one frame later. The rule of client_sequential_strike puts all 112 on the kill frame. (2) An attacking unit whose target fell to strikers all created before it walked or held a new target 6 frames after the kill in 71 of 81 events, 1 frame after in 3 (a Valkyrie, a Musketeer and a Spear Goblin, which do not wait), 4 or 5 frames after in 3, not within 12 frames in 4, and on the kill frame in none. client_sequential_strike moves a waiting unit to the fifth frame and one that does not wait to the kill frame. Client 15.535.29 agrees with client16402 here: 4 of 4 on the sixth frame (Barbarians 2, Angry Barbarians 1, Skeleton Army 1). (3) A unit struck down on a frame on which it was due to strike still strikes on that frame: its own target lost hp on the kill frame in 3 of 3 events on the 16.402 corpus (two battles, one of them recorded from both sides) and 2 of 2 on client 15.535.29, and on client 15.535.29 an Elite Archer struck down by a Knight still launched its arrow on that frame (the Knight lost 135 on the next). client_sequential_strike drops the victim's strike or launch when its killer comes first in the pass. (2) and (3) were not part of measured_2026_09_26, and the arm's readings of them are wrong on both clients.
TICK_ORDER.provenance: MEASURED on the 31 live 16.402 captures. THE ORDER: every unit's attack update runs before any unit moves; the move updates then run one unit after another in CREATION order -- unit i sees units j < i already moved and units j > i at their start-of-tick positions, against a spatial index and an occlusion grid built from the start-of-tick positions; the per-unit character update (the state machine and the DEPLOY COUNTDOWN) runs AFTER the move pass. THE EVIDENCE: (1) the creation order -- the units of every capture keep the order they were created in on 16151 consecutive frame pairs with no reorder, and the sequential pass in that order reproduces 98 % of the contact ticks against 46 % with previous-tick neighbours (collision.CONTACT_LAW); (2) a 1 -> 2 (walking -> attacking) transition takes effect BEFORE the move pass -- on 819 transition ticks the unit never took its walking step (621 stood still, 198 were only pushed), where an order with the move before the attack predicts a step on every one; (3) a 2 -> 1 unit walked in the SAME tick (412 / 413); (4) a 4 -> 1 (deploy finished) transition takes effect AFTER the move pass -- 398 / 445 stood still, the rest were pushed -- where a countdown run before the move predicts a full first step on that tick. movement.DEPLOY_TIMING's 'the movement state flips one tick early (4 -> 1 before the first displacement)' is the same fact seen in the offline 15.535 corpus.
TICK_ORDER.meaning: client16402: lib.rs TICK_PHASES = Upkeep, Status, Spawn, Target, Attack, Path, Move, Projectile, Resolve, Reap, Judge -- Target and Attack before Path and Move, the deploy countdown at the end of Move, the sequential move pass (state.rs phase_path16402) ordered by entity.rs `creation_seq` (a monotonic per-battle counter: the six towers take 0..5 in the order Blue king / own-left / own-right, Red king / own-left / own-right, then every spawn in queue order, so ascending creation_seq is the order the captures show). legacy_move_before_attack: lib.rs LEGACY_TICK_PHASES -- Path, Move, Attack with the deploy countdown in Upkeep, the order this engine ran before the measurement ('a unit that moves into range attacks the same tick'), under which a unit entering range winds up one tick early and a unit whose deploy ends walks on that tick; kept runnable as the refuted arm. Under both, the same three rules follow for the frame-planned path arms (phase_path_2026 / phase_path skip a Windup unit and a deploying one).
TICK_ORDER.promotion_rules: SETTLED on 819 / 413 / 445 transition ticks and 16151 frame pairs. Re-open only against a new client build; one designed capture re-verifies it: a single Knight walking into a tower's range with a frame on the transition tick (no step, state 2), and a deployed unit's first two frames after its countdown ends (state 1 with no displacement, then the full first step).
TICK_ORDER.engine: read by crates/royalesim (state.rs Calib::from_json, calib_enum TickOrder); a candidate without an engine implementation is refused at load, never silently substituted. state.rs BattleState::tick picks TICK_PHASES or LEGACY_TICK_PHASES by it; phase_upkeep / phase_move run the deploy countdown (deploy_countdown) under the arm that owns it; tests/tick_order.rs pins the three transition rules and the creation-order visibility; the regression plant `phase_order` forces the legacy order and turns tests/tick_order.rs and every phase-traced battle red. Snapshot format 12 carries creation_seq.
TICK_ORDER.not_modelled: (1) A unit in Windup is skipped by the whole move pass (no separation push either), where the corpus's attacking unit is pushed without walking (the 198 'only pushed' transition ticks) -- the engine's Cooldown / in-range unit is pushed, its Windup unit is not. (2) The start-of-tick spatial index is `Index` in move16402.rs; the occlusion rebuild is Grid16402::refresh. (3) Projectile arrivals and spells land after the move pass here (Phase::Projectile); where they fall within the game's tick is unmeasured. (4) A unit mid-windup whose live target moves out of range keeps winding up (combat.rs attack_step tests no range in Windup; status.PRESERVE_TARGET_IF_HIT_STARTED) and does not walk that tick, where the 412 / 413 measurement counts every 2 -> 1 transition; that case is the attack rule's, not the order's.

MANA_REGEN_MS_OVERTIME.confidence: REFUTED for late overtime: the corpus shows a third rate, 537 raw per tick, that this value does not model, and the engine has no third rate to put it in. It is not refuted for the rest of overtime, where the 2x rate it duplicates is what runs (measured_2026_09_22).
MANA_REGEN_MS_OVERTIME.engine_contract: NOT READ BY THE ENGINE. Calib carries mana_regen_ms_1x and mana_regen_ms_2x and nothing else, and state.rs phase_upkeep picks between exactly those two with `self.overtime || regular - elapsed <= mana_speed_up_remaining_s`. So the engine runs the 2x rate THROUGH overtime and triple elixir is not modelled. This key's number is inert: changing it changes no behaviour, which is why it was NOT flipped alongside START_MANA. Closing the gap is a code change, a third rate plus the tick it starts at, and the boundary is the part the corpus has not settled.
MANA_REGEN_MS_OVERTIME.proposed_value_note: about 9300 ms once the engine has a third rate to put it in; the measurement constrains it to 9294..9311 ms, because the engine truncates 100000 * TICK_MS / value and every value in that range yields the observed 537 raw per tick
MANA_REGEN_MS_OVERTIME.measured_2026_09_22_rate_bands:
Read off truth.elixir_raw of all 73 regenerated replay fixtures, every one of which now carries it (data/derived/replay; 10,000 raw is one elixir). Rates are counted only on CONSECUTIVE-tick pairs that ROSE, so a spend and a full bar cannot enter the count. THREE distinct rates appear, in three SEPARATED tick bands: 178 raw per tick over ticks 1..2539 (118,394 pairs), 357 over 2401..3680 (18,880), and 537 over 4856..4947 (403). The 537 band is separated from the 357 band by a gap of 1,176 ticks, so it is a distinct phase and not noise. 537 per tick is about 9,300 ms for the bar, half again as fast as the 14000 this key ships, which is the same value as MANA_REGEN_MS_2X. WHAT IS NOT SETTLED: the tick at which the triple phase begins. The corpus never observes a rise between ticks 3681 and 4855, because every bar in that window is full, so the boundary is bracketed and not measured.

A SECOND, INDEPENDENT SOURCE AGREES ON THE RATE. The scripted-battery tooling that drives the recordings carries "triple elixir, measured 537 raw/tick" from its own observation, arrived at without the replay fixtures. Two instruments that share no code agreeing on 537 is what makes this a rate rather than an artefact of one decoder. The same note places the overtime transition at about tick 3690, which is consistent with the corpus's last 357 rise at tick 3680 and brackets the start of the triple phase far tighter than the corpus alone: between 3680 and 4856 from the fixtures, at about 3690 from the tooling. NOT VERIFIED: whether that 3690 is itself measured or is the script's own parameter. Establish which before treating it as the boundary, and do not flip the value on this alone.
MANA_REGEN_MS_OVERTIME.note: 14000 is the 2x rate: in 2018, overtime was DOUBLE elixir. The live game's overtime is not double from tick 4855 on (measured_2026_09_22). Added 2026-09-13.
MANA_REGEN_MS_OVERTIME.measured_2026_09_22: Read off the replay corpus of client 16.402 (data/derived/replay, truth.elixir_raw, 10000 = one elixir). Three battles go past tick 3600 into overtime (20260920-002736, -081051 and -083112, each recorded from both seats; they end at ticks 5220, 5460 and 5732 to 5779). Below the cap, every consecutive-tick pair from tick 4856 to tick 4947 rises by exactly 537: 255 distinct pairs (403 counting both seats), and the elixir drops there are a whole number of elixir x 10000 less 537. 14000 predicts 357: 0 of the 255. A third of MANA_REGEN_MS_1X (9333 ms) predicts 535: 0 of the 255. Every value from 9,294 to 9,310 ms gives 537 (floor(100000 x 50 / T)); 9300 is the round value in that window, and the corpus cannot choose within it. NOT ESTABLISHED: the step over the first part of overtime. In all three battles every side sits at the cap with no card played from well before tick 3600 until tick 4855 to 4877, so no pair from 3601 to 4855 shows a step, and when in overtime the 537 begins (and whether overtime opens at the 2x step) is not in the corpus. The 177 distinct +357 pairs after tick 3600 belong to two battles whose combat stops at tick 3600 (20260920-081819 and -010218: no hit lands after it and regeneration carries on through the closing frames), not to overtime. Recorded by the client instrument that records ground-truth traces from the real game.
MANA_REGEN_MS_OVERTIME.engine: Not read by the engine: state.rs phase_upkeep uses the 2x step (MANA_REGEN_MS_2X) for the whole of overtime. Taking the proposal needs a third step there and a rule for when it starts, and the start is the part the corpus does not show.

MANA_SPEED_UP_WHEN_REMAINING_SECONDS.measured_2026_09_22: CONSISTENT, with one caveat. The first 357-per-tick rise anywhere in the corpus is at tick 2401, which is 120.05 s into a 180 s regular period, so 60 s remaining. But 178-per-tick rises continue to tick 2539 in some captures, so the boundary is not the same tick number in every capture and this figure rests on the EARLIEST observed switch rather than on a boundary the corpus pins per battle. A capture whose own match clock is offset from its tick numbering would explain it and has not been checked.
MANA_SPEED_UP_WHEN_REMAINING_SECONDS.provenance: MEASURED on client 16.402 from the replay corpus (data/derived/replay, truth.elixir_raw). The regeneration step doubles between tick 2400 and tick 2401. Below the cap, the rising pairs ending at ticks 2381..2400 are 278 x 178 and 0 x 357, and those ending at ticks 2401..2420 are 223 x 357 and 0 x 178 (distinct pairs over the 11 battles with a rising pair in either window, 10 of them in both); the pair ending at 2400 is 178 on 13 sides and the pair ending at 2401 is 357 on 12. Two more pairs ending at 2400 read 535 = 178 + 357 and are followed by a 0: one frame a tick late. In the engine (state.rs phase_upkeep) the step that produces tick t + 1 is doubled when REGULAR_TIME_S x 1000 - 50 t <= this value x 1000, so 60 with REGULAR_TIME_S = 180 doubles exactly from the pair ending at 2401. 61 would double the 278 pairs ending at 2381..2400 (0 are doubled); 59 would leave the 223 pairs ending at 2401..2420 single (0 are). What the corpus measures is the tick, 2400 = 120.00 s of battle time; it reads as 60 s remaining only with REGULAR_TIME_S = 180, so a change to that key moves this one with it. Recorded by the client instrument that records ground-truth traces from the real game.

GENERATOR.provenance: Supercell's own PRNG has never been recovered publicly. A real replay is a function of a single rndSeed int, so the generator is a REQUIRED component of reproducing a real match -- and an unavailable one.
GENERATOR.consequence: We cannot replay a real recorded match. We CAN guarantee bit-identical reproducibility within our own build, which is a different and entirely attainable property, and the one every test depends on.
GENERATOR.engine_contract: The RNG is owned by battle state and its bit-state is part of the serialized state. A replay is seed + action log + periodic state hash. The old engine had 23 module-global `random` call sites and zero occurrences of `seed`, so nothing it produced was reproducible at all.

$comment: Stated explicitly so nobody re-litigates it or quietly aims higher and stalls.
BIT-EXACT replication of Clash Royale is NOT achievable from public evidence,
and no further archaeology makes it achievable: unknown tick rate, unknown
speed divisor, unknown internal fixed-point scale and rounding, unrecovered
PRNG, unknown intra-tick ordering, and a pathfinder Supercell rewrote in 2025
and never documented -- against a data corpus that stops in 2023 and an arena
map that stopped shipping entirely.
THE TARGET IS: behavioural fidelity sufficient that strategies transfer, plus
bit-identical determinism WITHIN this build. That is RocketSim's own posture
and it was enough to train superhuman Rocket League agents.
The engine's job is to make every disputed constant cheap to change and cheap
to test, so that each measurement promotes a number instead of triggering a
rewrite.
Spell mechanics that NO shipped column settles (docs/spell-spec.md, PARTIALLY VERIFIED).
Card STATS for spells (damage, radius, pushback distance, crown percent, waves, roll
range, stun time, spawn count) are NOT here: they are card data, read from
data/derived/cards.json. WHICH VINTAGE THAT FILE HOLDS IS NOT FIXED: it is a
generated name, gitignored, and tools/extract_cards.py writes whichever vintage it
was asked for to it -- the published README's --vintage 2018 gives a clone the 2018
table under that name, a run with no flag gives the 15.535 one. Only the file's own
provenance.vintage says which is on disk, and the engine reads it at RUNTIME through
CardDb::load_repo rather than compiling it in, so the stale-build guard that covers
calibration.json, arena.json, globals.csv and rarities.csv does not cover the card
table. Anything comparing two engine results has to carry the table's hash: the
replay harness does (each report's cards_json_fixture / cards_json_engine, and
data/derived/replay/card_census.json), and that is what makes two runs comparable.
The live-2026 values the spec quotes (Fireball pushback 1000, Arrows 3 x 48 at
r 3500, Log range 10100, ...) are evidence for a data-vintage decision, not engine
inputs.

DISPLACEMENT_LAW.confidence: HIGH on the ladder (one live push, eight steps, each step discriminating); the candidates below all predict a different track
DISPLACEMENT_LAW.provenance: MEASURED on the Giant of capture 20260918-122757.b1, ticks 1216..1223, and implemented in crates/royalesim/src/move16402.rs start_pushback / pushback_step. THE LAW: a landing push does not displace the unit, it ARMS a countdown. From (dx, dy) = unit - source and d = isqrt(dx^2 + dy^2) (d == 0 -> see ZERO_VECTOR_DIRECTION), L = min(Pushback, MAX_PUSHBACK_LENGTH); the target point is unit + (tdiv(dx x L, d), tdiv(dy x L, d)) and the speed is loaded with 25n, n the smallest with 25n(n+1)/2 >= L. Every tick after, the ladder REPLACES the walk: the separation scan runs while the speed is > 0 and so does the water ejection (WATER_RESOLUTION); speed -= 25 BEFORE the move; move_towards(target, speed) with the step min(speed, dist, 250) and no lower clamp (the facing untouched; the avoidance offset rotates the step but is neither scanned nor decayed); the ladder is active while speed >= 0, and the path is dropped the tick it turns negative (a replan follows). THE MEASUREMENT: the Giant's per-tick |step| reads 150, 125, 100, 75, 50, 25, 0, then 25 BACKWARD (v0 = 175, so L in (525, 700]); its nodes and facing are unchanged during the ladder, the path is cleared on the last tick and replanned on the next -- TRUE OF THAT PUSH AND NOT OF EVERY ONE, see open item (4); the engine reproduces all eight steps from the card data alone (tests/knockback16402.rs). fixed_distance predicts one displacement of Pushback on the hit tick and no track; linear_falloff_with_distance and half_distance_constant_speed predict no back-step and a different first step; none of the three produces the 25-per-tick ladder. Over the replay corpus the `pushback` family's unit-ticks within 250 native rose from 35.0 % to 70.4 % with the ladder (20392 unit-ticks). The unit therefore ends 25n(n-1)/2 - 25 along the line when the ladder covers L (the 2018 Fireball's 1800: v0 = 300, steps 250 250 225 ... 25 0 -25, total 1600), which is what tests/spells.rs and tests/knockback16402.rs derive. The engine arms the ladder in the Resolve of the hit tick and takes its first step in the next tick's Path phase; the eight steps are compared from the first ladder step. The launch recoil AttackPushBack (a characters.csv column) arms this same ladder under knockback.ATTACK_PUSHBACK = ladder_away_from_target; the replay does not exercise it.
DISPLACEMENT_LAW.promotion_rules: SETTLED on one live ladder. Re-open only against a new client build; a second live capture of a Fireball-class push (L = 1800: v0 300, the 250 cap on the first two steps) and of a push landing on a deploying unit extends the evidence.

The ladder runs inside state.rs phase_path16402 under pathfinding.PATH_SEARCH = client16402 (in the move pass, with the separation scan and the water ejection) and in state.rs step_pushback_ladders under the frame-planned arms (no contact, the position through settle).

No mass term.'~~ -- kept runnable (spell.rs settle, state.rs step_knock_slides, with DURATION_MS, STACKING = vector_sum and ZERO_VECTOR_DIRECTION = caster_forward): it is the seat-symmetric arm tests/common symmetric_config() runs the rotation-mirror gates under, and the regression plant knockback_instant_slide.
DISPLACEMENT_LAW.units: native millitiles; the ladder's speeds are native units per tick
DISPLACEMENT_LAW.open: (1) A stunned or frozen victim mid-ladder: whether the game carries it through the ladder is unmeasured -- no capture has a stunned unit mid-ladder; the engine carries it (phase_path16402 step 0). (2) The charge tail inside every pushback tick (charge.RESET_ON_KNOCKBACK, hypothesis: no capture has a charging unit mid-ladder); the tick a charged unit's hit lands on is charge.CHARGED_HIT_TIMING. (3) The tilemap's blocked bits (WATER_RESOLUTION not_modelled). (4) WHETHER THE LADDER HOLDS THE TARGET AND THE ROUTE. The engine keeps both while the ladder runs (target.rs, state.rs's replan skip) and tests/knockback16402.rs asserts it, on the strength of the one Giant above. This item previously said the corpus refuted the general form. It does not, and the correction is 2026-09-23. The cited evidence was the Golem of capture 20260920-071744-B going target 6 -> none at t2043 -> 4 at t2044 with its path node count 3 -> 14, mid-ladder. Read again by FRAME INDEX (the entity arrays run from t0 over the frames of `ticks`, not by tick number), the same transition happens on the same ticks to key 3, a side-0 PrincessTower with path_n 0 throughout, and to key 1, a KingTower: 6 6 6 -1 4 4 4 and 6 6 6 -1 -1 -1 -1. Neither can move, be pushed, or retarget mid-ladder. What actually happened is that key 6, the side-1 princess the Golem was walking at, has its LAST FRAME on that tick: it died, and every side-0 entity that named it fell back at once. The node count moved because the destination moved. The misreading has one cause, shared with the harness's target_match column: the truth's `target` is the client's own pointer, which names the DESTINATION crown tower whenever a unit is not fighting, while the engine's e.target is only ever an attack target -- default_tower is a local walk goal at four sites and is never stored. So the hold is UNREFUTED rather than refuted, which is not the same as confirmed: it still rests on the one Giant, and a capture of a unit pushed while it is walking at a tower that stays alive would settle it.

The sign is the engine's own choice, not a measurement: it takes the parity of team_seq, its sanctioned id-like quantity (entity.rs 'IDS ARE NOT SEMANTICS'), so the choice is deterministic and a unit and its rotated twin go the same absolute way -- not seat-symmetric, like the search.
