STACKING.provenance: first_wins_while_active: a push is refused outright while the victim's ladder is active. Two pushes on one unit in one tick therefore do not sum: the first one processed (the engine's spell order, which is cast order) lands and the second is refused, and so is any push landing during the n + 1 ticks the ladder runs. Not commutative -- tests/knockback.rs pins that the outcome equals the first-cast push alone under either order. Nothing recorded so far lands a second push on a unit whose ladder is running, so vector_sum (the fixed_distance arm's rule) is not yet separated from it by a capture.
STACKING.promotion_rules: To measured: a live capture of a Log landing on a unit mid-Fireball-ladder -- no second displacement under first_wins_while_active, a summed one under vector_sum.
STACKING.engine: read by crates/royalesim (state.rs Calib::from_json); a candidate without an engine implementation is refused at load, never silently substituted. PAIRED with DISPLACEMENT_LAW in from_json: client16402 implements first_wins_while_active only and fixed_distance vector_sum only; the other two pairings are refused, not approximated.
STACKING.superseded: ~~vector_sum, status guess: 'Two knockbacks landing on one unit in one tick are summed (buffered and commutative).'~~ -- the fixed_distance arm's rule, kept runnable with it.

WATER_RESOLUTION.confidence: MEDIUM under the ladder (the timing follows from the measured law; the search grid is unmeasured); LOW under fixed_distance (its own ejection is the old guess)
WATER_RESOLUTION.provenance: Under DISPLACEMENT_LAW = client16402: at the start of every ladder tick whose pre-decrement speed is > 0, a ground unit (neither flying nor hovering) pushed onto water does not stay there: it is on land again at the start of the next ladder tick. WHICH land point it takes is unmeasured -- the engine's own choice is under `engine`. So the river does not block a push (the old provenance: wiki The Log pushes a unit 'over the river back to the opponent's side'), a ground unit knocked onto water is put on land at the start of the NEXT ladder tick, and the back-step tick (speed 0 before its decrement) runs no check, so a unit can end the ladder on water and stays there (the walk never ejects). No push in the corpus ends on a river cell, so the candidate grid and its tie are unmeasured. Implementation: move16402.rs blocked_or_water / nearest_land, run by state.rs phase_path16402. Under the fixed_distance arm the old guess stands: a ground unit whose pushed centre touches water moves to the nearest passable ground point along the x or y axis (ties in its own frame), pushed out of footprints, else it stays put (spell.rs settle); the frame-planned path arms run the ladder through settle too, to keep their own no-water invariant.
WATER_RESOLUTION.promotion_rules: To measured: a live capture of a push ending on a river cell (Log a Knight on the bridge exit; Fireball a Knight 0.3 tiles from the bank, off-bridge) -- the landing point settles the candidate order and its first-minimum tie.
WATER_RESOLUTION.engine: read by crates/royalesim (state.rs Calib::from_json); a candidate without an engine implementation is refused at load, never silently substituted. Two implementations of the one candidate, one per DISPLACEMENT_LAW arm (above); the other candidates have none. WHERE THE ENGINE PUTS THE UNIT, its own choice and not an observation: the position clamped 250 inside the grid, taken as is when that cell is not water, else the first of the candidates (xc - 2250 + 500k, yc + 250 + 500j), j = -5..5, k = 0..10, inside the grid and off water, that minimises the octagonal length max(|dx|, |dy|) + (min(|dx|, |dy|) x 53 >> 7), rows outer from -5 and columns inner from the left, strict <. Nothing observed fixes this search; see promotion_rules.
WATER_RESOLUTION.not_modelled: Blocked-but-dry cells: arena.json marks LANE_LEFT 1, LANE_RIGHT 2, NO_DEPLOY 16 and WATER 32, and none of them stops a unit STANDING where it already is, so move16402.rs blocked_or_water is handed the arena's water bit and an EMPTY blocked mask (state.rs phase_path16402, py.rs; an earlier version counted NO_DEPLOY as blocked). Consequence: a unit standing on a dry cell is never teleported here; the nearest-land ejection would only have moved it 250 inside the grid.

ATTACK_RESET.provenance: MEASURED on capture 20260920-081819-B: (a) a Bomber BETWEEN HITS (state 2, attack progress 3500, load timer 0) hit by the Bandit at tick 2020 -- tick 2021: state 1, the counter 0, the ladder 200 / 175 / ... / 25 / 0 / -25 to tick 2030, then it walks back and re-enters state 2 at 2037 with a FRESH LoadTime (1600) countdown; (b) a Knight MID-WINDUP (state 2, 300 of its 700 load left) hit by the Mega Knight's landing at 3535 -- the load timer is back to 700 on the hit tick itself, state 1 from 3536 through the ladder (the timer counting down meanwhile, to 200), and on re-entering state 2 at 3546 the windup is a fresh 700 again; the target is the same unit before, during and after in both. So a landed push interrupts the attack in ANY phase, the victim is state 1 for the ladder and swings again only after a full LoadTime windup once it is back in range, and the target survives. The community reading the reset_windup_* candidates carry -- wiki Fireball 'a true stun that resets the attack animations', wiki The Log 'will reset their attack animation', with a cooldown untouched -- is refuted on the cooldown by (a). CORRECTED 2026-09-27 (the readings of (a) and (b), not the value): the Knight hit on 3535 itself (its progress reads 1200 = HitSpeed and the Mega Knight loses 202 on that tick), so the 700 there is its own hit's reset of the load timer, not the push's; it re-entered on 3546 at 600 = 700 + 100 - 200. (a)'s Bomber was pushed by the boulder of the Bowler it was attacking (it loses 289 hp on 2020; the Bandit stood about 14,500 away), not by the Bandit. Neither unit swung 'only after a full LoadTime windup', and (a)'s re-entry was no fresh LoadTime countdown: the Bomber re-entered on 2037 at progress 1650 and launched on 2040, 3 ticks later, against a LoadTime of 32 ticks, and the Knight hit 12 ticks after its re-entry, against 14. The re-entry takes the progress credit off a load timer the push left running. On 23 push landings where the two readings differ the load timer ran on through the ladder and none reset: knockback.PUSH_LOAD_TIMER carries that law and its population.
ATTACK_RESET.promotion_rules: Measured. A capture of a push on a RANGED unit between hits (a Fireball on a Musketeer) pins the cadence after the ladder, and the re-entry counter's own law (the Bomber's 1650, the Knight's 600 at re-entry) is unexplained. The re-entry counters (the Bomber's 1650, the Knight's 600) are the progress credit taken off a load timer the push left running, knockback.PUSH_LOAD_TIMER's client_runs_on (a hypothesis until that key flips).
ATTACK_RESET.engine: read by crates/royalesim (state.rs Calib::from_json); a candidate without an engine implementation is refused at load, never silently substituted. reset_attack_keep_target: BattleState::apply_effects sets Windup OR Cooldown to Idle with the timer at 0 on the landing tick, the target kept; the hold through the ladder (phase_attack and target.rs through Entities::knocked) is the measured state 1; re-entering range after the ladder starts the ordinary LoadTime windup. The two reset_windup_* foils reset a Windup only and freeze a Cooldown through the ladder (resumed after it).
ATTACK_RESET.superseded: ~~reset_windup_keep_target, status community, 'cooldown is untouched'~~ -- refuted by the Bomber between hits (its swing counter zeroed, a fresh windup after the ladder); kept runnable as the foil. tests/spells.rs knockback_interrupts_a_unit_between_shots_and_the_old_arm_freezes_its_cooldown pins the two arms apart on a Musketeer between shots.

PUSH_LOAD_TIMER.meaning: client_runs_on: under knockback.ATTACK_RESET = reset_attack_keep_target, a landed push zeroes the swing counter and leaves the load timer as it was; the timer runs down through the ladder, and the re-entry credit takes off whatever is left (combat.ATTACK_CYCLE = progress_credit). reset_to_load_time: the old arm, shipped until the 2026-09-27 round-4 flip (scored on RoyaleSim fc4dbe4), which also sets the load timer to LoadTime on the landing tick, so a unit that re-enters within LoadTime of the push swings late.
PUSH_LOAD_TIMER.open: A push on the tick of the victim's own hit: the hit's reset and the push land on one tick, and both arms keep LoadTime there; the order of the Attack phase and the landing is not pinned by this key. A push on a charging unit, and on a unit whose attack is a special, are not measured.

The reports that move are among those where a recorded push lands on an attacker: the client 15.535.29 scenes named in the provenance, and the 16.402 seats of 20260918-121158, 20260918-122757.b1 and .b2, 20260920-071744, 20260920-081051-A and -B and 20260920-081819-A and -B (a Bowler's boulder pushes only under combat.RANGE_PROJECTILE = straight_to_range, so score its battles with that key too). A report that moves elsewhere must trace to a push the engine lands on its own positions.

DIRECTION_ROLLING.supersedes: travel_direction, status owner_ruling: 'A maintainer's direct observation of the live game: when The Log lands it never pushes a troop BACKWARD toward the player who cast it -- not even a troop standing just behind the tap -- it is always forward. Every ground troop the Log hits is therefore displaced by Pushback along the Log's direction of travel -- the caster's own forward axis -- including anything caught by its back edge on landing.' Superseded 2026-09-25 by the measurement in provenance, which corrects that observation: a troop standing behind the tap is pushed back toward the caster. Recorded rather than deleted, because the measurement that overturned it belongs beside it. The entry before it, radial_from_projectile_centre at status guess, was inferred from three strategy lines that need a sideways push (lane switching by deploying the Log on the side of the troop opposite; pushing troops closer to the inside of the Arena; pushing a corner Miner towards the King's Tower). The measurement now carries that value, on a troop behind the tap; whether it also explains those lines is not measured.
DIRECTION_ROLLING.measured_2026_09_22: Promotion rule (b) is now answered by the recorded corpus, and it answers it against travel_direction. Four Log pushes carry the knockback ladder exactly (per-tick step 150, 125, 100, 75, 50, 25 native, total 520), so they are unambiguous knockback rather than walking: a Knight 1.664 tiles off the roll axis pushed (450, 261); Giants 0.173, 0.275 and 0.722 tiles off the axis pushed (-73, 516), (-105, 510) and (-265, 447). travel_direction predicts (0, 520) for all four and is wrong by 519, 73, 105 and 275 native units. THE ARM THAT FITS is radial_from_contact_point: the push points away from a source on the caster's forward axis at the tap's x, one disc-sum BEHIND the victim, that is at along-axis coordinate victim - (log_radius + victim CollisionRadius). One free parameter, the Log's own radius, fits all four at 475 native with an RMS residual of 4.8 units out of 520 (per case 0.1, 2.3, 9.3 and 1.3). The Knight case, the one that separates the arms by 60 degrees, is reproduced to 2.3 units. THE OWNER'S SIGN RULING SURVIVES: because the source always sits behind the victim along the caster's forward axis, the forward component of every push is positive, so no victim is ever pushed back toward the caster. The old radial arm pushed victims backward because it used the projectile's instantaneous centre, which can lie ahead of a victim standing behind the tap; the contact point cannot. Reproduce: data/derived/replay/20260918-122757.b1 (cast tick 1199 at 14500, 6500), 20260918-121158 (tick 1274 at 3500, 7500) and 20260918-122757.b2 (tick 2359 at 3500, 5500); scan each victim for the 150/25 ladder and take the six-tick displacement. Recorded on client 16.402 by the client instrument that records ground-truth traces from the real game.
DIRECTION_ROLLING.measured_2026_09_25: Promotion rule (a) is answered, for radial_from_projectile_centre. A troop behind the tap is the case that separates the arms: travel_direction and radial_from_contact_point push it forward, radial_from_projectile_centre pushes it back. On client 15.535.29, the log-behind scenarios (both sides, mirrored to within 1 unit), Knights 500 and 1000 native behind the tap, on the roll axis and 800 off it, were hit for 268 on the first roll frame and carried back the full ladder, 150, 125, 100, 75, 50, 25 native per tick, net of their own walk; a Knight 1500 behind was not touched. The direction is the line from the Log's centre to the Knight, the tap snapped to its tile centre (placement.TAP_SNAP): 15, 26 and 35 degrees off straight back, against 15.4, 28.6 and 36.8 predicted. So the closing claim of measured_2026_09_22, that the sign ruling survives and no victim is ever pushed back toward the caster, does not hold: behind the tap the push is toward the caster, which the contact-point source cannot produce. On the 16.402 corpus the two radial arms score the same: 166 more unit-ticks within 250 native of the recording than travel_direction (towers excluded; 122757.b1 +151, 081819 A and B +7 and +8), and the both-alive and hp-exact counts unchanged.

All three candidates are implemented in spell.rs roll, under both displacement laws. Under DISPLACEMENT_LAW = client16402 the arm reaches the ladder through the SOURCE POINT the push is taken away from: radial_from_projectile_centre hands it the contact point, the Log's centre where its front face first meets the victim's near edge, clamped to the tick's sweep, so a victim behind that point goes back toward the caster and one exactly on it takes knockback.ZERO_VECTOR_DIRECTION; travel_direction hands it the point one native unit behind the victim on the roll axis, a push straight down the axis with no sideways component; radial_from_contact_point hands it the point on the roll axis one disc-sum behind the victim (knockback.ROLLING_CONTACT_RADIUS plus the victim's radius). travel_direction stays implemented because it is a listed candidate, and the regression plant rolling_push_travel_direction (tests/spells.rs) puts it back on the shipped arm.

ATTRACT_LAW.confidence: HIGH on the magnitude, the base (the victim's stored speed, stomp-corrected at load and through NO buff, measured on both clients -- see provenance, 2026-09-24), the composition and the duration; the law reproduces 32 of 32 clean unit-ticks to the native unit across both casts, and each of the four choices below was settled against a named alternative rather than assumed. LOW on everything in `open`: the evidence is TWO casts in ONE battle reaching three entities, one of which is a tower that cannot move.
ATTRACT_LAW.provenance: MEASURED on the two Tornado casts of capture 20260920-081819 (level 11, side 0): tick 1307 at (4500, 22500) and tick 1775 at (16500, 18500). THE LAW: every tick of the area effect's life each eligible victim takes an EXTRA step of length L = tdiv(S * AttractPercentage, 100) native straight at the centre, where S is the victim's own effective speed in native units per tick, taken from its position at the START of the tick, ADDED to whatever else moves it, with no arrival clamp, for exactly life_duration_ms / TICK_MS = 21 ticks. THE BASE IS THE EFFECTIVE SPEED: the Giant (key 17) is pulled 187 and tdiv(52 * 360, 100) = 187, where 52 is its stomp-corrected speed; its raw Speed column 45 gives 162, which puts the step at (33, 157) where (39, 182) is recorded on both ticks 1314 and 1315. Those two ticks are its stomp pause, identified independently by its 15-tick pause cadence outside the effect, and they also settle that the pull does NOT scale with the walk's speed for the tick, which is zero there. PER UNIT, NOT CONSTANT: the Knight (key 28) is pulled 216 = 60 * 360 / 100. ADDED, NOT SUBSTITUTED: subtracting the pull leaves a residual that is the victim's own walk, 51-52 on the Giant's 19 walking ticks and exactly (0,0) on its two paused ones. FROM THE TICK-START POSITION: over the Knight's 11 ticks within 254 native of the centre, 'pull from the pre-move position then walk' admits a legal walk on 11 of 11 while 'walk then pull from the moved position' admits none on 9 of them. OVERSHOOT, NOT A CLAMP: at 12 native out the Knight's recorded step is 169, landing 157 past the centre, and the whole 1784..1795 oscillation is reproduced by pull 216 plus a constant (-42,-42) walk, the two alternating step sizes being 216-60 and 216+60. TRUNCATION: 187.2 lands on 187 twice, so ceil is refuted; floor, trunc and round agree on this data. CENTRE: a +/-600 native grid search at 20-native steps leaves the tap point (16500, 18500) as the unique survivor. DURATION: first pulled tick to last is 1307..1327 and 1775..1795, both 21 moves, counted from positions alone so the estimated cast tick cannot shift it. THE SOURCE IS THE LIVE AREA EFFECT, NOT THE BUFF SLOT: BuffTime is 500 ms with CapBuffTimeToAreaEffectTime false, so the last application outlives the area by ten ticks, and the Giant's displacement is (0,0) on two of them. NOT GATED BY THE KNOCKBACK RULES: the Giant is IgnorePushback and was pulled, and the Knight was pulled through eight ticks of its own Bowler ladder -- subtracting the 216 leaves exactly the 200, 174, 149, 124, 99, 75, 49, 24 ladder knockback.DISPLACEMENT_LAW already records, which corroborates that law at the same time. --- 2026-09-24, THE BASE, RE-MEASURED ON CLIENT 15.535.29 WITH PAIRED CONTROLS (the same scenario with and without the Tornado; each scenario is deterministic, so the position difference on the first acting tick is the pull and no walk model is needed): a Knight is pulled about 216 = tdiv(60 * 360, 100) whether it is walking, attacking a tower (215.5), stunned by Zap (216.1), frozen (215.4), mid-knockback (215.2, the pull ADDED to the ladder step), under Rage (215.9 -- its own step 77 that frame, so the buffed arm predicts 280) or slowed by an Ice Wizard (215.7 -- step 41, buffed arm 147). THE PULL IGNORES EVERY SPEED BUFF. The Giant above never separated the two arms: effective_speed is the stored speed through buffs and the charge, the stored speed of a stomp card is ALREADY stomp-corrected at load (card.rs, S = floor(Speed * (Stop + Wait) / Stop), 52 for the Giant against its raw column 45), and an unbuffed, uncharged Giant gives both arms 52. An earlier reading here, and the engine's comments, took the base arm to mean the raw column 45 and counted the Giant against it; the code never read the column. Rage is the first victim whose two speeds differ, and it says base_speed. Also measured: the pull is not capped at 250 (a Hog Rider pulled 431.7 = tdiv(120 * 360, 100) - 0.3); flyers are pulled at full magnitude (Minions 323.9 against 324); own troops are never pulled.
ATTRACT_LAW.promotion_rules: SETTLED on the shipped arm for the magnitude, the base, the composition, the origin position, the overshoot and the duration; `base_speed` is refuted and kept runnable so the refutation can be re-run rather than believed. Re-open against a new client build. The items in `open` are NOT promotable from this capture and each names the observation that would settle it.
ATTRACT_LAW.engine: read by crates/royalesim (state.rs Calib::from_json -> attract_base); applied in state.rs phase_path16402 as a pre-pass over the start-of-tick positions, summed into the step by move16402::move_towards_extra and pushback_step_extra before the single grid_move. The column reaches the engine through status.rs BuffDef::attract_pct, which card.rs RawBuff::convert stopped refusing on 2026-09-23. A candidate without an engine implementation is refused at load, never silently substituted.
ATTRACT_LAW.units: percent of the victim's own speed; the resulting step is native millitiles per tick
ATTRACT_LAW.open: (1) WHERE IN THE MOVE PASS the attract sits relative to the avoidance rotation and the separation mean: no pair overlapped and no avoidance offset was non-zero in either window, so the corpus cannot order them. It is summed after the collision mean today. (2) ONE POSITION WRITE OR TWO: summing into the step and calling grid_move once is identical to a second independent grid_move EXCEPT where the water or grid-edge clamp fires, which is exactly what a Tornado cast at the river produces. One write ships. (3) FLOOR vs ROUND: only ceil is excluded; a card whose product lands above .5 would separate them and none does here. (4) A HELD victim -- stunned, frozen or zapped: none is inside either radius, and the adjacent facts point both ways, since the pull DOES apply while stomp-paused and while a knockback ladder runs. (5) A DEPLOYING victim, and whether the deploying-ground water clamp applies to an attract-driven step. (6) OWN-TROOP IMMUNITY: the one own-side unit inside a radius was attacking throughout, so OnlyEnemies and an attacking-unit immunity cannot be told apart here. OnlyEnemies is what the column says and what ships. (7) THE 250 STEP CAP: both measured pulls are under it. (8) d == 0 exactly, a victim standing on the centre: the Knight reached 12 native and never 0; normalize_to leaves the vector unchanged at n == 0, so the step is (0,0). (9) WHETHER A SPEED BUFF COMPOSES with the percentage -- a raged or slowed victim in a Tornado would say whether it multiplies the post-buff or pre-buff figure. (10) THE JUMP ARM: a jumping victim is not in the corpus and is not wired. (11) AIR: hits_air is true in the card data and no flying unit was in range in either cast, so the air arm is carried on the data and not on an observation.

STUN_CLEARS_TARGET.confidence: LOW for the shipped arm kept, today's engine: a held unit keeps its target through a stun or a freeze, so the target's death while it is held counts as its kill and the post-kill wait follows. HIGH for client_cleared on client 15.535.29 (23 of 24 Zap hits on a unit holding a live target read no target on the hit tick, and the frozen tower of sp-m4-towerhit-s0), with the carried windup a separate key's
STUN_CLEARS_TARGET.provenance: READ on client 15.535.29 (parity, round 9 item 30). sp-m4-towerhit-s0, its first divergence t357 (1,275 lost): an Ice Spirit freezes the princess tower on t320 (held t320..t341); the client's tower reads no target from t320 though its Fire Spirit lives to t332, holds its attack progress at 250, takes a Skeleton on t343 with 300 carried and fires at 800 on t353, the Skeleton dead on t357. The engine keeps the Fire Spirit through the freeze, counts its jump on t333 as a kill, serves the post-kill wait, and starts the Skeleton's windup from 0 (dead on t362). Over the 15.535.29 scenes, 23 of 24 Zap hits on a unit holding a live target read no target on the hit tick. status.RESUME_RETARGET_WINDUP = carry alone changes nothing in that scene (the kill path runs first); the two keys together give the client's ticks, so they are scored together.
STUN_CLEARS_TARGET.meaning: What a stun or a freeze landing on a unit does to its target on the landing tick: kept, the unit keeps it through the hold; client_cleared, the target is cleared (and the lock released) on that tick, so nothing it targeted dies as its kill while it is held and the resume rescan (status.STUN_RETARGET_ON_RESUME) takes a fresh one. What the rescan does with the paused windup is status.RESUME_RETARGET_WINDUP's.
STUN_CLEARS_TARGET.open: The one Zap hit of 24 that kept its target. Whether a Clone's hold clears it (the Clone keeps it, measured, and is not this key's). A stun on a unit whose target is a building.
STUN_CLEARS_TARGET.promotion_rules: The test file passes (crates/royalesim/tests/stun_clears_target.rs). Flip to client_cleared together with status.RESUME_RETARGET_WINDUP = carry when parity's scoring by override of the pair agrees with the reading above (sp-m4-towerhit-s0 and the Zap scenes) with nothing else moving.
STUN_CLEARS_TARGET.engine: state.rs land_stun (every hold that lands: apply_effects' stuns and full-stop buffs, reflect_melee_hit)

RESUME_RETARGET_WINDUP.provenance: When the resume rescan picks a DIFFERENT target, a paused windup is cancelled to Idle (the engine's existing change-of-target rule) rather than carried onto the new target.
RESUME_RETARGET_WINDUP.promotion_rules: A Musketeer locked mid-windup on a far Giant, a Skeleton dropped nearer, then Zap: new-target hit time minus stun end is a full LoadTime (cancel) or the remaining windup (carry).

BUFF_STACKING.confidence: MEDIUM (ours; correct for every combination the corpus ships). REFUTED for two Goblin Curses on one unit: measured on client 15.535.29, they pulse on their own clocks and at their own levels (35 and 39 a pulse, 3 runs), where one slot per row keeps one clock and the latest level.
BUFF_STACKING.provenance: character_buffs ships EnableStacking on Poison, Earthquake, RageModeRage and the Heal Spirit's buff, so the game can carry a row more than once. WHAT IT CANNOT MEAN is one copy per APPLICATION: a Poison area re-applies its 1000 ms buff every HitSpeed = 250 ms for a LifeDuration of 8000, so 32 copies would stack on a unit that stood in one cloud and the card would deal 32 times its published damage. Stacking therefore needs the buff's SOURCE (the area effect object, the projectile) as part of its identity, and the engine does not carry that: `one_slot_per_buff_row` keys a slot on the buff ROW alone, so a second cloud refreshes the first rather than adding to it. A NAMED GAP -- two Poisons on one unit deal one Poison's damage. Measured against this: with per-application slots a Knight standing in one Poison took 17 damage ticks over the cloud's 8 s instead of 8 (tests/status.rs).
BUFF_STACKING.promotion_rules: Two Poisons over one Knight, cast a second apart: the hp curve doubles its slope while both clouds stand under per_source_slot and does not under one_slot_per_buff_row.
BUFF_STACKING.engine: read by crates/royalesim (state.rs Calib::from_json, the only() rule); state.rs `apply_effects` keys a slot on the buff row. tests/status.rs pins the Poison's pulse count.

FULL_STOP_BUFF_IS_STUN.confidence: HIGH for the one split row: the countered attacker's clock ran at 2 a tick on 5 of 5 counters. The arms agree on every other row in both card tables.
FULL_STOP_BUFF_IS_STUN.provenance: The Ronin's counter stun row (ronin_reflect_stun_buff: SpeedMultiplier -100, HitSpeedMultiplier -95, SpawnSpeedMultiplier -100) separates the arms. Measured on client 15.535.29 in the Ronin scenarios (level 11): a countered Knight's attack progress ran at 2 a tick (5 % of 50) for the 10 ticks the 500 ms buff lasts, then at 50 again (2 of 2 runs); countered Skeletons ran at 2 a tick until the reflect killed them (3 of 3). The Knight's load timer kept falling 50 a tick, it kept its target and it did not step; a countered Skeleton kept drifting as it did before. Under stun_timer its attack would pause and it would be held. So only a row whose speed and hit speed both compose to 0 drives the hold timer; a row that stops the walk and leaves the clock running is a plain buff. Every other speed -100 row in both card tables (Freeze, ZapFreeze, Stun, ContinueFreeze, the Electro Giant's and the rest) is -100 in all three columns, so the arms agree on every other card.
FULL_STOP_BUFF_IS_STUN.meaning: stun_timer_speed_and_hit_speed_zero: a buff drives the engine's one hold timer, and holds the unit (entity.rs Entities::held), when its speed and its hit speed both compose to 0; a buff that stops only the walk is a plain buff, so the unit stays in the move pass and the collision set with a step of 0 and its attack clock runs at the composed hit speed. stun_timer: any buff whose speed composes to 0 drives the timer and holds the unit. buff_only: no buff drives the timer and every gate reads the composition itself (not implemented, refused at load).
FULL_STOP_BUFF_IS_STUN.open: Whether such a row pauses a spawner: under the shipped arm its hold timer stays 0, so spawner.STUN_PAUSES_SPAWNER does not read it (the Night Witch is a ground melee troop with a spawner). Not measured.
FULL_STOP_BUFF_IS_STUN.promotion_rules: Settled for the one split row. A countered Night Witch would settle the spawner question.
FULL_STOP_BUFF_IS_STUN.engine: read by crates/royalesim (state.rs Calib::from_json, land_buff; entity.rs Entities::held); buff_only is refused at load, never silently substituted. tests/parry.rs, tests/status.rs

AREA_BUFF_SOURCE_BINDING.meaning: client_source_bound: a buff hung by an area effect is bound to that area. HitTickFromSource: its damage pulses fall when the area's age crosses a multiple of the buff's HitFrequency (the area is 50 ms old on its landing tick), not a HitFrequency after the buff's first application. CapBuffTimeToAreaEffectTime: an application lasts min(BuffTime, the area's life left after the application's tick plus one HitSpeed of the area). ControlsBuff / ControlledByParent: the buff is removed when the area ends. not_read: today's engine, the buff lives BuffTime from its last application and pulses on its own clock.
AREA_BUFF_SOURCE_BINDING.open: The extractor carries HitTickFromSource (3 buffs) and CapBuffTimeToAreaEffectTime (21 area effects) into cards.json today; ControlsBuff and ControlledByParent are not extracted. Only the Earthquake and the Tornado are measured here, and the Rage's cap on client 16.402. The cap's HitSpeed term is measured at HitSpeed 100 (the Earthquake) and 300 (the Rage) only. Against the rule before the 2026-09-28 fix, where either cap binds: the other seven HitSpeed 300 areas (BarbarianRage, BarbarianRageEvoAeO, SuperRage_AOE, Event_Rage, AngryBarbarian_EV1_RageAEO, and the evolved Princess's slowing areas Princess_EV1_projectile_aeo and Princess_EV1_DeathFreeze) run up to four ticks longer, as the Rage does; Event_HolidayFeast_AEO (HitSpeed 500, an event unit's area) up to 400 ms longer; the six areas that apply every tick (HitSpeed 50: the four Event_Global areas, Event_Heal and SuperKnight_ShieldAEO) one tick shorter. No capture has measured one of them. With placement.TAP_SNAP on, the Tornado's pull in today's engine runs on L..L+20; client 15.535.29 pulls on L+1..L+21, one tick later, as a buff effect does after its application.
AREA_BUFF_SOURCE_BINDING.promotion_rules: The test file passes. Sweep: the Earthquake reaches 100 on within and the Tornado 99 or more on hp (with placement.TAP_SNAP for the Tornado's within).
AREA_BUFF_SOURCE_BINDING.engine: status.rs BuffSlot gains its source area (an id, or its age clock and its end); state.rs buff_pulse_pass reads the source's age for a HitTickFromSource buff; spell.rs area_bound caps the time (AreaClock carries the area's HitSpeed; plants area_cap_unread and area_cap_one_tick) and state.rs release_orphaned_buffs clears ControlledByParent slots when the area ends; the extractor carries ControlsBuff and ControlledByParent

TARGET_BUFF_ON_SPLASH.provenance: A projectile's TargetBuff column is named for the target, but the projectile's own splash hits everything inside its radius. `whole_splash`: every victim the impact damages takes the buff too, which is how the Snowball (Radius 2500, TargetBuff IceWizardSlowDown 3000 ms) is described. `primary_target_only` would slow one unit of a group -- for a troop's projectile the locked target, for a spell impact (which has a centre and no target) the victim nearest that centre. Not measured. BOTH PATHS dispatch on it: `combat.rs apply_attack_buff` for a troop's TargetBuff / BuffOnDamage and `spell.rs impact` for a spell's area buff (which had cited this key in a comment and never read it, so primary_target_only was a no-op for every spell carrying a buff until the two were joined).
TARGET_BUFF_ON_SPLASH.promotion_rules: Snowball three Skeletons standing together and time all three: all three slowed under whole_splash.

DAMAGE_REDUCTION.confidence: HIGH at DamageReduction 100, the one value a loaded card runs (the Super Knight's shield): four hits of two damages leave 1 each on client 15.535.29. HIGH at 15 and 60 on 16.402 (the hero Valkyrie's and the Evo Knight's rows, parity's round 9 reading): the hits truncate. LOW at 65 (the Monk's row): a datamined value, unmeasured. None of those three runs in the engine today: the Evo Knight and the hero Valkyrie are not in the card table, and the Monk's ability, which hangs its 65, is not run.
DAMAGE_REDUCTION.provenance: MEASURED at 100 on client 15.535.29, sweep-SuperKnight (seed 15): a level-11 Super Knight (2030 hp) against a level-11 Knight whose hit is 202. The Knight's hit that lands while the Super Knight's shield is up takes 1 (2030 -> 2029, on the tick of the Super Knight's own first hit), and the princess tower's three hits after the Super Knight walks on take 1 each (1423 -> 1422 -> 1421 -> 1420); the Knight's three hits while it attacks take the full 202, which is status.IDLE_BUFF's measurement. So a full reduction leaves 1 whatever the hit: not 0 (truncated_no_floor refuted) and not the full hit (not_read, refuted: the engine before this key took 202 every time, because the loader refused every buff row carrying the column but the Super Knight's shield loaded through a chain the loader did not walk). The division truncates, as every other percentage buff's does (status.rs compose; movement.BUFF_SPEED_RULE's raged Ice Golem, 52 -> 67): at a partial reduction that rounding was the engine's choice until the reading at 15 and 60 below. Several reductions on one unit: the strongest applies, as every multiplier column composes (status.rs compose); unmeasured. The datamined values (15.535.29 tables): SuperKnight_ShieldBuff_other 100 (events/event_super_knight.toml), Knight_Fortify_EV1 60 (character_buffs_evo.toml, the Evo Knight's BuffWhenNotAttacking), ShieldBoostMonk 65 (characters/monk.toml, the Monk's Deflect ability), ValkyrieHero_Damage_Reduction_Buff 15 (characters/hero_form/valkyrie_hero.toml), and DarkElixirBuff -100 (characters/darkelixir_bottle.toml, an event bottle; a damage increase, which the loader refuses). Scored by replay_parity on sweep-SuperKnight, every other key as shipped (the sim/r8dmgred build): hp exact with the towers left out is 55.7% under not_read and under truncated_no_floor (from t271 the Super Knight is 201 or 1 off the client) against 100.0% under truncated_floor_one and ceil_floor_one; within 250 is 100.0% and no unit is alive on one side only, under every arm. The 16.402 corpus holds no Super Knight, Evo Knight, Monk or hero Valkyrie: its 67 played fixtures score as before the key, every per-fixture report the same. READ at 15 and 60 on 16.402 (parity, round 9, the hero Valkyrie reading): the hero Valkyrie's 15 takes a 217 hit to 184, 202 to 171 and 109 to 92, and the Evo Knight's 60 takes 217 to 86 and 202 to 80. The division truncates; ceil_floor_one gives one more in every case.
DAMAGE_REDUCTION.meaning: What a hit does to a unit carrying a buff whose DamageReduction is r (1..=100): each hit, a > 0, becomes max(1, a x (100 - r) / 100), the division truncating, before the unit's shield takes the tick's sum. The unit's own drains and deaths (a building's lifetime drain and expiry, a delayed kamikaze's drain, a kamikaze's death on its fire) are not reduced.
DAMAGE_REDUCTION.open: The formula at 65 (a 202 hit: 70 here, 71 under ceil_floor_one); 15 and 60 are read (provenance). Whether two hits on one tick are reduced one by one (as here: 2 at 100) or summed first (1). Whether a reduction reaches a building's lifetime drain (not here). A negative DamageReduction (DarkElixirBuff, -100) is refused by the loader. The doomed-target count (targeting.DOOMED_TARGET_DROP) counts the full damage in flight at a reduced unit.
DAMAGE_REDUCTION.promotion_rules: The test file (crates/royalesim/tests/idle_buff.rs) passes. The partial reduction is read at 15 and 60 (provenance); 65 is settled by a known hit on the Monk under his ability: a 202 hit leaves 70 under truncated_floor_one and 71 under ceil_floor_one.
DAMAGE_REDUCTION.engine: combat.rs reduce_hit (the arithmetic), damage_reduction_of (the strongest of the unit's buff slots and of its own idle buff while that is on), resolve, land_at_once and killed_this_tick (each hit as Resolve lands it; a hit marked Hit::own lands whole). card.rs RawBuff::convert loads the column, 1..=100. Test: crates/royalesim/tests/idle_buff.rs.

LOW for when it is back after the unit stops attacking (the next hit came 122 ticks later, so the table's 50 ms is read, not measured), for the deploy (nothing hit the deploying unit), and for the area's reach (no ally stood near the Super Knight).
IDLE_BUFF.provenance: MEASURED on client 15.535.29, sweep-SuperKnight (seed 15): a level-11 Super Knight, placed on t218, and a level-11 Knight (202 a hit) enter their attack state together on t262 and both first hit on t271. The Knight's hit of t271 takes 1 (2030 -> 2029); its hits of t295, t319 and t343, while the Super Knight keeps attacking, take 202 each (-> 1423); the Super Knight walks on from t366, and the princess tower's hits of t488, t503 and t517 take 1 each. So the shield is on through the tick of the unit's own first hit (a shield off from the attack state's start, t262, would give that hit 202), off while the unit keeps attacking (a shield off only for BuffWhenNotAttackingTime after each hit, the Royal Ghost's reading of the same column, would give the three hits 24 ticks apart 1 each), and on again after it stops. The table's shape (events/event_super_knight.toml): BuffWhenNotAttacking SuperKnight_ShieldBuff, BuffWhenNotAttackingTime 50, whose OnStartAction is an ActionInterval of 50 ms spawning SuperKnight_ShieldAEO (LifeDuration 80, Radius 8000, HitSpeed 50, OnlyOwnTroops, FollowParent), whose buff SuperKnight_ShieldBuff_other is a DamageReduction of 100 capped to the area's time (status.DAMAGE_REDUCTION). The Evo Knight's BuffWhenNotAttacking, Knight_Fortify_EV1 (characters_evo.toml), is a DamageReduction of 60 on the unit itself: unmeasured, and the Evo Knight is not in the card table. Before this key the engine loaded the Super Knight and never read the column. Scored by replay_parity on sweep-SuperKnight, every other key as shipped (the sim/r8dmgred build): hp exact with the towers left out is 55.7% under not_read against 100.0% under off_after_hit_while_attacking, and the Super Knight's own row 17.6% against 100.0%; within 250 is 100.0% under both, and the first divergence is none.
IDLE_BUFF.meaning: A unit's BuffWhenNotAttacking that is not an invisibility: on from the unit's deploy end; the unit's own hit takes it off from the next tick; it stays off while the unit keeps attacking, and is on again BuffWhenNotAttackingTime (ceil to ticks) after the unit stops. While it is on, the unit takes its own buff's DamageReduction (the Evo Knight's shape), or puts its area down on its own point every Interval (the Super Knight's shape), and the area hangs its buff on what it reaches: own troops, and own buildings and crown towers under spells.OWN_SIDE_AREA_SCOPE = own_side_all_kinds.
IDLE_BUFF.open: When the buff is back after the unit stops attacking (the table's 50 ms, unmeasured). Whether a deploying unit carries it (not here). Whether a unit held right after its hit counts as attacking (here it keeps its attack phase, so it does). The area's reach: whether the Super Knight's shield covers allies, own buildings and own crown towers, as the table's OnlyOwnTroops and spells.OWN_SIDE_AREA_SCOPE read it; the table's area follows its unit (FollowParent), and here each one stands where it was put down, one tick behind. The Evo Knight's own shape, which no card of the table loads.
IDLE_BUFF.promotion_rules: The test file (crates/royalesim/tests/idle_buff.rs) passes. The return is settled by a hit landing within a few ticks of a Super Knight's attack ending; the reach by an own troop and an own princess tower within 8000 of an idle Super Knight taking known hits.
IDLE_BUFF.engine: state.rs idle_buff_pass (end of Resolve: the return, entity.rs idle_back; the area, cast through spell.rs cast from CardDef::idle_area); combat.rs idle_on and damage_reduction_of (the own shape). card.rs idle_buff_of loads the block that tools/extract_cards.py idle_buff_block writes, and refuses every other shape and a row whose BuffWhenNotAttacking the file carries no reading of. Test: crates/royalesim/tests/idle_buff.rs.

$comment: Buildings that hide when not attacking (buildings.csv HidesWhenNotAttacking / HideTimeMs /
UpTimeMs; Tesla true / 800 / 800 in both the 2018 data and 15.535). The timers are card data
(data/derived/cards.json, read by card.rs `HideDef`); everything the columns do not settle is a
key below. State machine: entity.rs `HideState`, stepped once per tick in state.rs `hide_pass`
(Target phase, before any entity decides its target). Community (unmeasured) rules the engine
takes without a key: the building lifetime keeps running in every state (wiki Tesla: 'its
lifetime still counts down while hidden'); a HIDDEN building ignores stun and knockback; a
hidden building neither targets nor attacks; a deploying Tesla is Up (targetable, damageable)
until its deploy time ends, when STARTS_HIDDEN applies. HideBeforeFirstHit (blank on every
2018 row) is not read.

STARTS_HIDDEN.provenance: Wiki Tesla: 'When deployed, it will be hidden underground' -- the building is under ground the moment its deploy time ends and rises only for a target. The false arm stands it up at deploy end with a full HideTimeMs countdown, so with no enemy near it goes under HideTimeMs later.
STARTS_HIDDEN.promotion_rules: Deploy a Tesla with an enemy Knight already adjacent: its first shot comes UpTimeMs after the deploy ends (true) or immediately at deploy end (false). A capture of the scene carries the Tesla's first-hit tick.
STARTS_HIDDEN.engine: state.rs Calib::hide_starts_hidden, applied by BattleState::hide_on_deployed (phase_upkeep on the tick deploy_ms reaches 0; spawn_now / setup spawns for a zero deploy time)

RISE_TRIGGER.provenance: Wiki Tesla: 'it will rise when an enemy comes within its range'. Tesla ships SightRange = Range = 5500, so the two arms agree on the shipped card and only a card whose sight exceeds its range could separate them. Both use the engine's own edge-to-edge range test and target eligibility (target.rs `enemy_in_wake_range` over `can_target`: an air unit does not wake a ground-only building, a hidden enemy building wakes nothing).
RISE_TRIGGER.promotion_rules: A hiding building whose SightRange exceeds its Range (none in the 2018 thin slice): an enemy standing between the two radii wakes it under enemy_in_sight_range only.
RISE_TRIGGER.engine: state.rs Calib::hide_rise_trigger, read by target.rs enemy_in_wake_range from state.rs hide_pass

TARGETABLE_WHILE_RISING.confidence: HIGH that enemies can target a Tesla from the tick it leaves the ground: client 15.535.29 and two independent 16.402 corpus cases agree, each locking on one tick after the Tesla surfaces. What the Tesla does while it surfaces is a different and larger defect; see open.
TARGETABLE_WHILE_RISING.provenance: MEASURED 2026-09-24. On client 15.535.29 (the tesla-vs-knight scenario) the Tesla surfaces on 240 and the Knight locks on at 241, taking the path goal (20,23). Under false the engine refuses the surfacing Tesla and the Knight keeps its princess route until 256, then turns to the same goal cell; under true it turns on 240. The Knight goes from 70.7% within 250 to 100.0%, the same across seeds and under both movement.ATTACKING_UNIT_MOVEMENT values, and no measure gets worse. On the 16.402 corpus, 3 of the 9 distinct Teslas surface, and two of them arbitrate the same way: a Tesla surfaces on 674 and a Giant locks on at 675; another on 1980 and a Minion locks on at 1981. Tested through a calibration override before the value moved. Re-checked the same evening by an independent derivation from the recordings, which found and corrected this entry's earlier claim that no corpus Tesla surfaces. The false arm is the older reading, that a Tesla is still under ground for targeting until its UpTimeMs rise has played.
TARGETABLE_WHILE_RISING.promotion_rules: A Giant walking past a hidden Tesla just inside its sight: the Giant turns toward the Tesla UpTimeMs after the Tesla starts rising (false) or on the same tick (true). On a capture, compare the Giant's target-change tick with the Tesla's rise tick.
TARGETABLE_WHILE_RISING.engine: state.rs Calib::hide_targetable_while_rising, read by target.rs hidden_from_targeting (inside can_target)
TARGETABLE_WHILE_RISING.open: THE RISING PHASE ITSELF IS THE REAL DEFECT, and it needs its own key. In both clients the surfacing state is already ATTACKING: on the surface tick the Tesla has its target and a running attack cycle, and its first hit lands 7 ticks later (15.535.29: 240 -> 247; corpus 674 -> 681 and 1980 -> 1987). The engine's Tesla has no target and no attack for its UpTimeMs rise (240-255), is up at 256 and first hits at 263, 16 ticks late under BOTH values of this key, so the Knight's hit points are exact on 67.9% of ticks under both. After its target dies the clients' Tesla goes back under in 6 ticks (15.535.29: 354 -> 360; corpus 1351 -> 1357, 2051 -> 2057); the engine's at 370. The law these fit: no pre-attack rise, the Tesla attacks the tick it surfaces, and hides 6 ticks after it loses its target. A red test for it has three numbers from the 15.535.29 scenario: first hit 247, Knight lock-on 241, hidden at 360. ONE TICK OF ORDERING remains under this key: the engine's Knight locks on 240, the clients' 241 (within 20: 54.6% -> 54.2%). It survives the fixtures' tick correction (the Knight is issued at 104 on both), so it is an ordering inside the tick and not a labelling artefact.

HIDDEN_IMMUNE_TO_DAMAGE.provenance: Wiki Tesla: 'while hidden it cannot be targeted or damaged by anything, including spells'. Enforced at ONE choke point, combat.rs `resolve` when the damage buffer is applied: every hit on a Hidden building is dropped whatever wrote it (attack, projectile, spell, rolling Log, death damage) -- except the building-lifetime expiry hit, which carries Hit.ignores_hide and always lands (a Tesla whose 40 s are up dies under ground). The false arm lets every hit land (targeting stays blocked).
HIDDEN_IMMUNE_TO_DAMAGE.promotion_rules: Fireball a Tesla that is under ground with nothing near it: its hp is unchanged when it next rises (true) or reduced by the Fireball's damage (false).
HIDDEN_IMMUNE_TO_DAMAGE.engine: state.rs Calib::hide_hidden_immune, read by combat.rs untouchable_now for resolve, straight_hits and land_at_once

HIDE_DELAY_MEANING.provenance: HideTimeMs is the time an Up building spends WITHOUT A LIVE TARGET before it goes under (the countdown resets to HideTimeMs on every Target phase it has one). The alternative reading counts from the building's LAST SHOT (state.rs phase_attack resets the countdown on fire), under which a target kept by the keep-target hysteresis but out of attack range does not hold it up. Tick alignment (both arms): the countdown is decremented in the Target phase; a building with no target from the Target phase of tick T on is Hidden in tick T + ceil(HideTimeMs / TICK_MS) - 1. LIMITS OF THE time_since_last_shot ARM: it is only viable on a hider whose HitSpeed <= HideTimeMs. The 2018 Tesla the engine loads ships HitSpeed 800 == HideTimeMs 800, which is why the arm hides on a STRICT countdown (< 0: with <= 0 it went under before every second shot); the 15.535 Tesla (characters/tesla.toml: HitSpeed 1100, LoadTime 700, HideTimeMs 800, UpTimeMs 800) would go under between every pair of shots with its target still in range, so on current data this arm cannot be the live rule as written -- a measurable restatement would be 'time since the last shot, not counting while a target is in attack range', which is not implemented. A THIRD READING the registry does not implement: HideTimeMs as the DURATION of the going-under transition (a Descending state) with the idle delay elsewhere -- the 15.535 Ghost row (characters/ghost.toml: BuffWhenNotAttackingTime = 2000 beside HideTimeMs = 400, no HidesWhenNotAttacking) pairs the same HideTimeMs column with a separate idle-delay column, so the schema does not rule it out; under it a Tesla whose target dies would start descending at once (untargetable immediately or only after the transition is the open question) instead of staying Up/targetable for 800 ms. Implementing it needs a fourth HideState.
HIDE_DELAY_MEANING.promotion_rules: Kill a Tesla's only target in the middle of its hit cycle: under idle_time_without_target it goes under HideTimeMs after the kill whatever the cycle phase; under time_since_last_shot HideTimeMs after its last shot, i.e. earlier by the time since that shot. For the unimplemented transition reading, a capture of a Tesla whose target dies: does it become untargetable (a Fireball / a locked attacker's retarget) immediately or only ~800 ms later?
HIDE_DELAY_MEANING.engine: state.rs Calib::hide_delay_meaning, read by state.rs hide_pass (and phase_attack for the reset under time_since_last_shot)

HIDDEN_OCCLUDES_PATH.provenance: A hidden Tesla's footprint still blocks deploys and still occludes the path grid (units walk around the spot; wiki: troops 'walk around a hidden Tesla'). The engine's path grid never looks at the hide state, so `true` is the only arm it runs; `false` needs the pathfinder to consult the hide state and is REFUSED at load.
HIDDEN_OCCLUDES_PATH.promotion_rules: A Knight walking a straight lane over a hidden Tesla's footprint with nothing to wake it (out of its sight is impossible on the footprint, so: a Tesla that cannot target the walker, e.g. an air unit over a ground-only hider -- none in the thin slice). Practically: the recorded path nodes of a Giant routed past a hidden enemy Tesla.
HIDDEN_OCCLUDES_PATH.engine: state.rs Calib::from_json refuses false (the only() rule for a boolean key); the value is not stored because nothing branches on it

$comment: PERIODIC SPAWNERS AND DEATH SPAWN (characters.csv / buildings.csv Spawn* and DeathSpawn*
columns; 2018: Tombstone, GoblinHut, BarbarianHut, FirespiritHut, Witch, DarkWitch spawn;
Tombstone, Golem, LavaHound, BattleRam, DarkWitch death-spawn). The columns are card data
(data/derived/cards.json `spawner` / `death_spawn`, read by card.rs `SpawnerDef` /
`DeathSpawnDef`, checked against the 15.535 csv_logic: same names, same meanings); every
rule they do not settle is a key below. Column semantics taken as read, not keyed:
SpawnNumber = units per wave; SpawnInterval = ms between the units of one wave (blank =
all at once); SpawnPauseTime = ms between waves; SpawnStartTime = ms to the first wave
(from activation or from placement: START_TIME_ORIGIN); SpawnLimit = most units from one
spawner alive at once (blank = unlimited); SpawnRadius = how far from the spawner the
units appear; a SpawnCharacter with SpawnNumber AND SpawnPauseTime both blank is no
periodic spawner (the SkeletonContainer row); DeathSpawnCount units at DeathSpawnRadius;
DeathSpawnDeployTime overrides the unit's DeployTime. COLUMNS THE DATA SHIPS THAT ARE NOT
READ: SpawnAngleShift (DarkWitch 90 -- the Bats on her flanks;
BattleRam 180 -- the Barbarians behind; 2018 and 15.535 alike), DeathSpawnPushback
(Golem, LavaHound, DarkWitch true), DeathSpawnMinRadius (SkeletonContainer 100), and
SpawnCharacterLevelIndex (2 on every hut, Witch 5, DarkWitch 8, BattleRam 2 -- not carried
into cards.json; every shipped value equals the owner's RelativeLevel and every spawned
unit is Common, so the owner's unified level is exact today). Engine: state.rs
`spawner_pass`, which runs in the MOVE phase right after the deploy countdown
(spawner.EMISSION_TIMING = move_phase_immediate, measured: a Tombstone's first Skeleton is
on the board on the Tombstone's own deploy-end tick) and creates its units in that same
tick; the Spawn phase, after the queue drains, pushing PendingSpawns that materialised in
the NEXT tick, is the spawn_phase_next_tick arm. Death spawn is still `phase_reap`, queued the old way (it
fires from a death, not from a timer). Timers run only past the deploy time; a building
lifetime is unaffected (see the lifetime section: a building's hp DRAINS over that time). A
wave's simultaneous units and every death spawn are laid out by the engine formation grid

A card that leaves the column blank emits FORWARD at the tangent (Tombstone, BarbarianHut: forward offset equals the centre distance). A card that sets it emits on a RING of that radius and not forward at all -- the Witch (SpawnRadius 2000) has a median centre distance of 1940 and a median FORWARD offset of 74 over 52 emissions, the Dark Witch (1500) 1490 and 120 over 44. Walking back one full step from the medians gives 1475 and 1484. The floor confirms it is structural rather than under-sampling: over the 196 emissions with no other same-side entity within 1500 native -- nothing to be pushed by -- the minimum ever recorded is 1515 and NOTHING falls below 1500, while all 21 sub-1500 readings in the full set have a neighbour within 1500 and are inward pushes. The emission point therefore lies in about [1475, 1544], centred on the tangent, and the instrument cannot narrow it. THE RING'S ANGLE IS NOT ONE LAW, and the two cards that set SpawnRadius disagree about which frame it is in. THE WITCH (SummonNumber 4, SpawnAngleShift blank), 13 waves over 4 instances: her four Skeletons sit on the axes 0 / 90 / 180 / 270 every time -- (4, 91, 178, 271), (2, 90, 177, 270), (1, 90, 178, 270), (2, 83, 178, 269) and so on -- while her own facing over those same waves spans 68 to 110 degrees and she is walking on three of every four. WHAT THE WITCH PINS IS ONLY THE FRAME MODULO 90: a 4-fold ring is invariant under a 90-degree rotation, so (0, 90, 180, 270) is equally predicted by an absolute base of 0, by the OWNER's forward (90 for side 0, 270 for side 1) with a base of 0, and by any base that is a multiple of 90. WHAT SHE DOES SETTLE, hard: the ring is NOT her per-tick facing. Her facing over those waves spans 68 to 110 degrees and none of those is a multiple of 90, so a facing ring would have put her Skeletons on 68 / 158 / 248 / 338 and on 110 / 200 / 290 / 20. It did not. FIRST_STEP_DYING_BODIES.open: WHERE AN EMISSION'S UPDATE RUNS. The client may run it at the spawner's own place in the creation-ordered move pass. Then it would meet a unit dying there only when that unit comes after the spawner (the dying Skeleton of 182539 does: it was created after its Tombstone), and the neighbours after the spawner at their start-of-tick positions. The engine runs it after the pass. The two events cannot separate these; an emission beside a unit that dies on its creation tick and was created before the spawner would. A death spawn beside a unit killed before the move pass (an Attack-phase hit), a dying unit that is not the parent but also releases units on that tick, and a dying building that is not the parent: none in the corpus.

$comment: A LIFETIME BUILDING'S HITPOINTS (characters.csv / buildings.csv LifeTime, carried into
data/derived/cards.json as `lifetime_ms` and read by card.rs `CardDef::lifetime_ms`).
The engine honours LifeTime on buildings, and on a troop that only a transformation reaches
(TROOP_LIFETIME below); the loader refuses a troop with one reached any other way (card.rs,
`units.{unit} is a troop with a LifeTime`). Engine: state.rs `lifetime_of`, `phase_status`.
The column is the building's whole life, not a timer that fires at the end: the game
bleeds the hitpoints away over it (HP_DECAY below), which is why a Tesla that nothing
ever touched is at half hp halfway through. status.STUN_PAUSES_BUILDING_LIFETIME says
whether a stun holds the clock; the hide state does not (a hidden Tesla drains: the live
corpus' Teslas lose hitpoints on frames they spend hidden).

HP_DECAY.confidence: HIGH: reproduced exactly on 92.2 % of 31113 live building frames, every residual a hit the building took; the exact-fraction alternative fits 46 %
HP_DECAY.provenance: MEASURED on the live 16.402 corpus. A building with a LifeTime does not keep its hitpoints and die at the end -- its hp falls every tick from its deploy-end tick and it dies when the pool runs out. The law that fits: a per-tick rate derived ONCE from the building's max hitpoints and its LifeTime, truncated to hundredths of a hitpoint, `drain = ((maxHitpoints * 100000) / LifeTime_ms) / 20` (nested floor division makes the two truncating divisions the same integer as one: max_hp x TICK_MS / LifeTime_ms in hundredths), then accumulated tick by tick with every whole hitpoint the accumulator crosses taken off the hp field; hp <= 0 is clamped to 0 and the building dies through the normal death path, so a drained Tombstone death-spawns exactly as a killed one does. With it, hp = maxHitpoints - (k * drain) / 100 for k ticks since the deploy-end tick reproduces 92.2 % of 31113 building frames over 79 buildings exactly (BombTower 1356 hp / drain 226: 100 % of 2132 frames; GoblinCage 780 / 195: 98.5 %; Tesla 1182 / 236: 95.9 %; Tombstone 91.7 %; InfernoTower 1748 / 291: 91.3 %; Cannon 824 / 137: 84.6 %), and every residual is a building that was hit -- of the 79, 54 are exact on every frame of their life. It also predicts the death tick: 501 for a Tesla (LifeTime 25000 = 500 ticks, the drain is one tick slower than the column), 600 for a BombTower, 602 for a Cannon or a level-11 Tombstone, 400 for a GoblinCage -- all confirmed on the last frame the recording shows. The drain starts at the DEPLOY-END tick, not at landing (a Tesla's hp is at max on every frame of its deploy window). The EXACT-FRACTION alternative (maxHitpoints x k / LifeTime_ticks, recomputed every tick) matches only 46 % of the frames and drifts one hitpoint high; truncating the rate first and accumulating it is what makes the law fit. expiry_hit, what the engine did before, keeps hp at max for the whole life and matches no frame past the deploy end of any building in the corpus.
HP_DECAY.meaning: linear_drain (shipped): every tick past the deploy end the building's hundredths accumulator gains ((max_hp * 100000) / LifeTime_ms) / 20 and each whole hitpoint it crosses is dealt as a hit that ignores the hide state, so damage and the drain share one hp pool and a death by drain goes through the normal death path. expiry_hit (the earlier engine, kept runnable): hp is untouched and a hit for everything the building has left lands when LifeTime is up.
HP_DECAY.promotion_rules: Settled for every building the corpus shows. Open: whether the drain rate is recomputed when a buff changes max hp, and which pool the drain takes from on a shielded building (no shipped LifeTime card carries a shield, so neither is testable on the data).
HP_DECAY.engine: state.rs Calib::lifetime_hp_decay, read by BattleState::phase_status (`lifetime_drain_per_tick`, the accumulator BattleState::lifetime_acc); tests/lifetime.rs

TROOP_LIFETIME.confidence: MEDIUM: the drain is measured in 3 of 3 runs; its end (the expiry at 400 ticks) was never reached.
TROOP_LIFETIME.provenance: Measured on client 15.535.29 on the Goblin Demolisher's kamikaze form (GoblinDemolisher_kamikaze_form, a troop row with LifeTime 20000), in the Goblin Demolisher scenarios at level 11: from its switch it lost 3, 3, 3, 4 hp a tick with nothing hitting it, in 3 of 3 runs. That is lifetime.HP_DECAY's building law on its max hp: 1300 x 100000 / 20000 / 20 = 325 hundredths a tick. Under expiry_at_lifetime its hp would have stood still.
TROOP_LIFETIME.meaning: same_as_buildings: a troop's LifeTime runs lifetime.HP_DECAY's law, as a building's does. expiry_at_lifetime: the troop keeps its hp for the whole LifeTime, then takes one hit for everything it has. Only a troop row that a transformation reaches carries a LifeTime: card.rs refuses a troop with one reached any other way, so every battle without a transformation is the same under both values.
TROOP_LIFETIME.open: The end of the life: 20000 ms is 400 ticks, and no scenario kept a kamikaze form alive that long.
TROOP_LIFETIME.promotion_rules: A kamikaze form that nothing kills for 400 ticks.
TROOP_LIFETIME.engine: state.rs lifetime_of (a troop's LifeTime) and phase_status (its decay law); card.rs, the unit loop (a troop with a LifeTime reached other than by a transformation is refused); tests/transform.rs, tests/lifetime.rs

HEALTH_TRIGGER_TIMING.provenance: Measured on client 15.535.29 (the Cannon Cart and Goblin Demolisher scenarios, level 11). With C the frame a hit takes the unit to half or below: a princess tower's shot took a Cannon Cart from 969 to 860 on C, and it drained first on C + 2 (860, 860, 857, then 3 a tick); a Knight created before it took a Cannon Cart from 1001 to 799 with a melee strike on C, and it drained first on C + 1. Every case fits a threshold read at the unit's own update, which in the engine is its turn in the Target phase: the tick after a projectile's damage (a shot lands at the end of a tick), and the same tick after a melee strike by a unit earlier in the order under the sequential order.
